# 00 — START HERE: Map, Reading Order, Audience Guide, Quick Start

Welcome. This is the complete handover documentation for **TRINETRA** (alternative name **HIMKAVACH**), an
offline-first, physics-grounded, **advisory** early-warning and hazard-detection research program and its
reference code implementation. This chapter tells you what this project is, what it is *not*, where every
answer lives, and how to get running in ten minutes.

---

## 0.1 The one thing to understand before anything else

This project has **two layers**, and confusing them is the single most common mistake:

1. **A research-only program.** Its own `FINAL_REPORT.md` says verbatim: *"Nothing was built, trained, or
   measured."* Every performance number anywhere in the research artifacts is **source-reported** from other
   people's papers on their own data. The program's job was to decide *what to build and why*, grounded in
   631 arXiv references (the FINAL_REPORT snapshot figure; the live ledger has since grown to ~775 — see
   `_CANON §7` and chapter 19).
2. **A reference code implementation** (`trinetra/`) written later: a pure-**numpy core** that runs and
   **passes 128 unit tests + 6 CI gates**, a **PyTorch `deep/`** layer (6 trainable models) that is
   **compile-verified but never GPU-trained here**, and **Kaggle training scripts** that are **multi-GPU
   ready but not executed on a GPU** in this environment.

> **No TRINETRA model has been trained and no dataset has been downloaded.** Any accuracy, latency, recall,
> false-alarm, or cost number you see attributed to a *paper* is that paper's result, not ours. Where you
> might expect a TRINETRA result, the honest answer is **"not measured."** This is not a gap in the
> documentation — it is the actual, deliberate state of the project (life-safety domain, honesty-first).

If you remember only this section, you will not misread the rest.

## 0.4 Quick start (10 minutes, no GPU, no datasets)

The numpy core runs with only Python + numpy. [CONFIRMED — this is exactly what was run to validate it.]

```powershell
# from the repository root that contains the trinetra/ folder
cd trinetra
$env:PYTHONIOENCODING = "utf-8"              # Windows: make unittest output UTF-8 clean
python run_tests.py                          # expect: "Ran 128 tests ... OK"
python scripts/ci_gates.py                   # expect: "ALL 6 CI GATES PASSED"
python demo.py                               # end-to-end advisory decision on synthetic evidence
```

Expected: 128 tests pass, 6 gates pass. (`run_tests.py` may print a spurious `[exit code: 1]` because
unittest writes its summary to stderr; the real pass signal is the final line `OK`.) The PyTorch models in
`trinetra/src/trinetra/deep/` and the Kaggle scripts in `trinetra/kaggle/` require a GPU environment and are
documented in chapters 05, 10 and 11 — they are **not** needed for the quick start.

## 0.5 How to trust this documentation (the honesty contract)

Every non-trivial claim is tagged: `[CONFIRMED]`, `[LIKELY]`, `[HYPOTHESIS]`, or `[INFEASIBLE]` (defined in
`_CANON.md §1`). "Our measurement" and "Paper X reports" are always kept visibly separate. Numbers that were
never measured say "not measured". References carry a real arXiv ID / DOI and a verification status.
Failures and reversed decisions are reported plainly (see chapters 13 and 24), including the headline
negative result that **IP-address-based alerting is infeasible** for life-safety targeting (chapter 08).

If you find a claim without a label, a number without a source, or a contradiction between two chapters,
that is a bug in the documentation — log it against the consistency gate in `PROGRESS_DOC.md`.

---

## 0.6 Scope in one breath
Rapid-onset mountain hazards (landslide, flash-flood, cloudburst, GLOF) in Uttarakhand + Himachal, plus
fire/disaster detection via CCTV + IoT + free satellite data, fused into a **calibrated, shielded, advisory**
alert level for a **human** operator who alone decides on public dissemination. Offline-first; ≤₹2000 IoT
node; ≤30 Kaggle GPU-h/week; never an autonomous public alert. Full scope and non-goals: chapter 03.

# 01 — Executive Summary

**Audience:** anyone who needs the whole project in two pages — PM, judge, reviewer, new lead.
**Status date:** 2026-10-10. **Honesty posture:** research + reference code; nothing trained or benchmarked.

---

## 1.1 What TRINETRA is

TRINETRA (alt. **HIMKAVACH**) is an **offline-first, multi-sensor, physics-grounded, advisory early-warning
and hazard-detection system** for two problem families:

1. **Rapid-onset mountain hazards** — landslide, flash-flood, cloudburst, and glacial-lake outburst flood
   (GLOF) in the Indian Himalaya (Uttarakhand + Himachal Pradesh).
2. **Fire / disaster detection** via existing CCTV, cheap ground IoT, and free satellite Earth-observation.

It ingests free satellite data, opportunistic camera vision, and ≤₹2000 LoRa IoT nodes; runs an anomaly
stack, a physics gate, a supervised ensemble, and an offline-RL advisory policy; **fuses** them in a gated
meta-fusion head; **calibrates** the fused risk with conformal prediction; applies a deterministic monotone
**safety shield**; and emits a single **advisory alert level** (Green < Yellow < Orange < Red) to a **human
operator**, who alone decides whether to disseminate a CAP/SACHET public alert. The trust boundary from
"advisory level" to "public alert" is **never crossed without a human** (safety rule R19).

## 1.2 What was actually produced (two layers)

- **Research program** [CONFIRMED by `FINAL_REPORT.md`]: a complete, literature-grounded design across all
  workstreams, 631 unique arXiv references (FINAL_REPORT snapshot; ~775 in the live ledger — see `_CANON §7`), 128 per-paper notes, physics derivations, a dataset registry,
  a Kaggle compute plan, a failure-mode catalogue, and a 33-item hazard-correctness bug ledger with fixes.
  **Nothing was trained or measured.**
- **Reference code** [CONFIRMED by running it]: `trinetra/` — a pure-numpy core (physics gates, fusion,
  conformal calibration, decision/shield, eval harness) that **passes 128 unit tests and 6 CI gates**; a
  PyTorch `deep/` layer with 6 trainable models + fusion heads (**compile-verified, not GPU-trained here**);
  and Kaggle training scripts (**multi-GPU T4×2 ready, not executed on a GPU here**).

## 1.3 Results posture — read this before quoting any number

There are **no TRINETRA performance results**, by design. The only numbers we measured are *engineering*
facts about the code:

| Our measurement | Value | How |
|-----------------|-------|-----|
| numpy-core unit tests | **128 pass** [CONFIRMED] | `python run_tests.py` → `OK` |
| CI honesty/safety gates | **6/6 pass** [CONFIRMED] | `python scripts/ci_gates.py` |
| deep + Kaggle scripts | **compile-clean** [CONFIRMED] | `py_compile`; not run on GPU |
| source size | ~3362 LOC src, ~917 LOC tests | `CODE_INVENTORY.md` |

Every *domain* number (detection mAP, false-alarm reduction, calibration coverage, drift-MSE reduction,
edge latency, BOM ₹) that appears anywhere in this project is **source-reported** from a cited paper on its
own data (safety rule R16), or is a **planning estimate** flagged `[EST]`. The chapter-12 "SOTA target"
table lists these as *process targets* ("match/approach under our protocol"), never as achieved results.

## 1.4 The headline verdicts (do not soften)

- **IP-address-based alerting is `[INFEASIBLE]`** for life-safety targeting. Consumer IP geolocation is only
  ISP/city-accurate (often tens of km), is corrupted by CGNAT/VPN/DHCP, maps to no premises, and cannot
  address a person at risk. It was **considered and rejected**. Public-IP exposure is handled instead as a
  *security* concern (authenticated endpoints). (Chapter 08.)
- **A full fire-PINN as a deployed on-device solver is `[INFEASIBLE]` now** (stiffness, spectral bias,
  non-identifiability). Physics enters as *soft features / priors / consistency-checks* with a Class-A
  fallback — not as a live solver. (Chapters 05–06.)
- **Autonomous public alerting without certification/authority is `[INFEASIBLE]`.** The system is advisory,
  human-in-the-loop, and fails safe to "uncertain/offline" (R19).
- **Random cross-validation overstates skill** → **spatial-block CV is mandatory** and gates every claim
  (admission gate G2; arXiv 2608.12422 — naive ~0.90 ROC-AUC collapses under matched spatial-CV). (Chapter 12.)
- Deepfake / zero-shot / social-media signals are **low-trust advisory only** and must be corroborated.

## 1.5 What is genuinely strong about the design

- **Honesty engineered into the code, not just the prose:** a `ReportGuard` refuses to emit a headline
  metric unless a spatial-CV "real win" over mandatory baselines (climatology, logistic/GBDT, persistence)
  clears a bootstrap confidence interval (R16). The 6 CI gates fail the build on common dishonesty/safety
  violations.
- **A single, auditable decision function:** `level = max(conformal_level(fused_risk, p*), shield_floor)`
  with **p\* = C_FA/(C_FA+C_miss) ≈ 0.0476** (C_FA=5, C_miss=100). One function; every legacy threshold maps
  to an internal role; no alert path bypasses it.
- **Calibration that survives shift:** split-conformal is replaced/augmented by weighted CP (WCPS),
  Adaptive Conformal Inference (ACI), Mondrian per-hazard CP, and Conformal Risk Control for the decision
  level-sets — because calibrated members ≠ calibrated ensemble and coverage collapses under drift.
- **Graceful degradation is a first-class requirement:** missing modalities, dead nodes, solar brownout,
  and cloud outages are treated as *expected*, with reliability-gated fusion and an offline alert path.
- **Hazard-physics correctness bugs were found and fixed** (e.g. the Iverson transient term must use
  `D1 = D0/cos²β` only, with no spurious `cos β` multiplier) and locked behind golden-case tests.

## 1.6 What is NOT done / biggest risks (full list: chapter 22)

- No training, no datasets downloaded, no measured skill, no on-device latency/RAM/current numbers, no final
  live-verified BOM, no verified India regulatory/LoRa-band path. The disaster-evacuation RL environment is
  a **build gap** (no off-the-shelf env). Dataset licenses are **unverified**; all datasets are candidates.
- References are mostly **subagent-reported identifiers, not independently re-fetched** (a web_search
  outage during the research program) — a disclosed residual risk the reference-verification pass addresses.
- Geo events are few (n≈5-ish), so any eventual skill estimate will be **variance-dominated**.

## 1.7 Recommended next steps (from `FINAL_REPORT.md §14-15`)

Build order: (1) evaluation tooling + the "real-win" gate and a leakage-controlled benchmark; (2) edge CCTV
detector + physics feature; (3) temporal event validation; (4) calibrated fusion + conformal-under-shift +
drift monitor; (5) IoT node + drift correction + prototype; (6) robustness red-team; (7) anomaly + advisory
RL (after building the evac env); (8) an India "shadow → advisory" pilot. Each step is gated by its
pre-registered cross-camera/cross-site decision rule. Before procurement: live-verify the BOM; before any
claim: pass the spatial-CV admission gate; before any public alert: certification + authority + a human.

# 02 — System Architecture

**Audience:** engineers and reviewers who need the end-to-end design, data flow, compute tiers, and the
interfaces between components. Ground truth: `DESIGN/HLD.md`, `DESIGN/LLD.md`, `DESIGN/COMPONENT_DESIGN.md`,
and the implemented packages in `trinetra/src/trinetra/`. Nothing here claims measured performance.

---

## 2.1 System context

```
          ┌──────────────────────────── EXTERNAL ACTORS ────────────────────────────┐
 ESA/NASA free EO ─►│                                                                │
 existing CCTV ────►│                     TRINETRA SYSTEM                            │─► Human operator
 ground IoT nodes ─►│   sense → detect → physics-gate → fuse → calibrate → shield    │   (DECIDES)
 inbound media ────►│                                                                │─► CAP/SACHET feed
          └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘        │
                                                                                                ▼
                                                                                 sirens / SMS / WhatsApp
```

The trust boundary is explicit: the system produces an **advisory level**; it **never** originates a public
alert on its own. Deepfake and zero-shot outputs are low-trust advisory signals only. (Safety rule R19.)

## 2.2 Logical pipeline (the spine)

Three sensing layers → encoders → anomaly stack → physics gate → supervised ensemble → offline-RL policy →
meta-fusion head → conformal calibration → hard safety shield → advisory level → operator → CAP/SACHET.

```
 L1 SENSE            L2 PROCESS                                           L3 DECIDE          L4 ACT
 ─────────           ─────────────────────────────────────────────       ──────────────     ──────────────
 EO/satellite ─┐     encoders (frozen EO-FM, CCTV detector, IoT feat.)    conformal          operator UI
 CCTV/vision ──┼───► anomaly (resid + Deep-SVDD + iForest + XGBoost) ─┐   calibrate (per      (human gate)
 ground IoT ───┘     physics gate (geo: FS/Iverson/Fukuzono/Caine;    │   zone, WCPS/ACI) ─►  │
 inbound media ───►  fire: Heskestad/Byram/Strouhal; fire-PINN=soft)  ├─► META-FUSION ──►     shield (monotone
                     supervised ensemble (XGBoost EWS + per-hazard)   │   (GMF+PHARAOH+FM)    floor, can only
                     offline-RL advisory policy (shielded) ───────────┘                       RAISE) ─► LEVEL
 authenticity (deepfake scorer) ───────────────────────────────── low-trust advisory ──────► into fusion/UI
 monitor (drift/calibration CUSUM) ────────────────────────────── advisory recalibration flag
```

## 2.3 The single decision function (the architectural contract)

```
level(state s) = max( conformal_level( fused_risk(s), p* ) ,  shield_floor(s) )
```

- `conformal_level` maps the calibrated fused risk to {Green < Yellow < Orange < Red}; the escalation point
  is the cost-loss alarm threshold **p\* = C_FA/(C_FA+C_miss) ≈ 0.0476** (C_FA=5, C_miss=100), optionally
  replaced by Conformal-Risk-Control-calibrated cut points.
- `shield_floor(s)` is a **deterministic, monotone** floor (e.g. FS<1 forces a minimum level). It can only
  **RAISE** the level, never lower it, and runs **after** the learner (post-posed shielding, no training).
- There is **exactly one** decision function. Every legacy threshold maps to an internal role; no alert path
  bypasses it. Implemented in `ws5_fusion_rl/decision.py` (`decide`, `conformal_level`).

## 2.4 Meta-fusion head (GMF + PHARAOH), high level

Experts: `e_phys` (physics/Bayes → p_phys + base action a₀), `e_RL` (offline-RL q-values), `e_sup`
(supervised/anomaly ensemble → p_sup). The head embeds raw evidence ⊕ RL output ⊕ expert probabilities ⊕
reliability/quality masks and emits a **bounded residual** over the base action a₀: `â = clip(a₀ + residual)`
(residual-policy learning; the residual is hard-clipped so a mis-trained head cannot dominate the
physics-anchored base). **PHARAOH** is an adaptive-order weighted power-mean pooling primitive (Class C,
flag-gated OFF) whose order bends toward "max" only under a credible, physics-consistent alarm
(anti-complacency) and fails open to "uncertain". **FM-1..FM-6** are derived fusion options
(precision-weighted — the Class-A default; evidential; conformal-stacked; covariance-intersection;
physics-gated MoE; RL-tuned). All Class-B/C fusion pieces are advisory, unvalidated, flag-gated, with the
Class-A linear fallback (FM-1). Correlation-aware **BLUE/GLS** weighting and a **two-layer hierarchical**
fusion decorrelate redundant sources. Details and the honesty critique: chapter 06.

## 2.5 Deployment topology — three compute tiers (hard design rule C8)

```
┌── TIER 0: NODE (ESP32-C3 / ESP32-CAM, ≤₹2000, solar + LiFePO4) ───────────────────────────────┐
│  tiny statistical screen ONLY: Z-score/RMS tilt, stage threshold, on-node FS, 1/v fit,         │
│  drift pre-correction (F-15), TinyML pre-filter. Deep sleep + duty cycle. RAW VIDEO STAYS LOCAL.│
└───────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                │ LoRa IN865–867 MHz (SX1262), store-carry-forward (DTN) when the link is down
┌───────────────▼── TIER 1: GATEWAY (LoRa concentrator + edge GPU/SoC + sat-IoT uplink) ─────────┐
│  CCTV detector (F-11) + temporal event validation (F-12) + IR flicker (F-16); VAD; InSAR        │
│  anomaly if cached; physics gate; LOCAL fusion + shield; CAP build + siren drive. CLOUD-OFFLINE. │
└───────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                │ intermittent internet / sat-IoT
┌───────────────▼── TIER 2: CLOUD / KAGGLE (≤30 GPU-h/week) ─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  frozen EO-FM embedding, SSL/anomaly training, offline-RL training, meta-head training,         │
│  hindcast/eval harness, model registry. NEVER on the life-safety critical path (constraint C1). │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Model→tier assignment is a hard rule: heavy models (EO-FM, VAD, deep anomaly) are **Tier-1/2 only**; Tier-0
runs only what fits MCU SRAM/flash/energy. The **offline alert path (node → LoRa/DTN → gateway → siren) is
independent of the cloud** (C1).

## 2.6 Key data flows

1. **Geo early-warning (slow):** EO datacube + IoT + precip → encoder/anomaly → physics gate → ensemble →
   RL → meta-fusion → conformal → shield → advisory level → operator. Cadence: per satellite pass + IoT
   heartbeat.
2. **Fire / CCTV (fast):** frame → detector (F-11) → temporal event validation (F-12) (+ IR flicker F-16,
   fire-physics soft features) → fusion → shield → advisory level. Cadence: near-real-time at the gateway.
3. **Offline alert (always available):** node event → LoRa/DTN → gateway shield decision → local siren/SMS,
   independent of the cloud.
4. **Calibration/bias loop:** LoRa rain gauges bias-correct satellite IMERG precip; F-15 corrects IoT
   sensor drift; F-14 raises advisory recalibration flags.
5. **Authenticity (advisory):** inbound media → deepfake scorer → low-trust flag into fusion / operator UI.

## 2.7 Interfaces and message contracts

The implemented contracts live in `trinetra/src/trinetra/common/types.py`. Core objects:

- **`ExpertOutput`** — one fused expert's contribution: `p` (probability), `u` (uncertainty), `c`
  (conflict), `r` (reliability), `cls` (`PhysicsClass` A/B/C/DATA/ADVISORY), `available` (bool). Every
  encoder/anomaly/physics/RL stage produces one of these; the fusion head consumes a list of them.
- **`Evidence`** — raw per-source signals + quality/availability masks entering the pipeline.
- **`ConformalResult`** — calibrated risk + coverage metadata (marginal, per-zone), honestly labelled.
- **`ShieldResult`** — the deterministic floor level + the human-readable reason it fired.
- **`Decision`** — the final advisory `Level` (Green/Yellow/Orange/Red) + contributing evidence + shield
  reason + trace id (R19 explainability: every advisory traces to its evidence and the shield reason).
- **Alerting:** the CAP/SACHET builder (`ws3_alert/cap.py`) refuses to emit without an `APPROVED:` operator
  token; DTN (`ws3_alert/dtn.py`) does store-carry-forward; endpoints are allow-listed (constraint C6);
  no raw video leaves the node (C7).

Message formats between tiers: LoRa payloads are compact codewords (`ws7_iot/lora_codec.py`, IN865–867
band); the gateway reconstructs `Evidence`; alerts are CAP XML, signed, deduplicated.

## 2.8 Cross-cutting concerns

- **Calibration & uncertainty (WS6):** every probabilistic output is conformally calibrated per zone;
  coverage is reported honestly (marginal, shift-sensitive), never as a "guarantee"; evidential/zero-shot
  signals are for ranking/OOD only, never as absolute probabilities.
- **Robustness (WS6):** per-corruption eval; adversarial-patch red-team on the detector; missing-modality
  adapter + reliability gating so a dropped layer degrades gracefully (constraint C8 / graceful degradation).
- **Security (WS6):** endpoint allow-list enforced in CI (C6); signed CAP alerts; dedup; key rotation; the
  historical key-exfiltrating proxy bug is removed (chapter 13).
- **Privacy (C7):** raw video stays local; federated/edge scoring; only events/scores leave the node.
- **Provenance & reproducibility (F-17):** pinned seeds, logged spatial-CV folds, experiment tracking, and
  the LMEM+GLRT "real-win" gate on every improvement.
- **Energy:** camera + comms dominate; a per-task energy budget is a requirement; winter/monsoon solar gaps
  mean node outage and missing inputs are treated as **expected**, not exceptional.

## 2.9 Non-functional requirements (summary; full list chapter 03)
Offline-first alert path (C1); graceful degradation; edge latency within the alert deadline at the gateway;
≤₹2000/node (C2); ≤30 GPU-h/week (C3); auditability of every advisory (R19); **no performance surface in
UI/API until the admission gate G2 passes**; Class-C blocks flagged in output metadata.

## 2.10 Quality gates (architecture-level; see chapter 12 for G2 detail)
G1 physics golden tests · **G2 spatial-CV admission gate (blocks ANY performance claim)** · G3 single
decision fn + realizable monotone shield + measured coverage · G4 fusion stability + reliability gating ·
G5 ≤₹2000 BOM + tiered feasibility + fault discrimination + LoRa band · G6 no credential egress + offline
alert path + anti-leak timestamp audit · G7 datacube size + dataset licenses + novelty honesty + Kaggle fit.

<!-- ====================== BEGIN 03_requirements_and_scope.md ====================== -->

# 03 — Requirements and Scope

**Audience:** anyone deciding what the project must do, must not do, and under what fixed constraints.
Ground truth: `DESIGN/HLD.md §7`, `DESIGN/SYSTEM_DESIGN_PROMPT.md`, `ASSUMPTIONS.md`, `FINAL_REPORT.md`,
`TRINETRA_Workstreams.md`. All constraints below are **binding** on every chapter and every design choice.

---

## 3.1 Goals (what the system must achieve)

G-1. Detect and give early warning of rapid-onset mountain hazards — landslide, flash-flood, cloudburst,
GLOF — in Uttarakhand + Himachal Pradesh, from free satellite EO + cheap ground IoT + opportunistic vision.

G-2. Detect fire/smoke/disaster from existing CCTV at the network edge, with temporal event validation to
suppress false alarms.

G-3. Produce a **single, calibrated, shielded, advisory alert level** (Green/Yellow/Orange/Red) with honest
uncertainty, auditable back to its contributing evidence and the shield reason.

G-4. Operate **offline-first**: the alert path (node → LoRa/DTN → gateway → siren) must work with the cloud
unreachable.

G-5. Degrade gracefully when modalities, nodes, solar power, or connectivity are lost — treat these as
expected, not exceptional.

G-6. Keep a human in the loop for every public-facing action; provide decision support, never autonomous
dissemination.

> **Local-siren carve-out (reconciled with chapter 08 §08.3):** the one actuation Tier-1 may trigger without
> a human is the **local on-site siren/strobe** (`siren.py`, source ∈ {node_edge, shield, operator}). This is
> treated as a *local physical alarm* for people in immediate earshot — **not** an "official public alert"
> (no CAP message, no broadcast, no naming of a hazard to the public). Official dissemination (CAP/SACHET/
> cell-broadcast) always requires a human + authority. So G-6 holds for *dissemination*; the local siren is
> the deliberate, scoped exception.

G-7. Be reproducible and falsifiable: pinned seeds, logged spatial-CV folds, mandatory baselines, and a
pre-registered "real-win" gate on every claimed improvement.

## 3.2 Non-goals (explicitly out of scope)

N-1. **Autonomous public alerting.** The system never originates an official alert without a human and the
proper authority/certification. `[INFEASIBLE]` / disallowed. (R19.)

N-2. **IP-address-based location or targeting of people/alerts.** Ruled `[INFEASIBLE]` (chapter 08): consumer
IP geolocation is ISP/city-granular, CGNAT/VPN/DHCP-corrupted, maps to no premises. Not carried.

N-3. **A deployed on-device fire-PINN solver.** `[INFEASIBLE]` now (stiffness/spectral-bias/
non-identifiability). Physics is used only as soft features/priors/consistency-checks with a Class-A
fallback, and as offline simulators (Class C, documentation-only).

N-4. **Any measured performance claim in this phase.** Nothing is trained or benchmarked; the project
produces designs, derivations, and honesty-gated reference code. (R16.)

N-5. **Paid data or paid cloud dependencies.** Only free datasets may ever be `STATUS=selected`; build
compute is Kaggle-only. (Constraints below.)

N-6. **Surveillance / biometric identification of private individuals, or raw-video egress.** Privacy
constraint C7; raw video stays on the node.

N-7. **Legal/regulatory determinations.** All India standards / certification / radio-band / alerting-
authority facts are `[UNVERIFIED]` search leads for qualified professional review. Nothing here is legal
advice.

## 3.3 Hard constraints (binding, from the master program)

| ID | Constraint | Consequence in design |
|----|-----------|-----------------------|
| **C1** | Offline-first alert path | node→LoRa/DTN→gateway→siren works cloud-offline; cloud never on the critical path |
| **C2** | ≤ ₹2000 per IoT node (incl. GST + shipping, ~10% contingency) | tiered BOM; all ₹ are `[EST]` until live-verified |
| **C3** | Build compute = Kaggle only, ~25–30 GPU-h/week, ≥15% reserve | PEFT/frozen-backbone first; CPU for all non-training work |
| **C4** | Free data only may be selected | datasets are candidates `[D]`; licenses unverified |
| **C5** | Life-safety → advisory, human-in-loop, fail-safe (R19) | no autonomous alert; fail to "uncertain/offline" |
| **C6** | Endpoint allow-list (no credential egress) | enforced in CI; signed CAP; key rotation |
| **C7** | No raw-video egress / privacy | edge-scored; only events/scores leave the node |
| **C8** | Heavy models Tier-1/2 only | Tier-0 runs only MCU-feasible statistics |
| **C9** | India LoRa band = IN865–867 MHz | SX1262 radio; 433 MHz SX1278 is non-compliant (bug #6) |
| **C10** | Honesty rules R16/R19/R20/R21 | no claim pre-gate; class labels; novelty = search claim |

## 3.4 Working assumptions (from `ASSUMPTIONS.md`; each has a verify-by phase)

| ID | Assumption | Risk if wrong | Verify |
|----|------------|---------------|--------|
| A-05 | BOM ₹ figures are `[EST]`; ≤₹2000 gate not yet enforced | infeasible BOM slips through | at build (live listings) |
| A-06 | LoRa band = IN865–867 MHz for India | illegal/non-functional radio | at build |
| A-07 | Only FREE datasets may be selected | paid dependency | dataset phase |
| A-08 | Kaggle only, ~25–30 GPU-h/wk, ≥15% reserve | plan exceeds compute | compute phase |
| A-10 | Sandbox date is 2026 (arXiv IDs up to 26xx valid) | mis-dated citations | ongoing |

Assumptions are **not facts** and never enter a report as facts.

## 3.5 Functional requirements by workstream (abridged; detail in chapters 06–13)

- **WS1 physics + fusion:** correct infinite-slope FS (saturated-limit guard), Iverson transient head
  (`D1=D0/cos²β` only), Fukuzono 1/v (α=2), Caine I–D; fire physics (Heskestad/Byram/Strouhal); a single
  gated meta-fusion head with a bounded residual and a Class-A fallback; golden-case unit tests (gate G1).
- **WS2 deepfake:** defensive-only authenticity scoring of inbound social-media media; low-trust, advisory,
  corroborated; continuous red-teaming (defenses and evasions co-evolve).
- **WS3 alerting:** offline-first store-carry-forward (DTN); signed CAP/SACHET; siren path; **no IP-based
  targeting** (N-2); no origination without authority.
- **WS4 CCTV:** compact edge detector (F-11) + temporal event validation (F-12) + IR flicker feature (F-16);
  cross-camera evaluation.
- **WS5 RL:** offline-RL **advisory** alarm policy that must **beat strong non-RL baselines** (e.g. MILP),
  selected by OPE with a lower-bound-≥-baseline rule, post-posed hard shield; never actuation.
- **WS6 robustness/eval:** spatial-block (not random) CV; mandatory baselines; conformal-under-shift;
  drift/calibration monitoring; cross-sensor corroboration as the most transferable defense; the 33-item
  hazard-correctness bug ledger closed with golden tests.
- **WS7 IoT:** ≤₹2000 tiered LoRa node; on-node drift correction + scheduled recalibration; fault-vs-event
  discrimination so a single faulty node cannot drive a RED alert unaided.
- **WS8 anomaly:** forecast-residual + Deep-SVDD (collapse-prevented) anomaly heads under a strict protocol
  (must beat persistence/general baselines; leakage-controlled; advisory input to fusion, never standalone).

## 3.6 Acceptance gates (a requirement is "met" only when its gate passes)

| Gate | Requirement it certifies | Blocks |
|------|--------------------------|--------|
| G1 | physics golden-case tests (geo + fire) | any downstream physics use |
| **G2** | spatial-CV admission (baselines + CI + cost-loss + real-win) | **ANY performance claim / publication** |
| G3 | single decision fn + realizable monotone shield + measured coverage | deployment |
| G4 | fusion stability + reliability gating + shield-floor monotonicity | GMF/PHARAOH deployment |
| G5 | ≤₹2000 live-verified BOM + tiered feasibility + fault discrimination + LoRa band | hardware order |
| G6 | no credential egress + offline alert path + anti-leak timestamp audit | field pilot |
| G7 | datacube size + dataset licenses + novelty honesty + Kaggle fit | submission |

## 3.7 Stakeholders and operating context
Target region: Indian Himalaya (Uttarakhand + Himachal). Primary user: a trained human operator/dispatcher
at a gateway/control room who reviews advisory levels and decides on CAP/SACHET dissemination through the
proper authority. Secondary stakeholders: fire-science / ML / safety / legal / ethics / accessibility
reviewers whose sign-off is a precondition for any Class-B/C physics or any field pilot. Deployment follows
a staged pilot: Stage 0 offline replay → Stage 1 shadow (observe/log, trigger nothing) → Stage 2 advisory
(human decides), with pre-registered metrics and rollback rules (chapter 15).

# 04 — DATASETS (index): every dataset, its status, and how to trust it

This is the **index** to the TRINETRA (HIMKAVACH) dataset registry. The one place where **all 164 dataset
IDs appear** is the master table in §4. The long per-dataset content lives in the companion file
[04a_DATASETS.md](<04a_DATASETS.md>): 16-field **deep entries for the 13 STATUS=selected datasets**, then the
whole **candidate pool** as compact tables grouped by modality.

Ground-truth sources for this chapter (`_CANON.md §9`): [`DATASETS.md`](<../DATASETS.md>) (registry
D01–D112) and [`DATASETS_CATALOGUE.md`](<../DATASETS_CATALOGUE.md>) (candidate pool D113–D164).

---

## 1. Honesty box — read before using any row

> **NONE acquired.** No dataset has been downloaded in this program (links / metadata / plans only).
> This matches `_CANON.md`: *"No model has been trained and no dataset has been downloaded."*
> - **No EDA, no statistics.** Every size / `N` below is **as recorded in the registry**, not measured by
>   us. Many are flagged UNVERIFIED or "named" (taken from a citing abstract, not the owning paper's page).
> - **Licenses are as-recorded and mostly UNVERIFIED.** "the source records X" is **not** a verified fact.
>   We reproduce the registry's own tags honestly; we did not re-adjudicate them.
> - **Everything is a candidate until the license is verified** at the owning portal. Only 13 datasets are
>   marked `STATUS=selected`, and even those carry open license/count confirmations (several are `[V*]`/`[D]`).
> - Honesty labels (`_CANON.md §1`): `[CONFIRMED]` only for existence we verified; the registry's dataset
>   facts here are at best `[LIKELY]`/`[UNVERIFIED]` pending a portal fetch. No dataset performance number
>   is a TRINETRA measurement.

---

## 2. How to read the registry — STATUS and the verification legend

**STATUS values** (set by the free-only policy, `_CANON.md §5` constraint **C4**):
- **selected** — free (or free-with-registration), existence-verified, and chosen for the build. 13 total.
  Free-only rule: a dataset may be `selected` **only** if it is free; UNCLEAR-cost sets stay candidate.
- **candidate** — discovered and plausibly usable, but **not** adopted: license unverified, cost unclear,
  out-of-region, or domain-shifted. 151 total (every D27–D164, plus the unselected D09–D26).
- **rejected-paid** — a paid dataset excluded by the free-only rule. **0 in the registry**: no paid dataset
  was carried far enough to be formally rejected; cost-restricted government feeds (IMD D47, CWC D53) are
  recorded as `candidate` with cost "varies / often restricted", not as `rejected-paid`.

**Verification legend** (reproduced verbatim from `DATASETS.md`):
- **`[V]`** — verified on a direct authoritative fetch this phase (portal / Zenodo / GitHub / arXiv).
- **`[V*]`** — existence verified, but **one** stated fact (a count or the exact license) is UNVERIFIED,
  flagged inline.
- **`[D]`** — discovery-only: the authoritative page was **not** directly fetched; corroborated only by a
  secondary source. Most of the catalogue (D27–D164) is `[D]`.

## 5. Licensing & access

**Indian government EO/hazard portals are JS-driven → MANUAL verification required.** Bhuvan, MOSDAC,
VEDAS, NRSC, IMD, CWC, and GSI (BHUKOSH) portals render as a JS-only "Loading…" shell and **could not be
scraped** here (`web_fetch` reached but got no content; `web_search` had no API key). Their terms-of-use and
the India-specific layers behind them (D24 Bhuvan inventories, D46 GSI, D47 IMD, D52 ICIMOD, D53 CWC) are
**[UNVERIFIED]** and carried to the deployment backlog — these are the priority for an India pilot. D24
Bhuvan/NRSC-ISRO is the single item most likely to need a slow government request → flagged EARLY ACTION.

**Free-only rule (constraint C4, `_CANON.md §5`).** A dataset may be `STATUS=selected` only if it is free
(or free-with-registration). UNCLEAR-cost sets (D11 GLOFNet, D20 GDCLD) stay candidate. **IMD (D47)** and
**CWC/India-WRIS (D53)** are frequently restricted/paid — the central access risk for calibrating Himalayan
rainfall thresholds and discharge ratings; recorded as `candidate / cost varies`, never selected.

**Registration needed early (free):** NASA Earthdata (D03/D04/D06/D07-V1), Copernicus Data Space
(D01/D02), Copernicus CDS + API key (D05), PlanetScope research access (D19).

**EULA / access-restricted (deepfake & CPS):** FaceForensics++ (D68/D159), Celeb-DF (D69), DFDC
(D70/D158), WildDeepfake (D71), DF40 (D72), FakeAVCeleb (D160) need signed research agreements; SWaT/WADI
(D63) and CRAWDAD (D93) are request-based. Face/AV sets carry consent/privacy constraints — method
development only, **no deceptive media created** (see ch 14).

**Out of scope:** **D140 MMLSv2 is MARTIAN** — listed only for registry completeness; excluded from the
Earth early-warning scope. "Upon acceptance" / host-TBA sets (D115 GWFP, D128 EFFIS, D145 Bihar, D156
TSEqD) may not be live — recheck before use.

## 6. Leakage & split policy

Random/scene cross-validation **overstates** skill in geospatial hazard tasks; spatial-block CV is
mandatory. This verdict is triangulated across three re-fetched papers (`_CANON.md §6`): arXiv **2608.12422**
(Himalayan GLOF/landslide — naïve ROC-AUC ~0.90 collapses to 0.54–0.76 under matched spatial-CV),
**2608.22293** (Palisades urban-wildfire — 0.92→0.75 under 1 km blocks), and **2610.08227** (effective
sample size N_eff = Θ(n²/r²) justifying block holdout). **Full protocol: chapter 12.**

Per-dataset split guidance (from the registry's dataset→model matrix):
- **SAR/EO cubes (D01, D21):** tile + time block CV with buffer ≥ InSAR range (DC-01).
- **Flood (D17 GEOID, D12 Sen1Floods11, D19, D26):** adopt event-level splits; **re-split Sen1Floods11 by
  event** (its native scene-level split is leaky).
- **Landslide (D18 LMHLD, D09, D20):** region-block CV + val→held-out shift test.
- **Covariates (D03/D05/D04):** temporal block CV, monsoon-season held-out.
- **GLOF (D07, D15, D11):** leave-one-basin-out.
- **Indian events (D22, D25, D08):** temporal + leave-one-region-out.
- **Crisis media (D16):** leave-one-event-out; never autonomous (Rule 19).

**Small-n GLOF caveat:** GLOF/landslide positives are thin in-region (D15 ~766 events UNVERIFIED,
leave-one-basin-out), so transfer stress (train global D12/D13/D26/D20 → test Himalayan subset) is
unavoidable and is registered as a **domain-shift risk** (ch 12/22). Mandatory baselines before any
foundation model: persistence (C-03) + GBDT (C-02) + a tuned U-Net.

## Honesty posture (carried from 04 — do not soften)
- **NONE downloaded.** Every acquisition status below is `[UNVERIFIED — not downloaded]`.
- **No EDA / no statistics computed.** Any `N` / size is *as recorded in the registry*, not measured by us;
  several are explicitly flagged UNVERIFIED or "named" (from a citing abstract, not the owning paper).
- **Licenses are as-recorded and mostly UNVERIFIED.** "source records X" ≠ fact. Tags `[V]/[V*]/[D]` and
  `STATUS` are reproduced from the registry, not re-adjudicated here.
- Free-only rule **C4**: no paid dataset is STATUS=selected; UNCLEAR-cost sets stay candidate.

# Part 1 — SELECTED datasets (16-field deep entries)

The 13 datasets the program marked **STATUS=selected** in `DATASETS.md` — the free, existence-verified
"shopping list" that matters for handover. All others are candidates (Part 2). Field order:
*ID/name · modality · hazard/task + WS/chapter · provider · access URL · license[as-recorded] · size · N ·
spatial coverage · temporal coverage · resolution · label type · known biases/caveats · split guidance ·
acquisition status · consuming model/chapter.*

> Reminder: D01–D07 are **continuous sensor missions**, not fixed benchmarks — we index our own
> event-indexed cubes from them, so "N / native split" is n/a and leakage control is ours to impose.

### D01 — Sentinel-1 SAR (Copernicus CDSE) · `[V]` selected
- **Modality:** C-band synthetic-aperture radar (GRD / SLC), all-weather, cloud-penetrating.
- **Hazard/task · WS · chapter:** monsoon flood mapping + landslide/ground deformation; WS1/WS8; ch 06, 12.
- **Provider:** ESA / Copernicus (Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem).
- **Access URL:** https://dataspace.copernicus.eu/ (AWS/GEE mirrors exist).
- **License [as-recorded]:** Copernicus free/open `[V]`.
- **Size:** continuous mission (not a fixed corpus).
- **N:** n/a — we build event cubes.
- **Spatial coverage:** global, incl. India / Himalaya.
- **Temporal coverage:** continuous mission.
- **Resolution:** ~10 m.
- **Label type:** none intrinsic; labels come from hazard inventories (D08/D15/D22).
- **Known biases/caveats:** SLC interferometry is compute-heavy → use GRD + a learned-coherence proxy
  (D21 / arXiv 2606.07374) to stay in the Kaggle budget.
- **Split guidance:** tile + time block CV, buffer ≥ InSAR range (DC-01). [HYPOTHESIS protocol — see ch 12.]
- **Acquisition status:** [UNVERIFIED — not downloaded]; free registration needed for bulk/STAC/openEO.
- **Consuming model/chapter:** masked-InSAR SSL encoder + deformation-forecast head (ch 05/06).
- **F3 — paper/official/mirror:** no owning data-paper recorded → "not found in sources"; official https://dataspace.copernicus.eu/; mirrors AWS `s3://sentinel-s1-l1c`, GEE `COPERNICUS/S1_GRD`.
- **F8 — load [UNTESTED]:** `pystac_client.Client.open("https://catalogue.dataspace.copernicus.eu/stac").search(collections=["SENTINEL-1"], bbox=..., datetime=...)` (CDSE account required).
- **F12 — preprocess/augment order [HYPOTHESIS, planning]:** apply-orbit → border+thermal-noise removal → radiometric cal (σ⁰) → optional speckle filter (keep raw for learned coherence) → RTC geocode → dB + per-tile normalize → tile; augment flips/rot90 only (no photometric jitter on SAR).
- **F15 — source-reported baseline:** not found in sources (continuous mission; no benchmark number recorded).
- **Verification 2026-10-10:** not re-checked this pass.

### D02 — Sentinel-2 MSI (Copernicus CDSE) · `[V]` selected
- **Modality:** 13-band optical multispectral.
- **Hazard/task · WS · chapter:** flood extent / burned-area / land context; WS4/WS8; ch 06, 09, 12.
- **Provider:** ESA / Copernicus (CDSE). **Access URL:** https://dataspace.copernicus.eu/.
- **License [as-recorded]:** Copernicus free/open `[V]` (legal-notice PDF itself not fetchable — minor).
- **Size:** continuous mission. **N:** n/a (we index). **Spatial:** global incl. India/Himalaya.
- **Temporal:** continuous mission. **Resolution:** 10/20/60 m by band.
- **Label type:** none intrinsic.
- **Known biases/caveats:** monsoon **cloud cover** is the dominant limitation → pair with SAR
  (optical–SAR fusion, DC-09).
- **Split guidance:** tile + time block CV, same buffer policy as D01.
- **Acquisition status:** [UNVERIFIED — not downloaded]; free registration for download.
- **Consuming model/chapter:** optical–SAR fusion flood head + EO encoder (ch 05/06).
- **F3 — paper/official/mirror:** no owning data-paper recorded → "not found in sources"; official https://dataspace.copernicus.eu/; mirrors AWS `s3://sentinel-s2-l2a`, GEE `COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED`.
- **F8 — load [UNTESTED]:** `pystac_client.Client.open("https://catalogue.dataspace.copernicus.eu/stac").search(collections=["SENTINEL-2"], bbox=..., datetime=...)` (CDSE account); or `openeo`.
- **F12 — preprocess/augment order [HYPOTHESIS, planning]:** L2A surface-reflectance (Sen2Cor if L1C) → cloud/shadow mask (s2cloudless/SCL) → band-select + resample to 10 m → per-band normalize → tile; augment flips/rot90 + mild spectral jitter.
- **F15 — source-reported baseline:** not found in sources.
- **Verification 2026-10-10:** not re-checked this pass.

### D03 — GPM IMERG precipitation (NASA) · `[V]` selected
- **Modality:** satellite precipitation raster. **Hazard/task · WS · ch:** rainfall trigger / nowcast
  covariate; WS1/WS3; ch 06, 08, 12.
- **Provider:** NASA. **Access URL:** https://gpm.nasa.gov/data/imerg (Earthdata/PPS login; Giovanni/GeoTIFF).
- **License [as-recorded]:** NASA open data `[V]`.

- **F12 — preprocess/augment order [HYPOTHESIS, planning]:** subset region/time → unit handling (mm/hr) → accumulate to event window → regrid to common grid → log1p for skew → temporal-block split (monsoon held-out). *(no image augmentation; covariate raster.)*
- **F15 — source-reported baseline:** not found in sources.

# 05 — MODELS: every model, its formulation, I/O, training recipe, calibration

> **Read `_CANON.md` first.** This chapter agrees with it exactly. Two numbers you must carry into every
> paragraph below:
> 1. **No TRINETRA model has been trained and no dataset has been downloaded.** Every accuracy / skill /
>    latency / cost figure attributed to TRINETRA is **"not measured."** Numbers attributed to a *paper* are
>    that paper's result on that paper's data, kept visibly separate (`_CANON.md §1`).
> 2. The PyTorch `deep/` models are **`py_compile`-clean only** — they were **NOT run on a GPU** in this
>    environment (no torch/CUDA in the authoring sandbox, `_CANON.md §2`). The numpy core (physics + fusion +
>    decision + conformal) **runs**: `python run_tests.py` → **128 tests OK**, `python scripts/ci_gates.py`
>    → **ALL 6 CI GATES PASSED** `[CONFIRMED]`. Any torch code snippet in this chapter is therefore
>    **UNTESTED** (cannot execute torch here).

Honesty labels used throughout: `[CONFIRMED]` / `[LIKELY]` / `[HYPOTHESIS]` / `[INFEASIBLE]` (`_CANON.md §1`).
"Paper X reports …" (source-reported) is always separated from "Our code implements …" (verifiable from the
files read for this chapter). Where a field cannot be filled from code or a cited source, it reads
**"not specified in code"** or **"not measured"** — never invented.

This chapter is split for length:
- **`05a_MODELS.md`** — the six trainable PyTorch models (Geo-PINN, FireSmokeNet, EODownstream,
  DeepAnomaly, AuthenticityNet, CQLPolicy) and the two learned fusion heads (GMFHead, AttentionFusionHead).
- **`05b_MODELS.md`** — the numpy physics models (infinite-slope FS, Iverson transient head, Fukuzono 1/v,
  Caine I–D, Heskestad / Byram / Strouhal / gray-body fire physics) and the numpy fusion / decision / shield
  / conformal pieces (NF-1..4, FM-1, PHARAOH, GMF, BLUE/GLS, hierarchical, adapters, RL/OPE, conformal
  calibration, the single decision function, the shield).
- **This file (`05_MODELS.md`)** — the opening all-models comparison table, then the closing end-to-end
  meta-fusion explanation, the all-models comparison table (annotated), and the "which model when" guide.

---

## 0. Opening comparison table — ALL models

Class legend (`MODEL_CARDS.md`): **A** deterministic/established physics · **B** physics-informed or
physics-regularized learning · **C** novel term (flag-gated OFF, A/B fallback — Rule 20) · **data**
data-driven · **advisory** RL policy. "Trained?" is **no** for every row (nothing trained — `_CANON.md §0`).
"Runs?" distinguishes the numpy core (executes, tested) from the torch layer (compile-verified only).

| 2 | **FireSmokeNet** | Spatiotemporal fire/smoke detection (CCTV); temporal false-alarm suppressor | A-aux + data | clip `(B,T,C,H,W)` → `{fire,smoke} prob, flicker_hz` | no | no (torch) | `deep/fire_cnn.py` |

## CLOSING A. End-to-end meta-fusion (how the models combine into one advisory level)

This is the integration contract. All source is from `ws5_fusion_rl/` and `ws6_robust/` (read for this
chapter). The pipeline has **exactly one decision path** (`decision.py` docstring):

```
                 physics gates (ws1a/ws1b)         deep models (deep/, trained on Kaggle)
                 ──────────────────────────         ─────────────────────────────────────
   geo_gate ──► ExpertOutput(geo_phys, Class A)      geo_pinn ─┐
   fire_gate ─► ExpertOutput(fire_phys, Class A)      fire_cnn  ├─ deep_expert(source, prob)  (adapters.py)
                                                       eo        │  → ExpertOutput with class + reliability cap
                                                       anomaly   │     (deepfake HARD-capped r ≤ 0.4)
                                                       deepfake ─┘
                             │                                   │
                             └──────────────┬────────────────────┘
                                            ▼
           (optional) hierarchical.fuse_group per workstream  ──►  one ExpertOutput per group
             • within-group weights = effective_weight (NF) OR BLUE/GLS (correlation.py) if redundancy given
             • propagates u (NF-3), c (agreement), r (reliability-weighted), class (weakest-guarantee wins)
                                            ▼
                        fusion_models.fuse(experts, cfg)   (dispatcher)
             • default/fallback  : FM-1 precision-weighted mean          (Class B)
             • if fusion.model=GMF: gmf_fuse → base + bounded residual    (Class B; residual=0 w/o a head)
             • if operator.pharaoh: PHARAOH power-mean (ρ=1+κ·D·S)         (Class C, OFF by default)
             → FusionResult(p, u_star = NF-3 conflict uncertainty, salience = NF-4, model, used_classC)
                                            ▼
                        decision.decide(experts, shield_signals, cfg)
             • point = conformal_level(fused.p, p*, level_thresholds)      p* = C_FA/(C_FA+C_miss) = 0.0476
             • floor = shield_floor(shield_signals)   (monotone; can only RAISE)
             • level = Level.raise_to(point, floor)
             • uncertain = (no experts) OR (u_star > 0.6) OR drift   → abstain + escalate, never silent
             → Decision(level, risk, conformal set, shield, uncertain, advisory=True, used_classC)
```

**Gating.** Per expert, the effective (gating) weight is (`nf.effective_weight`, UNTESTED-free — this is
numpy, runs):

```
w~_i = available_i · r_i · c_i · exp( −u_i / τ ),   τ = 0.5 default
```

so an expert is down-weighted by low reliability `r`, low physics-consistency `c`, or high uncertainty `u`.
FM-1 normalizes these to a convex combination of the experts' probabilities. GMF uses the same weights for
its gate, then adds a residual that is **hard-clipped to ±`residual_cap` (default 0.1)** and defaults to **0**
when no trained head is loaded — so with no head, GMF ≡ FM-1 (verified by construction, `gmf.py`).

**Uncertainty propagation.** NF-3 (`nf.nf3_conflict_to_uncertainty`):

```
U* = Σ w_i u_i  +  λ · D(p),   D(p) = weighted dispersion of the p_i,   λ = 0.3 default
```

Disagreement between experts (`D`) *raises* the fused uncertainty, so conflict drives the system toward
"uncertain," not toward a confident wrong answer. `U*` sets the `Reliability` enum
(`decision._reliability_from_uncertainty`: <0.2 HIGH, <0.4 MEDIUM, <0.6 LOW, else UNRELIABLE; drift forces
UNRELIABLE) and widens the provisional conformal prediction set (`decision._pred_set`).

**Missing / out-of-regime behavior.** `ExpertOutput.available=False` experts are dropped from every sum
(FM-1, GMF, NF, hierarchical). If **no** expert is available, `fuse` returns `p=0` and `decide` sets
`uncertain=True` (`decision.decide`: `uncertain = (not avail) or …`). Physics gates fail safe: Iverson
returns 0 head for `t≤0`; Caine returns NaN threshold for `D≤0`; `nd2_transmittance_temperature` lets its
uncertainty `σ_K` **blow up as transmittance τ_s → 0** (ill-conditioned ⇒ "uncertain"). Graceful modality
degradation is handled in `ws6_robust/missing_modality.py` (C8). `[CONFIRMED by code]`.

**Bounded residual (the central safety property).** Only the GMF/attention residual can nudge the fused
value, and it is clipped to ±cap, so a mis-trained head **cannot dominate the physics-anchored base**
(`gmf.bounded_residual`, `fusion_head.AttentionFusionHead`). The attention base is additionally **convex**
(softmax over experts) so it stays within `[min_i p_i, max_i p_i]` — attention can re-weight but cannot
invent a probability outside the experts' own range. `[CONFIRMED by code]`.

**Shield (deterministic, monotone, un-trained).** `shield.shield_floor` raises a floor from hard signals:
`FS<1` → ORANGE; corroborated `tilt_rate>5°/day` (≥2 nodes) → RED; `rain_24h>150 mm` on high-susceptibility
slope → ORANGE; GLOF lake-drop + downstream stage-jump → RED; fire multi-node → ORANGE. The decision takes
`max(point, floor)` — the shield can **only raise** the level, never lower it (Rule 19). A single
uncorroborated node cannot reach RED (spatial corroboration required). `[CONFIRMED by code]`.

**Calibrated thresholds.** `decision.conformal_level` maps risk to a level at cut points `(p*, 4p*, 10p*)`
by default, or at **calibrated** cut points from `ws6_robust.conformal_risk_threshold` (RCPS/CRC) when a
calibration set exists — provably bounding the miss-rate instead of using an ad-hoc multiplier.

**Advisory invariant.** Every output is a `Decision(advisory=True)` for a human operator; **no path issues a
public alert** (R19). The deepfake expert's reliability is hard-capped at 0.4 in `adapters._POLICY`, so it can
never gate a life-safety decision. `[CONFIRMED by code]`.

## CLOSING C. "Which model when" — decision guide

- **Landslide / slope, you have soil params + rainfall:** run the **numpy geo gate** (FS + Iverson + Caine
  [+ Fukuzono if creep velocities exist]) — it always runs offline and drives the hard shield (`FS<1`). Add
  **GeoPINN** as *corroborating* evidence only (never a substitute for the hard gate; `MODEL_CARDS.md §1`).
- **Creep instrument with a rising trend:** **Fukuzono 1/v** for a failure-time forecast — but report the
  **prediction interval**, not a point (advisory, R19). Needs ≥ a few positive velocities.
- **CCTV fire/smoke:** **FireSmokeNet** (temporal GRU kills single-frame glint/headlight false alarms);
  **fire gate** supplies the Heskestad/Byram physics plausibility. Keep the Strouhal/ND Class-C terms OFF
  unless validated.
- **Satellite change / susceptibility:** **EODownstream** (frozen encoder + small head) — cheap under the
  GPU budget; record which encoder was used (Rule 16).
- **IoT telemetry stream, no labels:** **DeepAnomaly** (trained on normal only) as the admitted upgrade; the
  always-on fallback is the **numpy ws8 ensemble** (`CODE_INVENTORY §7`).
- **Crowd-sourced / social media clip:** **AuthenticityNet** to *down-weight* suspect media — it can only
  suppress confidence, never trigger (r ≤ 0.4).
- **Turning a fused risk into HOLD/WATCH/ALARM:** the **RuleBaselinePolicy** (threshold = p* = 0.0476) is the
  default; **CQLPolicy** is used *only* if `ope_admission` admits it (positivity + ESS + value ≥ baseline),
  and it is always raised to the shield floor.
- **Combining several experts:** default **FM-1**; use **hierarchical + BLUE/GLS** when a workstream has
  redundant sensors (anti-double-count); turn on **GMF** residual only with a validated exported head; keep
  **PHARAOH** OFF unless its anti-complacency behavior is explicitly wanted and validated.
- **Reporting any number:** nothing may be advertised until `train.admit_model` (spatial-block CV real-win
  over climatology AND logistic, bootstrap CI lower bound > 0) admits the model (R16) — and today that gate
  has **not been run on real data** (no datasets).

See `05a_MODELS.md` and `05b_MODELS.md` for the full per-model treatment.

# 05a — MODELS (deep layer): the six PyTorch models + the two learned fusion heads

> Companion to `05_MODELS.md` (index, opening table, closing meta-fusion). **Every model here is
> `py_compile`-clean only and was NOT run on a GPU in this environment** (`_CANON.md §2`). All torch snippets
> are therefore **UNTESTED** (no torch/CUDA in the sandbox). All architecture/shape/loss statements are taken
> **verbatim from the code read for this chapter** (`trinetra/src/trinetra/deep/*.py`); where the code does
> not fix a value it reads **"not specified in code."** No TRINETRA accuracy/latency number exists — every
> such field is **"not measured."**

Shared infrastructure (`deep/layers.py`, read for this chapter), reused below so each model section can refer
to it without repetition:
- **`MLP(sizes, act=SiLU, norm=False, dropout=0.0, out_act=None)`** — linear stack; inserts `LayerNorm` (if
  `norm`) + `SiLU` + optional `Dropout` between hidden layers; no activation after the final linear.
- **`ConvBNAct(c_in,c_out,k=3,s=1,p=1)`** — `Conv2d(bias=False) → BatchNorm2d → SiLU`.
- **`Chomp1d`, `TemporalBlock`, `TCN`** — dilated **causal** 1-D conv stack (weight-norm convs, right-pad
  trimmed by `Chomp1d`, residual + `SiLU`, dilation `2**i` per block). Causal ⇒ no look-ahead (anti-leak
  invariant, gate G6).

Shared training infrastructure (`deep/train.py`, read for this chapter) — applies to models 1–6 and the
heads; details repeated per-model only where they differ:
- `set_seed(seed=0)` seeds `random`, `numpy`, `torch`, `torch.cuda` (all GPUs).
- `TrainConfig`: `epochs=20, batch_size=64 (per-GPU base), lr=3e-4, weight_decay=1e-4, grad_clip=1.0,
  amp=True, seed=0, k_folds=5, num_workers=4, parallel="auto", scale_batch_by_gpus=True,
  scale_lr_by_gpus=True, pin_memory=True`.
- Multi-GPU: `nn.DataParallel` by default on **T4×2** (`_LossModule` wraps model+step so the whole loss runs
  per-replica); effective batch = `batch_size × n_gpus`; **linear-LR scaling** `lr × n_gpus` (Goyal et al.
  2017, named in code); AMP via `torch.cuda.amp` + `GradScaler`; `AdamW` over `requires_grad` params;
  `clip_grad_norm_(grad_clip)`; `setup_perf()` enables cuDNN benchmark + TF32.
- DDP path (`deep/ddp.py`): `mp.spawn` one process/GPU, `DistributedSampler`, NCCL all-reduce, rank-0 save.
- Admission (`admit_model`): spatial-block CV → `ReportGuard` requires a bootstrap **real-win** over
  **climatology AND numpy logistic** on the cost-loss (C_FA=5, C_miss=100) with CI lower bound > 0 (R16); it
  also reports ECE/MCE/Brier **diagnostics** (never relaxes the gate). Temperature scaling via
  `TemperatureScaler` (single `log_T`, LBFGS on validation logits — Guo et al., named in code).

**GPU-hour budget (planning, `_CANON.md §8`):** Kaggle ~30 GPU-h/week, keep ≥15% reserve → ~25.5 usable;
session ~12 h; P100 (16 GB) or 2×T4. Per-model GPU-h splits below are **[EST] / planning** — nothing has been
run, so no measured wall-clock exists.

## 1. GeoPINN — physics-informed slope-hydrology network (Class B)

**File:** `deep/geo_pinn.py` · **WS:** ws1b_geophys · **Trained?** no · **Runs here?** no (torch).

### (1) Name / role / inputs → outputs
A physics-informed NN that learns the transient pressure-head field `ψ(Z,t; forcing, soil)` under the
linearized Iverson/Richards diffusion, then maps the physical state to a calibrated landslide probability.
**Role:** *corroborating* evidence that sits beside — never replaces — the deterministic FS/Iverson hard gate,
which still runs at inference (`MODEL_CARDS.md §1`, `geo_pinn.py` docstring).

- **In:** `Z (B,1)`, `t (B,1)`, `rain (B,1)`, `static (B,6)` = `[c', φ, γ, z, β, susceptibility]`.
- **Out (`forward`):** `{logit (B,1), prob=σ(logit), psi (B,1), fs (B,1)}`.

### (2) Selection rationale + alternatives
Why a PINN (code docstring): failure labels are scarce, so the **PDE residual + FS physics supply a dense,
label-free training signal** that keeps the net on the physically admissible manifold and improves
extrapolation to unseen rainfall forcing.

Alternatives considered (from `_CANON.md §6`, `model_set_decision.md`):
- **Full fire/geo PINN as a deployed on-device solver → [INFEASIBLE]** (stiffness, loss-weight imbalance,
  spectral bias, non-identifiability). Decision: physics enters as **soft features/priors with a Class-A
  fallback**, not as a live solver. Our result: **not measured**.
- **Pure data-driven classifier (logistic / GBDT):** the mandatory `eval` baseline is exactly a
  `LogisticNumpy` the model must beat on spatial-CV — kept as the baseline, not the deployed model.
- **Deterministic FS/Iverson only:** retained as the **hard gate**; PINN added only as corroboration. Our
  comparative skill vs any of these: **not measured** (nothing trained).

### (3) Full formulation (as in code)
Field network: `MLP([3 + 6, 128, 128, 128, 1], norm=True)` maps `[Z, t, rain, static] → ψ`.
Risk head: `MLP([2 + 1 + 6, 64, 32, 1], norm=True)` maps `[ψ, tanh(ψ), FS, static] → logit`.

Differentiable FS (`losses.factor_of_safety_torch`, mirrors the numpy `ws1b_geophys.fs`):
```
FS = ( c' + σ'_n · tan φ' ) / ( γ · z · sin β · cos β ),   σ'_n = γ z cos²β − u_w + σ_s
u_w = γ_w · max(ψ, 0),   γ_w = 9.81
```
PDE residual (`losses.richards_iverson_residual`) — linearized Iverson/Richards diffusion:
```
residual = ψ_t − D1 · ψ_ZZ          (target 0)
```
with `ψ_t, ψ_Z, ψ_ZZ` from `torch.autograd.grad` (create_graph). **Slope enters ONLY via `D1`**
(`D1 = D0/cos²β`, bug-guard mirrored from the numpy gate — `_CANON.md §4`, `geo_pinn.py` §).
Physics loss (`physics_loss`):
```
L_phys = physics_weight · mean(residual²)  +  fs_weight · mean( 1[FS<1] · (1 − prob)² )
```
The second term is a **label-free hinge**: when FS<1 the risk prob should be high (physics-anchored
supervision). Total objective (`geo_pinn_step`):
```
loss = physics_weight · L_phys  +  (data_weight · BCE(logit, label))   # BCE only where labels exist
```
Config defaults (`GeoPINNConfig`): `n_static=6, hidden=(128,128,128), dropout=0.0, physics_weight=1.0,
fs_weight=0.5, data_weight=1.0`.

- **Assumptions / regime:** linearized 1-D vertical diffusion of pressure head; slope-parallel seepage;
  `z ≪ slope length` (inherited from the infinite-slope / Iverson parents, `08_equations_register.md`
  E-01/E-02, GH-01/GH-02). `MODEL_CARDS.md §1`: "linearized 1-D diffusion; not a substitute for the hard
  gate; needs site soil params."
- **Boundary/initial conditions:** **not specified in code** (the net learns `ψ` over sampled `(Z,t)`
  collocation points supplied in the batch; no explicit BC/IC term appears in `geo_pinn.py`/`losses.py`).
- **Limiting cases:** as `ψ→0`, `u_w→0` and FS → the dry infinite-slope value; the FS form reduces to the
  saturated effective-stress form at `σ_s=0` (matches `fs.py`). Dimensional check: FS is dimensionless
  (kPa/kPa); `residual` has units of `ψ_t` (m/s) once `D1` carries m²/s — consistent with a diffusion PDE.

### (4) Architecture diagram + tensor shapes (UNTESTED)
```
 Z(B,1) t(B,1) rain(B,1) static(B,6)
        │        concat → (B,9)
        ▼
   field MLP [9→128→128→128→1]  (LayerNorm+SiLU between)         → ψ (B,1)
        │
        ├── u_w = 9.81·max(ψ,0) ─┐
        │                        ▼
        │           factor_of_safety_torch(c',φ,γ,z,β,u_w)        → FS (B,1)
        ▼
   feats = [ψ, tanh(ψ), FS, static]  → (B, 2+1+6 = 9)
        ▼
   risk MLP [9→64→32→1]  → logit (B,1) → σ → prob (B,1)
```

### (5) I/O spec, normalization, units
Inputs are physical: `Z` depth [m], `t` time [s or h — unit not fixed in code; must match `D1` units],
`rain` surface flux/intensity, `static` = `[c' kPa, φ deg, γ kN/m³, z m, β deg, susceptibility (unitless)]`.
`u_w` in kPa (`γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³ · ψ[m]`). **Input normalization: not specified in code** (no scaler in
`geo_pinn.py`/`datamodules.GeoSeriesDataset`; `static` is consumed raw). Output `prob ∈ [0,1]`.

### (6) Training recipe (as in code / planning)
- Dataset: `datamodules.GeoSeriesDataset` (`.npz` with `Z,t,rain,static[6]`, optional `label`, `lat,lon` →
  spatial `block`). Label key emitted only when labels exist (physics-only pretraining supported).
- Step: `geo_pinn_step` rebuilds `Z,t` as **leaf tensors** via `detach().requires_grad_(True)` so
  `autograd.grad` works under both single-GPU and DataParallel (DP scatter makes inputs non-leaf) — code
  comment flags this as the fix that makes the PINN "safe to train on Kaggle T4×2."
- Optimizer/schedule/precision: shared `TrainConfig` (AdamW, lr 3e-4 ×n_gpus, wd 1e-4, grad-clip 1.0, AMP,
  20 epochs, 5-fold spatial-CV). **LR schedule beyond linear GPU scaling: not specified in code.**
- Early stopping / checkpointing: **not specified in code** (`train.py` trains a fixed epoch count; no
  early-stop or checkpoint logic in the files read). Seeds via `set_seed`.
- GPU-h: **[EST] planning only**, part of the ≤30 GPU-h/week budget; **not measured**.

### (7) Hyperparameter table (values from code only)
| HP | Value | Rationale (from code/docstring) | Sensitivity |
|----|-------|---------------------------------|-------------|
| hidden | (128,128,128) | field-net capacity | not measured |
| risk hidden | (64,32) | small head on physical state | not measured |
| physics_weight | 1.0 | weight on PDE residual | not measured |
| fs_weight | 0.5 | weight on FS<1 hinge | not measured |
| data_weight | 1.0 | weight on data BCE | not measured |
| dropout | 0.0 | — | not measured |
| lr / wd / epochs | 3e-4 / 1e-4 / 20 | shared TrainConfig | not measured |

PINN loss-weight sensitivity is a known failure axis (`_CANON.md §6`) but is **not measured** here.

### (8) Code (from repo; UNTESTED)
Model definition (`geo_pinn.py`, abridged):
```python
class GeoPINN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, cfg=GeoPINNConfig()):
        self.field = MLP([3 + cfg.n_static, *cfg.hidden, 1], norm=True, dropout=cfg.dropout)
        self.risk  = MLP([2 + 1 + cfg.n_static, 64, 32, 1], norm=True, dropout=cfg.dropout)
    def forward(self, Z, t, rain, static):
        psi = self.field(torch.cat([Z, t, rain, static], dim=1))
        u_w = 9.81 * torch.clamp(psi, min=0.0)
        fs  = factor_of_safety_torch(*(static[:, i:i+1] for i in range(5)), u_w)
        logit = self.risk(torch.cat([psi, torch.tanh(psi), fs, static], dim=1))
        return {"logit": logit, "prob": torch.sigmoid(logit), "psi": psi, "fs": fs}
```
Training-loop objective (`geo_pinn_step`, abridged):
```python
Z = batch["Z"].detach().requires_grad_(True); t = batch["t"].detach().requires_grad_(True)
out  = model(Z, t, batch["rain"], batch["static"])
phys = model.physics_loss(Z, t, batch["rain"], batch["static"], D1)
loss = model.cfg.physics_weight * phys
if batch.get("label") is not None:
    loss = loss + model.cfg.data_weight * bce(out["logit"].squeeze(-1), batch["label"].float())
```
Inference (UNTESTED): `prob = model(Z,t,rain,static)["prob"]` → `deep_expert("geo_pinn", prob)` →
ExpertOutput(Class B, reliability default 0.90, cap 1.00; `adapters._POLICY`).

### (9) Uncertainty & calibration
Confidence = `σ(logit)`. Calibrated post-hoc by `TemperatureScaler` on validation logits (Guo et al.). ECE/
MCE/Brier reported as diagnostics in `admit_model`. What is passed to fusion: a single `prob`, wrapped by
`deep_expert` with Class B and reliability ≤ 1.0; the fusion layer attaches `u` (default 0.3 in `deep_expert`
unless overridden). No aleatoric/epistemic split is produced in code. `[CONFIRMED by code]`.

### (10) Failure modes
- **Validity regime:** linearized 1-D diffusion; invalid for strongly 2-D/3-D flow, macropore/fracture flow,
  or non-linear van Genuchten regimes (parents are Class A/B with regime limits). → down-weighted, never the
  hard gate.
- **OOD:** unseen soil/rainfall far from training support; PINN extrapolation is unreliable (the stated
  reason it is corroboration-only).
- **Adversarial / numerical:** autograd-based residual is sensitive to loss weighting (spectral bias). The
  leaf-tensor fix (`geo_pinn_step`) prevents a known DataParallel crash → linked to chapter 13.
- **Mitigations:** hard FS gate + shield (`FS<1`→ORANGE) run regardless; residual bounded role; Class-B
  fallback to deterministic Iverson.

### (11) Ablations / results
Our numbers: **not measured** (not trained). Paper anchors (source-reported, kept separate): PINN method
(Raissi et al. 2019 — classic, **no arXiv ID in this repo ledger**); Iverson 2000 (WRR) for the transient
physics; spatial-block CV mandated to avoid overstated skill (2608.22293 `[ABS]`, `_CANON.md §6`). No
TRINETRA ablation has been run.

### (12) Literature-backed improvement ideas
- Antecedent-moisture-aware probabilistic rainfall threshold as an extra physics prior (`08_…register` GB-03,
  "CORE EWS"). `[HYPOTHESIS]`
- Probabilistic infinite-slope `P_f = Φ(−β_rel)` to emit a calibrated failure probability instead of a point
  FS (`08_…register` GB-01). `[HYPOTHESIS]`
- Causal/curriculum PINN training to combat spectral bias. `[HYPOTHESIS]`

### (13) Reference IDs (→ chapter 19)
Iverson 2000 WRR; standard infinite-slope geotech; Lu & Likos (suction stress); Raissi et al. 2019 (PINN);
2608.22293 `[ABS]` (spatial CV). Classic refs carry **no arXiv ID in this repo**.

## 2. FireSmokeNet — spatiotemporal fire/smoke detector (Class A-aux + data)

**File:** `deep/fire_cnn.py` · **WS:** ws1a_firephys / ws4_cctv · **Trained?** no · **Runs here?** no (torch).

### (1) Role / I/O
Per-frame CNN encoder → temporal GRU → multi-label `{fire, smoke}` logits + an auxiliary flicker-frequency
head. The **temporal pathway is the key false-alarm suppressor** (sun glint/headlights are single-frame; real
fire flickers persistently). The Heskestad/Byram physics gate still runs at inference.
- **In:** clip `x (B, T, C, H, W)`, default `C=3`.
- **Out:** `{logits (B,2), prob=σ(logits), flicker_hz (B,)}`.

### (2) Selection rationale + alternatives
- **Single-frame CNN:** rejected as the sole detector — cannot suppress transient glint/headlight false
  alarms. Kept conceptually as the frame encoder, wrapped by the GRU.
- **3-D CNN / video transformer:** heavier; not chosen (GPU budget C3; `_CANON.md §8`). CNN→GRU is the
  lighter spatiotemporal choice in code. Our comparison: **not measured**.
- **Pure physics (Heskestad/Byram) gate:** retained as the owning physics gate; the net adds learned
  appearance/temporal features. Novel ND flicker term stays Class-C OFF (Rule 20). Our skill: **not measured**.

### (3) Formulation (as in code)
`FrameEncoder` (`ConvBNAct` blocks + MaxPool, final `AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)`):
```
ConvBNAct(C,32)→Pool→ConvBNAct(32,64)→Pool→ConvBNAct(64,128)→Pool→ConvBNAct(128,128)→AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
out_dim = base*4 = 128
```
Temporal + heads:
```
feats = encoder(x.reshape(B·T,C,H,W)).reshape(B,T,128)
seq,hN = GRU(input=128, hidden=128, batch_first=True)
h = hN.squeeze(0)                 # (B,128) last hidden state
logits = Linear(128,2)(h)         # [fire, smoke]
flicker_hz = relu(Linear(128,1)(h)).squeeze(-1)
```
Loss (`loss`): multi-label `BCEWithLogits(logits, targets)` (+ optional `pos_weight`), plus the **Class-C,
default-OFF** Strouhal aux:
```
total = BCE  +  strouhal_weight · strouhal_consistency_loss(flicker_hz, plume_size_m)
strouhal_consistency_loss = MSE( flicker_hz , 1.5 / sqrt(max(D,1e-3)) )    # f ≈ 1.5/√D  (Class A EF-08)
```
`FireNetConfig`: `in_ch=3, base=32, gru_hidden=128, n_classes=2, strouhal_weight=0.0` (OFF by default —
Rule 20). Dimensional check: Strouhal target `[Hz] = 1/√(m)` only with the implicit `1.5 m^½·Hz` coefficient
(SI-inconsistent constant, flagged `[coeff-verify]` in `established_ef.py`).

### (4) Architecture diagram + shapes (UNTESTED)
```
x (B,T,C,H,W)
   └ reshape (B·T,C,H,W) → FrameEncoder → (B·T,128) → reshape (B,T,128)
        └ GRU → hN (1,B,128) → h (B,128)
             ├ Linear(128,2) → logits (B,2) → σ → prob (B,2)=[p_fire,p_smoke]
             └ Linear(128,1) → relu → flicker_hz (B,)
```

### (5) I/O spec, normalization, units
Images expected as float tensors; **normalization/augmentation: not specified in code** (dataset
`ImageFolderNPZ` casts to float32, no transform pipeline in the files read). `flicker_hz` in Hz; `plume_size_m`
in metres. Outputs are per-class probabilities in [0,1].

### (6) Training recipe
Shared `TrainConfig` (AdamW, AMP, DataParallel, 5-fold spatial-CV, temperature calibration). Dataset
`ImageFolderNPZ` (`images`,`labels`,`block`). `pos_weight` supported for class imbalance. Augmentation/
early-stopping/checkpointing: **not specified in code**. GPU-h: **[EST] planning**; **not measured**.

### (7) Hyperparameters (code only)
| HP | Value | Rationale | Sensitivity |
|----|-------|-----------|-------------|
| base channels | 32 | encoder width | not measured |
| gru_hidden | 128 | temporal state | not measured |
| n_classes | 2 (multi-label) | fire+smoke | not measured |
| strouhal_weight | 0.0 (OFF) | Class-C gated (Rule 20) | not measured |

### (8) Code (repo; UNTESTED)
```python
def forward(self, x):           # x: (B,T,C,H,W)
    B,T,C,H,W = x.shape
    feats = self.encoder(x.reshape(B*T,C,H,W)).reshape(B,T,-1)
    seq,hN = self.gru(feats); h = hN.squeeze(0)
    logits = self.head(h); flick = torch.relu(self.flicker(h)).squeeze(-1)
    return {"logits": logits, "prob": torch.sigmoid(logits), "flicker_hz": flick}
```
Inference → `deep_expert("fire_cnn", p_fire)` → ExpertOutput(Class DATA, r default 0.80, cap 0.95).

### (9) Uncertainty & calibration
Per-class `σ(logit)`; temperature-scaled; ECE/MCE/Brier diagnostics. GRU temporal persistence is the implicit
confidence mechanism for flicker. Passed to fusion: `p_fire` as a DATA expert (cap 0.95). `[CONFIRMED by code]`.

### (10) Failure modes
Night/IR domain shift, smoke-only vs flame-only ambiguity, aliased flicker on low-fps CCTV (the exact failure
B-05 targets, `model_set_decision.md`). Mitigations: temporal GRU, physics gate, Class-C flicker term OFF
until validated → chapter 13.

### (11) Ablations / results
Our numbers: **not measured**. Paper anchors: Strouhal/puffing `f≈1.5/√D` (Cetegen & Ahmed 1993, classic);
EF-08 inventory `[coeff-verify]`. No TRINETRA ablation run.

### (12) Improvement ideas
Aliasing-aware flicker feature (B-05) as a learned-vs-physics consistency input `[HYPOTHESIS]`; IR/thermal
second stream `[HYPOTHESIS]`; swap GRU for a small temporal transformer if budget allows `[HYPOTHESIS]`.

### (13) Reference IDs
Cetegen & Ahmed 1993 (puffing); Heskestad 1983; Byram (convection number) — classic, no repo arXiv.

## 3. EODownstream — frozen EO foundation encoder + head (Class data)

**File:** `deep/eo_encoder.py` · **WS:** ws1b (EO) · **Trained?** head only (planned) · **Runs here?** no.

### (1) Role / I/O
A pretrained geospatial foundation model is used **FROZEN** as a feature extractor; a small trainable MLP head
maps patch embeddings to a hazard-susceptibility/change logit.
- **In:** multispectral patch `x (B, C, H, W)`, default `in_chans=6` (e.g. S2 subset).
- **Out:** `{logit (B,1), prob=σ(logit)}`.

### (2) Rationale + alternatives
- **Full fine-tune of the encoder:** rejected — blows the GPU budget (C3) and overfits scarce labels; code
  freezes the encoder deliberately.
- **Train a CNN from scratch:** rejected for the same reasons (label scarcity).
- **FM weights vs timm substitute:** code injects a real FM via `encoder_factory`, else falls back to a
  **timm backbone** (`resnet50` default) as a "transparent, clearly-labelled substitute" — the chosen encoder
  **must be recorded in the eval report** (Rule 16, docstring + `MODEL_CARDS.md §3`). Our result: **not measured**.

### (3) Formulation (as in code)
```
encoder = encoder_factory() OR timm.create_model(backbone, pretrained, in_chans, num_classes=0, global_pool="avg")
if freeze: encoder.parameters().requires_grad_(False); encoder.eval() even in train()  # fixed BN stats
head = MLP([feat_dim, 256, 64, 1], norm=True, dropout=0.1)
forward: feats = encoder(x) under set_grad_enabled(not freeze); logit = head(feats); prob = σ(logit)
loss = BCEWithLogits(logit.squeeze(-1), targets, pos_weight)
```
`EOConfig`: `backbone="resnet50", in_chans=6, pretrained=True, freeze=True, head_hidden=(256,64), n_out=1`.
Note (code): overriding `train()` keeps the frozen encoder in `eval()` so BatchNorm running stats stay fixed.

### (4) Architecture diagram + shapes (UNTESTED)
```
x (B,6,H,W) → [FROZEN encoder] → feats (B, feat_dim)   # feat_dim = encoder.num_features
            → head MLP [feat_dim→256→64→1] → logit (B,1) → σ → prob (B,1)
```
`feat_dim` is backbone-dependent (**not fixed in code**; `resnet50` → 2048 by timm convention, not asserted
in-repo).

### (5) I/O spec, normalization, units
Multispectral reflectance patches; **channel count set per dataset** (`in_chans`). Normalization: **not
specified in code** (depends on the FM's expected preprocessing — a documented gap). Output `prob∈[0,1]`.

### (6) Training recipe
Only the head trains (encoder frozen). Shared `TrainConfig`; `pos_weight` for imbalance; dropout 0.1 in head;
spatial-CV; temperature calibration. Augmentation/early-stop/checkpoint: **not specified in code**. GPU-h:
small (head-only) **[EST]**; **not measured**.

### (7) Hyperparameters
| HP | Value | Rationale | Sensitivity |
|----|-------|-----------|-------------|
| backbone | resnet50 (timm) | transparent substitute | not measured |
| in_chans | 6 | S2 subset default | not measured |
| freeze | True | budget + anti-overfit | not measured |
| head_hidden | (256,64) | small head | not measured |
| head dropout | 0.1 | regularize small head | not measured |

### (8) Code (repo; UNTESTED)
```python
self.encoder = timm.create_model(cfg.backbone, pretrained=cfg.pretrained, in_chans=cfg.in_chans,
                                 num_classes=0, global_pool="avg"); feat_dim = self.encoder.num_features
if cfg.freeze: [p.requires_grad_(False) for p in self.encoder.parameters()]
self.head = MLP([feat_dim, *cfg.head_hidden, cfg.n_out], norm=True, dropout=0.1)
```

### (10) Failure modes
Encoder-preprocessing mismatch, band/sensor shift, label scarcity. Mitigation: freezing + record encoder +
spatial-CV. The timm substitute must be flagged in the report so skill isn't attributed to a real FM.
