| `strouhal_consistency_loss`, `deep_svdd_loss`, `cost_sensitive_bce`, `brier_score` | `losses.py` | Physics/honesty-aware training losses. |
| `GeoPINN(cfg=GeoPINNConfig())` | `geo_pinn.py` | **Model 1.** `.forward(Z,t,rain,static) → {logit,prob,psi,fs}`; `.physics_loss(...)`; `geo_pinn_step(model,batch,D1,bce)` (rebuilds Z,t as leaves so autograd works under DataParallel). |
| `FireSmokeNet(cfg=FireNetConfig())` | `fire_cnn.py` | **Model 2.** CNN→GRU; `.forward(x)→{logits,prob,flicker_hz}`; `.loss(...)` with Strouhal aux (weight 0 default). |
| `EODownstream(cfg=EOConfig(), encoder_factory=None)` | `eo_encoder.py` | **Model 3/4.** Frozen timm/FM encoder + MLP head; `.forward(x)→{logit,prob}`. |
| `DeepAnomaly(cfg=AnomalyConfig())` | `anomaly_deep.py` | **Model 4.** TCN AE + forecast + Deep-SVDD; `.init_center(...)`, `.loss(x)`, `.anomaly_score(x)`. |
| `AuthenticityNet(cfg=DeepfakeConfig())` | `deepfake_net.py` | **Model 5.** RGB + FFT two-stream; `.forward(x)→{logit,p_fake}`; `max_reliability=0.4`. |
| `CQLPolicy(cfg=CQLConfig())` | `offline_rl.py` | **Model 6.** `ACTIONS=("HOLD","WATCH","ALARM")`; `.cql_loss(s,a,r,s_next,done)`; `.act(s, shield_floor_idx=0)` (raised to shield floor); `.action_probs(s)` for OPE. |
| `GMFHead(hidden=16)` | `fusion_head.py` | Learned bounded residual over `[base,dispersion,salience]`. |
| `AttentionFusionHead(feat_dim=4, hidden=16, cap=0.1)` | `fusion_head.py` | Attention over per-workstream experts; convex base (bounded to `[min p_i, max p_i]`) + bounded residual. `.loss(out, target, c_fa, c_miss)` cost-sensitive BCE. |
| `export_numpy(head, cap=0.1)` / `export_attention_numpy(head)` | `fusion_head.py` | **The numpy export bridge** — serialize a trained head to a pure-numpy closure for the torch-free gateway. |

| `ddp_setup/cleanup`, `is_main`, `wrap_ddp`, `ddp_sampler`, `ddp_loader`, `launch_ddp`, `ddp_worker` | `ddp.py` | DistributedDataParallel launcher (one process per GPU, rank-0 save). |

## 16.6 CONFIG SYSTEM

### 16.6.1 Where config lives and how it loads

Configs are **JSON** under `configs/` (not yaml — `pyyaml` is unavailable; `README.md §Environment`). The
loader in `common/config.py`:

1. starts from the in-code `DEFAULTS` dict (the safe path);
2. `load_config("fusion","firephys")` deep-merges `default.json`, then each named file on top;
3. parameters are read with dotted keys: `cfg.get("fusion.tau", 0.5)`, `cfg.get("firephys.nd1", False)`.

The three shipped files are intentionally minimal (defaults carry the rest):

```json
// configs/default.json
{ "seeds":[0,1,2,3,4], "cost":{"C_FA":5.0,"C_miss":100.0}, "alert":{"require_human_approval":true} }
// configs/fusion.json
{ "fusion":{"model":"FM-1","operator":{"pharaoh":false},"tau":0.5,"lambda":0.3} }
// configs/firephys.json
{ "firephys":{"nd1":false,...,"nd7":false} }
```

### 16.6.2 The cost model and p*

`cost.C_FA=5`, `cost.C_miss=100` ⇒ `Config.p_star = C_FA/(C_FA+C_miss) ≈ 0.0476`. This single number drives
(a) `eval.value_score.alarms_from_prob` (alarm iff `p ≥ p*`), (b) `conformal_level` bands at `p*, 4p*, 10p*`,
and (c) `RuleBaselinePolicy(threshold=0.0476)`. Change the asymmetry here and the whole decision policy
re-tunes consistently. (Matches `_CANON.md §4`.)

### 16.6.3 Class-C default-OFF flags (Rule 20)

The safety-critical flags, all **False by default**:
- `fusion.operator.pharaoh` — PHARAOH power-mean (Class C). Off ⇒ dispatcher falls back to FM-1.
- `firephys.nd1 … nd7` — novel fire-physics soft features (Class C). Off ⇒ `fire_gate` omits them.

`scripts/ci_gates.py` (`G-classC`) asserts all of these are `False`, and `Config.require_human_approval()` is
hard-wired `True` (`G-advisory`). This is why enabling a Class-C path is a deliberate, auditable act: the flag
must be flipped in a config, and when it is on, `used_classC=True` propagates into the `Decision` and the CAP
parameters.

---

## 16.7 CONVENTIONS

### 16.7.1 Naming
- Packages are `wsN<name>` matching the design workstreams (`ws1b_geophys`, `ws5_fusion_rl`, …). The doc-frame
  → artifact → package mapping is in `_CANON.md §3`; always say which scheme you mean.
- Each package `__init__.py` re-exports its public API in `__all__`; import from the package, not the module
  (`from trinetra.ws5_fusion_rl import decide`).
- Dataclasses pair a `…Inputs`/`…Config` with a `…Result` (e.g. `GeoInputs`/`GeoResult`,
  `FireInputs`/`FireResult`, `TrainConfig`).
- Physics coefficients needing primary-source confirmation are marked `[coeff-verify]` in docstrings.

### 16.7.2 The additive-upgrade rule (this is what protects the 128 tests)
New capability is added **without breaking existing call sites**:
- **New dataclass fields get defaults.** `ExpertOutput` grew `available=True`; `Decision` grew `used_classC`,
  `trace_id`; `FukuzonoFit` grew the prediction-interval fields — all defaulted, so old constructors still work.
- **New function parameters are keyword-only** (after `*`). Examples:
  `decide(..., *, drift=False, level_thresholds=None)`, `fuse_group(..., *, corr=None, redundant_groups=None)`,
  `inverse_velocity_fit(..., *, weights=None, recency_halflife=None, z=1.96)`. Positional calls in the tests
  keep passing.

Follow this rule for every extension; it is the reason upgrades like multipulse Iverson, ACI/Mondrian/CRC,
BLUE weighting, and hierarchical fusion landed without disturbing the existing suite.

### 16.7.3 numpy-2.0 note
Peak-to-peak uses the **free function** `np.ptp(x)`, not the removed array method `x.ptp()` (see
`ws8_anomaly.iforest_lite_score`/`mahalanobis_lite_score`/`anomaly_ensemble`). Keep using `np.ptp(...)` so the
core stays numpy-2.0 clean. `[CONFIRMED — present in source]`

### 16.7.4 PYTHONIOENCODING note
On Windows, set `$env:PYTHONIOENCODING="utf-8"` before running the suite so unittest's stderr summary is
UTF-8 clean (`_CANON.md §2`, `00_README §0.4`). `run_tests.py` may print a spurious `[exit code: 1]` because
unittest writes its summary to stderr — the real pass signal is the final `OK`.

### 16.7.5 How Class A/B/C labels appear in outputs
- On every `ExpertOutput.cls` (`PhysicsClass`): geo/fire gates emit `A`; the GeoPINN adapter maps to `B`;
  anomaly/eo/cctv/deepfake map to `DATA`; the RL policy is `ADVISORY`.
- On `Decision.used_classC` (bool) whenever a Class-C operator/feature contributed; `hierarchical.fuse_group`
  additionally labels a whole group with the **weakest-guarantee** member's class so novelty is never hidden.
- Surfaced to the operator by `ws3_alert.operator.present()` and into the CAP XML `used_classC` parameter.

### 16.7.6 Fail-safe / honesty conventions
- Heavy-lib paths **raise `MissingDependency`** rather than fabricate a result (Rule 16). Every torch
  interface stub does this; the `interfaces/` test suite asserts it.
- The decision **fails safe to `uncertain=True`** (never silent) when there are no experts, conflict `u_star`
  is high, or drift fired.
- The shield is **monotone** (`Level.raise_to`): fusion can never lower a safety floor.

---

## 16.8 HOW TO EXTEND

Concrete recipes. Each lists the files to touch and the test to add. Honor §16.7.2 (defaults + keyword-only)
so the 128 tests keep passing, and keep Class-C paths default-OFF.

### 16.8.1 Add a new expert / deep model
1. Implement the torch model under `src/trinetra/deep/<model>.py` (mirror `fire_cnn.py`: a `@dataclass`
   config, an `nn.Module` returning `{"logit"/"prob", …}`, a `.loss(...)`). Keep it torch-only.
2. Register its trust policy in `ws5_fusion_rl/adapters.py` `_POLICY` (`(default_r, cap_r, PhysicsClass)`),
   then at runtime: `deep_expert("<source>", prob) → ExpertOutput`. (Unknown sources raise, by design.)
3. Add a Kaggle kernel under `kaggle/` and the dataset entry in `deep/datamodules.py` (`KagglePaths` + a
   `Dataset` class exposing a `.block` array for spatial-CV).
4. The expert now flows through `decide()` unchanged — no decision-path edits.
5. **Test:** add to `tests/interfaces/` that the torch stub raises `MissingDependency` and that
   `deep_expert("<source>", p)` yields the right `cls`/capped `r` and flows through `decide()` (see
   `tests/fusion/test_adapters.py::test_flows_through_decide`).

### 16.8.2 Add a new physics relation
1. Add the function to the right gate package (`ws1b_geophys/` or `ws1a_firephys/`), pure numpy, with a
   Class label and `[coeff-verify]` in the docstring. If Class C, it must be **default-OFF** behind a new
   `firephys.ndX`/`geophys.*` flag with a Class-A/B fallback.
2. Wire it into the package `gate.py` as a **soft** sub-signal (noisy-OR for geo, consistency/uncertainty
   adjustment for fire) — never a hard trigger. Export it in `__init__.py` `__all__`.
3. If a differentiable version is useful for the PINN, mirror it in `deep/losses.py` (keep the slope-only-via-D1
   bug-guard).
4. **Test:** add a golden test in `tests/physics_golden/` (a limit/monotonicity property, like
   `test_saturated_limit` or `test_slope_only_through_D1`), and if Class-C, a `test_classC_off_by_default`.

### 16.8.3 Add a new fusion option (FM-x / operator)
1. Implement the operator in `ws5_fusion_rl/` (e.g. a new module, like `pharaoh.py`/`gmf.py`), using the
   audited NF primitives.
2. Register it in `fusion_models.fuse()`'s dispatcher behind a `fusion.model` value (or an `operator.*` flag
   if Class C — default OFF). Ensure it reports `used_classC` and **can never lower the shield floor**.
3. Keep FM-1 as the fallback whenever the new path is disabled or has <2 experts.
4. **Test:** add to `tests/fusion/` a property test (e.g. PHARAOH's `test_ge_arithmetic_mean_for_rho_ge_1`,
   or GMF's `test_residual_is_hard_bounded`), plus `test_default_is_fm1_not_classC`.

### 16.8.4 Add a new eval baseline
1. Add the baseline to `eval/baselines.py` (numpy/stdlib only, like `LogisticNumpy`).
2. Register it as a mandatory comparator wherever the gate is assembled — `pipeline/hindcast.run_hindcast`
   and `deep/train.admit_model` both loop over `[("climatology",…),("logistic",…)]`; add your `(name, p_base)`
   there and call `guard.add_baseline_verdict(name, real_win(...))`.
3. `ReportGuard.admit()` already requires a real win over **every** registered baseline, so adding one makes
   the gate strictly harder — exactly the intent (R16).
4. **Test:** extend `tests/eval/` (see `test_eval.py::test_better_model_wins_worse_does_not` and
   `test_not_admitted_blocks_claim`).

# 17 — Testing and Validation

This chapter documents the TRINETRA (HIMKAVACH) test harness: what it tests, how to run it, the exact
output a healthy run produces, and how the tests lock down the correctness invariants and safety posture the
project depends on. Read `_CANON.md §2` alongside this chapter — it is the arbiter for the numbers quoted
here, and this chapter agrees with it exactly.

Everything in this chapter was **run in this environment** on the numpy core. Where a claim is a run result
it is tagged `[CONFIRMED]`; where it is an inference about code behaviour not separately executed it is
tagged `[LIKELY]`; design intent not re-measured is `[HYPOTHESIS]`.

---

## 17.1 Test philosophy — what these tests are, and what they are *not*

The single most important thing to understand before reading a single assertion: **nothing in TRINETRA has
been trained, and no dataset has been downloaded** (`_CANON.md §0`). Therefore the test suite does **not**,
and cannot, measure skill — there is no accuracy, recall, false-alarm rate, lead time, or AUROC produced by
TRINETRA to measure. Any such number anywhere in the documentation is **source-reported** from someone
else's paper on their own data, never ours.

What the suite *does* test falls into two families, and the two files you run map onto them one-to-one:

1. **Correctness / golden tests** (`python run_tests.py` → the `tests/` tree, stdlib `unittest`). These pin
   down the *math and the contracts* of the pure-numpy core: that a physics formula reduces to its known
   closed-form limit, that a fusion weight vector sums to one, that a conformal interval achieves its
   nominal coverage on exchangeable data, that a bug the research phase caught stays fixed. They are
   deterministic and seed-pinned. They assert *properties and limits* ("saturated FS equals the saturated
   closed form to 12 places", "α=2 inverse-velocity recovers the true failure time"), not learned
   performance. This is the right kind of test for an untrained system: you can prove a formula is correct
   without ever having a dataset.

2. **CI honesty-and-safety gates** (`python scripts/ci_gates.py` → six fail-closed invariants). These are
   **not performance tests either** — the file says so in its own docstring. They are *tripwires* that fail
   the build if a safety or honesty rule from `_CANON.md §5` is violated in code: human approval must be
   hard-wired, Class-C novel terms must default OFF, raw video must not egress, look-ahead feature
   timestamps must be rejected, the LoRa frame must fit its byte budget, and no banned buggy-code token may
   reappear in `src/`.

The design principle (R16, `_CANON.md §5`) is that a system in a life-safety domain earns the right to make
a performance claim only after passing a spatial-CV admission gate — and since no model has been trained,
TRINETRA has not earned any such claim. The tests enforce that discipline rather than papering over it: see
the `ReportGuard` tests in §17.4, which literally refuse to emit a headline number until spatial CV and
baselines are present.

---

## 17.2 How to run — exact commands and the observed output

The numpy core needs only Python + numpy. Run from the `trinetra/` directory with the bundled interpreter.
The `PYTHONIOENCODING` line matters on Windows: `unittest` writes its progress and summary to **stderr**, and
without a UTF-8 stream the console can mangle or truncate that output.

```powershell
cd trinetra
$env:PYTHONIOENCODING = "utf-8"
& "C:\Users\Dell\.dsh\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\python\python.exe" run_tests.py
& "C:\Users\Dell\.dsh\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\python\python.exe" scripts\ci_gates.py
```

### 17.2.1 Observed output of `run_tests.py` [CONFIRMED, this environment]

The final lines of the real run were:

```
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 128 tests in 0.468s
OK
[exit code: 1]
```
> The `0.468s` is one representative run; wall-clock duration varies slightly run-to-run (e.g. 0.468–0.477 s).
> The load-bearing facts are the `Ran 128 tests` count, the `OK`, and the explained spurious `[exit code: 1]`
> (unittest writes its summary to stderr — see below), not the exact seconds.

**`Ran 128 tests ... OK`** is the pass signal. Read §17.6 before you react to the `[exit code: 1]` — it is a
harness artifact of `unittest` writing to stderr, **not** a failure. The real pass/fail signal is the final
word `OK` (all passed) or a `FAILED (...)` line (something broke).

### 17.2.2 Observed output of `scripts/ci_gates.py` [CONFIRMED, this environment]

```
  [PASS] G-advisory
  [PASS] G-classC
  [PASS] G-security
  [PASS] G-leak
  [PASS] G-iot
  [PASS] G-legacy
------------------------------------------------------------
ALL 6 CI GATES PASSED
```

This run exited 0. The six gate names are fixed by the `@gate(...)` decorators in `scripts/ci_gates.py`
(lines 39–100): `G-advisory`, `G-classC`, `G-security`, `G-leak`, `G-iot`, `G-legacy`.

Both results match `_CANON.md §2` exactly: 128 tests OK, all 6 CI gates passed.

## 17.3 Suite-by-suite inventory (correctness / golden tests)

The 128 tests live under `tests/` in topic directories, each run through stdlib `unittest` discovered by
`run_tests.py` (it inserts `src/` and the repo root onto `sys.path`, then discovers `test_*.py`). The total
of **128 tests, OK** is `[CONFIRMED]` from the runner; the per-suite descriptions below are drawn directly
from reading each file, and each line names the production module the suite guards.

### 17.3.1 Physics golden — geo (`tests/physics_golden/test_geophys.py`)
Guards `trinetra.ws1b_geophys` (FS, Iverson, Fukuzono, Caine). These encode the exact correctness invariants
the research flagged as bugs in the original report (see the module docstring and §17.7):
- **FS saturated limit** (`test_saturated_limit`): `factor_of_safety(..., sigma_s=0.0)` must equal
  `factor_of_safety_saturated(...)` to **12 decimal places** — the general unsaturated form must collapse
  exactly to the saturated closed form as suction stress → 0.
- **FS monotonicity** (`test_monotonic_in_suction`, `test_decreasing_in_pore_pressure`): more matric suction
  ⇒ more stable (higher FS); more pore-water pressure ⇒ less stable (lower FS). These are directional
  physics sanity checks.
- **Iverson slope-only-through-D1** (`test_slope_only_through_D1`): the single most load-bearing physics
  test. `transient_head(...)` with slope β must equal the slope-free core `_transient_core` evaluated at
  `D1 = D0/cos²β` to 12 places, **and must NOT equal** the buggy variant that multiplies the response by an
  extra `cos²β`. This is the regression lock for the headline hazard bug (§17.7).
- **Iverson boundary** (`test_ierfc_at_zero`: `ierfc(0)=1/√π`; `test_transient_zero_at_t0`: head is 0 at
  t=0): the special-function and initial-condition anchors.
- **Fukuzono α=2 ⇒ 1/v linear** (`test_recover_tf_alpha2`): with inverse velocity falling linearly to zero
  at t_f=100, `inverse_velocity_fit(..., alpha=2.0)` recovers t_f to 4 places with R²>0.999.
- **Caine I–D exceedance direction** (`test_exceedance_direction`): a high-intensity point exceeds the
  intensity–duration threshold and a low-intensity one does not, with a strictly larger exceedance ratio.

### 17.3.2 Physics golden — Iverson multi-pulse (`tests/physics_golden/test_iverson_multipulse.py`)
Guards `trinetra.ws1b_geophys.iverson.transient_head_multipulse` (rainfall-pulse superposition):
- Single step equals `transient_head` (12 places); a finite pulse recovers (head drops) after rain stops but
  stays positive; **superposition linearity** (two onset pulses == sum of each standalone contribution, 10
  places); intensity monotonicity. These confirm the response is a correct linear-system superposition.

### 17.3.3 Physics golden — Fukuzono prediction interval (`tests/physics_golden/test_fukuzono_ci.py`)
Guards `trinetra.ws1b_geophys.fukuzono`:
- Noiseless 1/v line recovers t_f=10 (6 places) with near-zero standard error; added noise widens the
  interval and the point estimate is bracketed by `t_failure_low < t_failure < t_failure_high`; recency
  half-life weighting leaves a clean line's estimate unchanged (stays finite/sane). This is the uncertainty
  quantification contract around the inverse-velocity failure-time prediction.

### 17.3.4 Physics golden — fire (`tests/physics_golden/test_firephys.py`)
Guards `trinetra.ws1a_firephys` and the Rule-20 flag-gating of Class-C novel terms:
- **Established (Class A)**: Heskestad flame height increases with heat-release rate; Strouhal puffing
  frequency decreases with fire diameter (the 1.5/√D law); gray-body radiance↔temperature round-trips (6
  places); Byram convection number is larger in low wind (plume-dominated) than high wind.
- **Novel ND (Class C)**: aliasing identity (no aliasing when fs>2·f_true; 7 Hz flicker at 10 Hz sampling
  aliases to 3 Hz); ND2 smoke-transmittance uncertainty **grows as smoke thickens** — the model fails toward
  "uncertain", not toward false confidence.
- **Flag-gating**: Class-C `nd3` path is **OFF by default** (`used_classC` False) and only turns on when the
  config flag is explicitly set; a windy regime lowers the fire-gate consistency score. This is the code-level
  proof of Rule 20.

### 17.3.5 Fusion — PHARAOH / FM-1 / shield (`tests/fusion/test_fusion.py`)
Guards `trinetra.ws5_fusion_rl` fusion dispatch and the safety shield (gate G4):
- PHARAOH power mean (ρ≥1) is ≥ the arithmetic mean (the anti-complacency corollary — fusion can only raise
  risk, never dilute a loud expert); PHARAOH order rises with expert disagreement and salience.
- **Dispatch default is FM-1, not Class-C**: `fuse(..., Config())` returns model `"FM-1"` with
  `used_classC` False; PHARAOH is reached only when its flag is set, and then `used_classC` is True. No
  experts ⇒ maximum uncertainty (`u_star == 1.0`).
- **Shield floor**: a single node cannot reach RED (`tilt_rate=9` alone stays below RED); **corroborated**
  tilt across 3 nodes reaches RED; FS<1 raises at least ORANGE; nothing triggered ⇒ GREEN. This is the
  monotone "shield can only raise, never lower" safety invariant.

### 17.3.6 Fusion — GMF bounded residual (`tests/fusion/test_gmf.py`)
Guards gated-mixture fusion:
- Gate weights sum to 1; with no learned head the residual is exactly 0 (output equals the base precision
  mean); **a rogue head returning ±999 is hard-clipped to ±residual_cap** (0.1); dispatch to `"GMF"` with
  PHARAOH off is Class-B not C; empty experts are safe (p=0). An **exported numpy head JSON** (the format
  `kaggle/train_fusion_head.py` writes) loads via `load_numpy_head` and stays bounded even with large export
  weights, and the fused probability stays in [0,1]. This proves a trained head can only ever nudge, never
  override, the physics base — torch-free.

### 17.3.7 Fusion — hierarchical / correlation-aware BLUE (`tests/fusion/test_hierarchical.py`)
Guards two-layer fusion and the double-counting fix:
- Independent equal-quality experts get equal weights summing to 1; a **redundant pair (ρ=0.8) does not
  double-count** — the independent expert out-weighs each redundant one and beats the naive 1/3; as ρ→1 the
  redundant pair collapses to ~one effective vote; weights stay non-negative (no hedging). Group fusion
  reduces a group to a single expert, lowers consistency on disagreement, propagates the weakest physics
  class, and the end-to-end `decide_hierarchical` flow stays advisory with Class-C transparency propagating
  to the decision. Three identical geo alarms collapse to the shared 0.9, not an amplified value.

### 17.3.8 Fusion — deep-model adapters (`tests/fusion/test_adapters.py`)
Guards `deep_expert(...)` adapters (torch-free: they convert a deep model's scalar output into an
`ExpertOutput`, no torch imported):
- Deepfake reliability is **hard-capped ≤0.4** (Rule 19 low-trust) and labelled `PhysicsClass.DATA`; a
  geo-PINN is Class-B; probabilities are clamped to [0,1]; an unknown source raises `KeyError`; a full
  `decide(...)` flow with a low-trust deepfake expert does not let it dominate (risk stays <0.8) while the
  FS<1 shield floor still applies. This proves deep outputs enter the system under the same trust and class
  discipline as everything else — even though the deep models themselves are not run here (§17.5).

### 17.3.9 Decision — single decision function (`tests/decision/test_decision.py`)
Guards `conformal_level` and `decide` (gate G3, Rule 19):
- Conformal bands are monotone at p\*=0.0476: risk 0.0→GREEN, 0.1→YELLOW, 0.3→ORANGE, 0.9→RED.
- **Shield can only raise**: GREEN fused risk + FS<1 ⇒ final ≥ ORANGE with `shield.raised` True; every
  decision is `advisory`; **no experts ⇒ fail-safe `uncertain`** (abstain and escalate, never a silent
  all-clear); high-conflict experts ⇒ `uncertain`; Class-C flagged when PHARAOH on; the decision
  serialises to a dict carrying `level`, `shield`, `advisory=True`.

### 17.3.10 Eval harness (`tests/eval/test_eval.py`)
Guards `trinetra.eval` (gate G2 — the admission machinery):
- **Spatial-block CV** never lets a block span train and test (no spatial leakage); temporal split keeps all
  training times before test times; `assert_no_time_leak` raises `LeakageError` on a future timestamp.
- **Cost-loss value score**: p\* = C_FA/(C_FA+C_miss) = 5/105; a perfect forecast scores 1.0; a constant
  climatology-equivalent forecast scores ≤0 (no credit for a non-informative predictor).
- **real-win**: an informative model wins the bootstrap comparison and a noise model does not.
- **ReportGuard** (R16 in code): refuses to emit a headline number without spatial CV, without baselines, or
  when a baseline is not beaten; only an *admitted* guard (both baselines beaten with positive CI floors)
  returns a headline. `LogisticNumpy` learns a separable problem to >0.9 accuracy (the baseline learner
  works, torch-free).

### 17.3.11 Eval — bootstrap stats (`tests/eval/test_stats.py`)
Guards `trinetra.eval._stats`: normal CDF/PPF are mutual inverses and hit known quantiles (z₀.₉₇₅≈1.95996);
the **BCa interval** brackets the true mean; the **stationary (block) bootstrap** returns an index array of
the right length and range. These underwrite the honest confidence intervals used by the admission gate — a
pure-numpy reimplementation because scipy is unavailable.

### 17.3.12 Eval — calibration (`tests/eval/test_calibration.py`)
Guards `trinetra.eval.calibration`: ECE is low on perfectly calibrated outcomes and high (>0.8) when the
model claims 0.9 but nothing happens; the reliability curve has the right bin shapes; the Brier
decomposition reconstructs the Brier score; **isotonic recalibration reduces ECE** and is monotone; Platt
scaling outputs valid probabilities. Calibration is the property that lets an advisory *level* mean what it
says — critical when a human acts on it.

### 17.3.13 Robust — conformal + drift + degradation (`tests/robust/test_robust.py`)
Guards `trinetra.ws6_robust` (gate G3/M4): conformal marginal coverage lands within ±0.03 of 1−α on
exchangeable data; regression intervals cover ≥0.85; PSI is ~0 for same distribution and flags a mean shift;
CUSUM detects a step change; **missing-modality degradation** marks an absent source unavailable and inflates
its peers' uncertainty rather than pretending the signal is still there.

### 17.3.14 Robust — advanced conformal (`tests/robust/test_conformal_advanced.py`)
Guards adaptive/Mondrian/risk-control conformal:
- **ACI under drift**: with the residual scale drifting upward, Adaptive Conformal Inference tracks ~90%
  realized coverage (between 0.82 and 0.97) where static CP would under-cover.
- **ACI sign**: a *miss* **decreases** αₜ, which **raises** the (1−α) quantile and **widens** the next
  interval — the correct self-correction (the test asserts the post-miss quantile is ≥ the baseline).
- **Mondrian** per-group quantiles differ (GLOF wider than LANDSLIDE) and an unseen group gets the most
  conservative (max) quantile. **Conformal risk control** picks a threshold that bounds the realized miss
  rate near the 0.03 target.

### 17.3.15 Interfaces — anomaly / CCTV / EO / RL-OPE / deepfake (`tests/interfaces/test_interfaces.py`)
Guards the M2/M3/M5/M9 interfaces, including the **honest-stub contract** for torch-only paths:
- Anomaly ensemble scores injected outliers higher; forecast-residual spikes at the jump sample.
- CCTV `TemporalValidator` requires persistence (3 confirming frames) and rejects a single glint; the real
  `EdgeDetector().detect(...)` **raises `MissingDependency`** (torch absent).
- EO encoder's real `.embed(...)` raises `MissingDependency`; its deterministic hashing fallback is
  reproducible and unit-norm.
- RL: the rule baseline acts correctly; the learned `OfflineRLPolicy().fit(...)` raises `MissingDependency`;
  the **positivity/OPE feasibility gate** blocks an under-explored logging policy and admits a learned policy
  only when feasible *and* better.
- Deepfake authenticity reliability never exceeds 0.4 (Rule 19); fake cues raise p_fake; the real
  `DeepfakeDetector().score(...)` raises `MissingDependency`. These `MissingDependency` assertions are how
  the suite proves "no fake results": a path that genuinely needs torch fails loudly instead of inventing a
  number.

### 17.3.16 Alerting (`tests/alert/test_alert.py`)
Guards `trinetra.ws3_alert` (M8, Rule 19): a CAP message is **refused without an approval token** and with a
bogus token (`SafetyViolation`); only after `approve(...)` returns a real token does `build_cap` emit signed
CAP XML (`<severity>Severe</severity>`, the zone id, the word `advisory`, an `hmac-sha256:` signature). GREEN
has no public CAP and cannot be approved. Severity mapping is pinned (RED→Extreme/Immediate/Observed,
ORANGE→Severe/Expected/Likely, YELLOW→Minor/Future/Possible). The operator console text says `ADVISORY` and
`human operator must review`. DTN binary-spray hands off half the copies and clears on delivery.

### 17.3.17 IoT (`tests/iot/test_iot.py`)
Guards `trinetra.ws7_iot` (M7, gate G5): the LoRa frame is ≤51 B and round-trips (seq, edge level, tilt,
rain, temp recovered within tolerance); readings sign/verify, tamper is detected, replays and stale
sequence numbers are rejected, out-of-range battery is flagged; the node-local edge screen escalates to
`LOCAL_SIREN` on two cues, `WATCH` on one, `NONE` when quiet. This is the offline-first alert path (C1)
proven to fit the radio budget.

---

## 17.4 The six CI gates (`scripts/ci_gates.py`) — honesty and safety tripwires

These are **fail-closed invariants**, not performance tests: any one failing exits non-zero and fails the
build. Each maps to a numbered rule/constraint in `_CANON.md §5`. All six passed this environment
`[CONFIRMED]` (§17.2.2).

| Gate | Violation it blocks | Pass criterion (from the code) |
|------|---------------------|--------------------------------|
| **G-advisory** | Autonomous public alert without a human (Rule 19) | `Config().require_human_approval()` is hard-wired `True`, **and** `build_cap(decision, approval_token=None, ...)` raises `SafetyViolation`. If a CAP could be built without an approval token, the gate fails. |
| **G-classC** | A novel, unvalidated Class-C term being ON by default (Rule 20) | `fusion.operator.pharaoh` is `False` **and** every `firephys.nd1..nd7` flag is `False` in the default config. |
| **G-security** | Endpoint exfiltration / raw-video egress (C6/C7) | An empty allow-list rejects *all* endpoints (`EndpointNotAllowed`), **and** `assert_no_video_egress({... "clip": raw bytes})` raises `SafetyViolation`. |
| **G-leak** | Look-ahead data leakage into a decision (G6) | `assert_no_time_leak([1,2,11], decision_time=10)` raises `LeakageError` — a feature timestamped after the decision time is rejected. |
| **G-iot** | A LoRa frame that overflows the radio budget (G5/C-offline) | `FRAME_LEN <= 51` bytes. |
| **G-legacy** | A previously-fixed buggy code pattern reappearing in `src/` | No file under `src/` contains any `BANNED_TOKENS` — currently `"EXTRA_COSBETA_ON_TRANSIENT"`, `"advisory = False"`, `"advisory=False"`. |

The last gate, **G-legacy**, is a textual regression lock: it scans every `*.py` under `src/` and fails if a
banned substring reappears. `EXTRA_COSBETA_ON_TRANSIENT` is the sentinel for the Iverson transient bug
(§17.7); `advisory=False` would be an attempt to turn off the advisory posture. This is a cheap, blunt, and
effective second line of defence behind the numeric golden tests.

---

## 17.5 Coverage — what is and is not exercised here, and why

**Covered and run here (numpy core) [CONFIRMED]:** all 128 unit/golden/contract tests above, plus the 6 CI
gates. That is the complete deterministic/numerical core: geo and fire physics, all fusion operators (FM-1,
GMF, hierarchical/BLUE, PHARAOH), the safety shield, the single decision function, conformal (static, ACI,
Mondrian, CRC), calibration and recalibration, the bootstrap stats, the eval admission harness, the LoRa
codec, signing/replay, the CAP builder, and the deep→expert adapters (torch-free). The sandbox provides
**numpy, pandas, lxml only** — no torch/scipy/sklearn/yaml (`_CANON.md §2`) — which is exactly why the stats,
logistic baseline, and recalibrators are reimplemented in pure numpy and *are* tested.

**Not run here, and honestly marked so:**

- **The PyTorch `deep/` layer** (EO foundation encoder, CCTV fire CNN, deepfake net, deep anomaly heads,
  offline-RL training — the 6 trainable models). **No test module under `tests/` exercises these models**
  (confirmed by enumerating the test tree). `_CANON.md §2` records them as **`py_compile` clean, not run on
  a GPU**. I did **not** independently re-run `py_compile` in this task, so I carry that as a
  **[CONFIRMED by _CANON]** fact rather than my own measurement — mark these models **UNTESTED-here
  (no torch in sandbox)**. What *is* tested here is the *boundary* around them: the interface tests
  (§17.3.15) assert that each torch-only entry point raises `MissingDependency` instead of fabricating a
  result, and the adapter tests (§17.3.8) assert their *outputs* would enter fusion under the right class and
  trust caps.
- **GPU training / Kaggle scripts**: multi-GPU (T4×2) ready but **not executed on a GPU** in this
  environment (`_CANON.md §2`). The *exported-head* consumption path, however, *is* tested torch-free via
  `load_numpy_head` (§17.3.6), so the handoff from a (hypothetically) trained head back into the numpy core
  is validated even though the training itself is not.

The honest summary: the parts that can be proven correct without data or a GPU are proven; the parts that
genuinely need torch/GPU are compile-checked only and are tested *at their boundary* for fail-loud behaviour.

---

## 17.6 Expected outputs and reading a real pass vs the spurious exit code

A future runner should expect **exactly**:
- `run_tests.py` → a stream of `... ok` lines on stderr, then `Ran 128 tests in <~0.5s>` and a final `OK`.
- `scripts/ci_gates.py` → `[PASS]` for each of `G-advisory, G-classC, G-security, G-leak, G-iot, G-legacy`,
  then `ALL 6 CI GATES PASSED` (exit 0).

**The exit-code trap.** `run_tests.py` returns `0` only when `result.wasSuccessful()` (line 23), but
`unittest.TextTestRunner` writes its entire report — including `OK` — to **stderr**. Under this harness a
command whose stderr is non-empty can surface a trailing **`[exit code: 1]`** marker even on a clean,
all-passing run; that is what happened here (§17.2.1). **Do not read that marker as a failure.** The
authoritative signals, in order:

1. The final line is `OK` and the count line reads `Ran 128 tests` → **real pass**, regardless of the
   `[exit code: 1]` marker.
2. The final line is `FAILED (failures=N, errors=M)`, or the count differs from 128 → **real failure**;
   scroll up for the `FAIL:`/`ERROR:` tracebacks.
3. For the gates, trust the literal `ALL 6 CI GATES PASSED` line and exit 0; any `[FAIL] <gate>` line or
   `CI GATES FAILED: n/6` is a genuine safety-gate failure that must block the build.

If you see `OK` but a count other than 128, something was added or skipped — reconcile it against
`_CANON.md §2` before trusting it.

---

## 17.7 How the tests lock the hazard-correctness bug fixes (cross-ref chapter 13)

Chapter 13 (robustness, bugs, fixes) documents the correctness defects the research phase caught. The two
load-bearing ones are **double-locked** so they cannot silently regress:

- **Iverson transient slope factor.** The original report applied an *extra* `cos²β` factor to the transient
  pressure-head response. The corrected physics puts slope in **only** through the diffusivity
  `D1 = D0/cos²β`. Two independent locks:
  1. **Numeric golden** `test_slope_only_through_D1` (§17.3.1): asserts `transient_head(...)` equals the
     slope-free core at `D1` to 12 places **and** `assertNotAlmostEqual` against the buggy
     `core·cos²β` variant. A reintroduced extra factor fails this test immediately.
  2. **Textual gate** `G-legacy` (§17.4): the banned token `EXTRA_COSBETA_ON_TRANSIENT` cannot appear in
     `src/`, so even a commented-out or flagged re-introduction trips the CI gate.
- **Advisory-only posture.** `decide` always sets `advisory=True`, the shield can only *raise* a level, no
  experts fail-safes to `uncertain`, and CAP refuses to build without a human approval token. These are
  held by `test_decision.py` + `test_alert.py` (§17.3.9, §17.3.16) **and** by `G-advisory` plus the banned
  `advisory=False` token in `G-legacy`. To regress the safety posture you would have to defeat both a unit
  test and a CI gate.

The pattern — a precise numeric property test **plus** a blunt textual tripwire — is deliberate: the golden
test proves the current code is correct, the gate makes the specific wrong pattern un-mergeable. When you
read a before/after in chapter 13, the "after" is the state these tests pin.

---

## 17.8 How to add a new test when you extend the code (cross-ref chapter 16)

Chapter 16 (code guide) is the map of which module lives where; this section is the mechanics of keeping it
tested. The harness is intentionally dependency-free, so adding a test is cheap:

1. **Pick the directory** under `tests/` matching the code's workstream (`physics_golden/`, `fusion/`,
   `decision/`, `eval/`, `robust/`, `interfaces/`, `alert/`, `iot/`). Create a `test_*.py` — the filename
   must match the `test_*.py` glob or `run_tests.py` will not discover it. Each dir already has an
   `__init__.py`; keep that convention for new subdirs.
2. **Use stdlib `unittest` only** — subclass `unittest.TestCase`, no `pytest`, no `hypothesis` (not
   installed here). Import from `trinetra....`; `run_tests.py` has already put `src/` on `sys.path`.
3. **Assert a property, limit, or contract — never a trained-performance number.** Follow the house style:
   a known closed-form limit (FS saturated), a mathematical identity (superposition linearity), a monotone
   direction (more suction ⇒ higher FS), a bound (residual clipped to ±cap), a sign (ACI widens after a
   miss), or a fail-loud contract (`MissingDependency`, `SafetyViolation`, `LeakageError`). Seed every RNG
   (`np.random.default_rng(0)`) so the test is deterministic.
4. **If you fix a bug, add BOTH locks** (§17.7): a numeric golden test that would have caught it, and — if
   the bug has a recognisable code signature — a new entry in `BANNED_TOKENS` in `scripts/ci_gates.py` so
   `G-legacy` blocks its return. If you add a new safety rule, add a new `@gate("G-...")` function; the
   gate count in the final line is computed from `len(CHECKS)`, so the summary updates itself.
5. **If you add a torch-only path**, do **not** add a test that needs torch. Instead test the *stub
   contract* (the real call raises `MissingDependency`) and, if it produces fusion input, test its numpy
   adapter the way `test_adapters.py` does.
6. **Run both commands** (§17.2) and confirm the count rose and the final line is still `OK` with all 6
   gates passing. Then update `_CANON.md §2` and `CODE_INVENTORY.md` so the documented test count stays the
   single source of truth — a count that disagrees with `_CANON` is itself a documentation bug (per the
   honesty contract in chapter 00).

The guiding rule for extensions is the same as for the whole suite: you may test that the math is correct and
the safety rails hold; you may **not** add a test that asserts a skill number, because TRINETRA has not been
trained and has no skill to assert.

# 18 — Reproduce From Scratch: The Zero-to-Results Runbook

This is the strictly ordered runbook that takes a new engineer from an empty machine to the **only results
TRINETRA (HIMKAVACH) can actually produce today**: the numpy core passing **128 unit tests + 6 CI gates**
and an **end-to-end advisory decision** from `demo.py`. Every command below is real and copy-pasteable.

Read §18.0 before running anything — it tells you exactly what is reproducible and what is not.

---

## 18.0 What this runbook can and cannot give you (read first)

This project has two layers (`_CANON.md §0`, `00_README_START_HERE.md §0.1`), and this runbook treats them
very differently:

- **The numpy core** (physics gates, fusion math, conformal, cost-loss, baselines, safety shield, decision
  function, CAP builder) is **pure numpy + stdlib** and is **fully reproducible on this machine right now**.
  Everything in STEPS 1–3 below was executed in this environment and the checkpoints are the **real
  observed output** `[CONFIRMED]`.
- **The deep / GPU / Kaggle layer** (PyTorch `deep/` models + `kaggle/` training scripts) is
  **`py_compile`-clean only and was never run on a GPU here** — there is no torch/CUDA/GPU and no dataset in
  this sandbox (`_CANON.md §2`: available libraries are numpy, pandas, lxml only). Every GPU/training/dataset
  step in STEPS 4–5 is therefore marked **UNTESTED**; its commands are "what a future user *would* run",
  taken verbatim from each script's real `argparse`, and all runtimes are planning estimates `[EST]`.

> **No TRINETRA model has been trained and no dataset has been downloaded** (`_CANON.md §0`). Nothing in this
> runbook produces a measured accuracy, skill, latency, recall, false-alarm, or cost number for TRINETRA. The
> `demo.py` hindcast even prints `admitted=False` on its own synthetic data — that is the honesty gate working,
> not a result. See the honesty box in §18.9.

Honesty labels follow `_CANON.md §1`: `[CONFIRMED]`, `[LIKELY]`, `[HYPOTHESIS]`, `[INFEASIBLE]`, plus `[EST]`
for a planning estimate and **UNTESTED** for anything not executed in this environment.

## 18.5 STEP 4 — Kaggle GPU training path  **(UNTESTED here — no torch/GPU/datasets)**

> **UNTESTED.** None of the commands in this step were executed in this environment: there is no
> torch/CUDA/GPU and no dataset here (`_CANON.md §2`). The flags below are read **verbatim from each script's
> real `argparse`**; the runtimes are planning estimates `[EST]`. Do not read any of this as "observed".
> **Before scheduling any of it, re-confirm your live Kaggle quota first** — see **chapter 11**
> (`11_training_compute_kaggle.md`), which is the operational contract for the ~25.5 usable GPU-h/week budget.

### 18.5.1 Set up the Kaggle session (`trinetra/kaggle/README.md §1`)
1. New Notebook/Script → **Settings → Accelerator = GPU T4 ×2** (or P100), **Internet = On** (first run only,
   so pip can resolve `requirements-deep.txt`).
2. Add this repo as a **Kaggle Dataset** (or from GitHub) so `src/` is importable.
3. Attach your datasets; loaders default to `/kaggle/input/<slug>` (`deep.datamodules.KagglePaths`).

Install the DEEP tier (first run only):
```bash
pip install -r requirements-deep.txt
```

### 18.5.2 Per-script training commands — REAL flags from each `argparse`

All training scripts share the GPU-scaling flags (from `train.py` `TrainConfig` + `kaggle/README.md §2b/§3`):
`--batch N` is the **PER-GPU** batch (effective batch = `N × n_gpus`, LR scaled linearly, Goyal 2017), and
`--parallel {auto,dp,none}` (`auto` = DataParallel when `n_gpus()>1`; `dp` forces it; `none` forces
single-GPU). On startup each script prints a banner like
`[trinetra] GPUs visible=2 | DataParallel=True | effective_batch=128 lr=6.00e-04`.

**Geo-PINN** — `kaggle/train_geo_pinn.py` (flags: `--data` (required), `--out` default `/kaggle/working`,
`--epochs` default **30**, `--D0` default **2e-4**, `--beta_deg` default **35.0**, `--batch` default **64**,
`--parallel` default **auto**). Slope enters **only** via `D1 = diffusivity_D1(D0, beta_deg)` — the
`D1 = D0/cos²β` bug-guard (`_CANON.md §4`).
```bash
python kaggle/train_geo_pinn.py --data /kaggle/input/trinetra-geo/geo.npz --out /kaggle/working
# optional: --epochs 30 --D0 2e-4 --beta_deg 35.0 --batch 64 --parallel auto
```
> Geo-PINN caveat (`kaggle/README.md §2b`, chapter 11 §11.4.4): its physics loss uses `autograd.grad` inside
> the forward; DataParallel *usually* works but on a thread/autograd error rerun with **`--parallel none`**
> or use the DDP launcher.

**Classifier (fire | eo | deepfake)** — `kaggle/train_classifier.py` (flags: `--model` (required, choices
`fire,eo,deepfake`), `--data` (required), `--out` default `/kaggle/working`, `--epochs` default **20**,
`--batch` default **64**, `--parallel` default **auto**).
```bash
python kaggle/train_classifier.py --model fire     --data /kaggle/input/trinetra-fire/fire.npz   --out /kaggle/working
python kaggle/train_classifier.py --model eo       --data /kaggle/input/trinetra-eo/eo.npz       --out /kaggle/working
python kaggle/train_classifier.py --model deepfake --data /kaggle/input/trinetra-media/media.npz --out /kaggle/working
```

**Deep anomaly** — `kaggle/train_anomaly.py` (flags: `--data` (required), `--out` default `/kaggle/working`,
`--epochs` default **25**, `--batch` default **64**, `--parallel` default **auto**). Trains on **NORMAL
windows only** (`y==0`); events become out-of-distribution and score high.
```bash
python kaggle/train_anomaly.py --data /kaggle/input/trinetra-telemetry/tele.npz --out /kaggle/working
```

**Offline-RL** — `kaggle/train_offline_rl.py` (flags: `--data` (required), `--out` default `/kaggle/working`,
`--epochs` default **50**, `--gamma` default **0.0**, `--batch` default **256**). **Deliberately 1 GPU**
(`scale_batch_by_gpus=False`): the Q-net is tiny, so scatter/gather would cost more than it saves; it uses a
large batch instead. Prints `offline-RL uses 1 GPU (tiny net)`.
```bash
python kaggle/train_offline_rl.py --data /kaggle/input/trinetra-rl-logs/logs.npz --out /kaggle/working
# optional: --epochs 50 --gamma 0.0 --batch 256
```

**Fusion head (GMF)** — `kaggle/train_fusion_head.py` (flags: `--data` (required; `.npz` with keys
`base,dispersion,salience,y`), `--out` default `/kaggle/working`, `--cap` default **0.1**, `--epochs`
default **300**). Learns the bounded residual head, then **exports it to numpy** and asserts torch/numpy
parity (`abs(t_val-n_val) < 1e-5`) before writing.
```bash
python kaggle/train_fusion_head.py --data /kaggle/working/fusion_cache.npz --out /kaggle/working
```

### 18.5.3 Checkpoint / resume  (UNTESTED; chapter 11 §11.5)
- Checkpoint to `/kaggle/working` **every ≤30 min AND before the ~11 h wall** (one hour margin before the
  ~12 h session kill); **resume on restart**. A run that misses the wall loses all its spent quota.
- Resume anchors written per fold/model: `geo_pinn_fold{fold}.pt`, `{model}_fold{fold}.pt`,
  `anomaly_fold{fold}.pt`, `offline_rl.pt`, `gmf_head.pt`.
- Prefer **commit / batch runs** over interactive (idle timeout wastes quota).

### 18.5.4 The admission-gate report JSON — the only thing that may claim skill (UNTESTED)
Each script with labels runs `admit_model(...)` on spatial-CV and writes a `*_report.json` honesty report
(`train_geo_pinn.py`, `train_classifier.py`, `train_anomaly.py` → `admit_model`; `train_offline_rl.py` →
`ope_admission` → `offline_rl_report.json`). **Deploy a model ONLY if `"admitted": true`** (Rule 16, enforced
in `train.py`); offline-RL deploys the learned policy only if `deploy_learned` is true (else it keeps the
rule baseline — Rule 19 fail-safe). Copy to the edge runtime: `*.pt` checkpoints, `*_report.json`, and
`gmf_head_numpy.json` (the numpy-serialized GMF head so the torch-free offline gateway can run it).
These reports are **not produced in this environment** — UNTESTED.

## 3. MUST-READ TOP 30 (in reading order)
Reading order runs foundational-method → applied-system. `(REF-id, file, read_depth)` are shown; **classics have no arXiv/DOI in the ledger** and are sourced to `analysis/08_equations_register.md`.

1. **2608.12422** (REF-PHY-010, 19a, ABS) -- Which Site, and When: A Free-Satellite-Data Test of Himalayan Glacial Lake Bursts, Landslides, and Ice Floods
   - Why: Spatial-CV leakage verdict (CANON-grounded). Naive terrain ROC-AUC ~0.90 collapses to 0.76/0.71/0.54 under matched spatial-block CV; a simple GB/3-rule tree matches deep nets. CORRECTION: this is the correct id -- NOT 2608.22293.
2. **2610.08227** (REF-EVAL-027, 19b, FT-PARTIAL) -- How Many Independent Samples Does a Satellite Image Contain?
   - Why: Effective-sample-size theorem: a satellite tile holds far fewer independent samples than pixels -> why random CV over-states skill. Read right after 2608.12422.
3. **2101.05397** (REF-PHY-099, 19a, ABS) -- Should Ensemble Members Be Calibrated?
   - Why: "Should Ensemble Members Be Calibrated?" -- the calibrated-members argument that underpins the fusion/calibration stack (ledger axis WS1b, topically calibration).
4. **2303.12783** (REF-FUS-020, 19b, ABS) -- Conformal Prediction for Time Series with Modern Hopfield Networks (HopCPT)
   - Why: HopCPT: conformal prediction for time series via modern Hopfield nets -- the time-series conformal method behind the alarm interval guarantee.
5. **2106.08909** (REF-RL-002, 19d, ABS) -- Offline RL Without Off-Policy Evaluation (One-Step)
   - Why: One-step offline RL beats iterative actor-critic on much of D4RL and avoids high-variance repeated OPE -- the first RL baseline to benchmark.
6. **2110.14000** (REF-RL-005, 19d, ABS) -- Towards Hyperparameter-free Policy Selection for Offline Reinforcement Learning
   - Why: BVFT: hyperparameter-free offline policy SELECTION -- how to pick the alarm policy without live trials.
7. **2311.18206** (REF-RL-006, 19d, ABS) -- SCOPE-RL: A Python Library for Offline Reinforcement Learning and Off-Policy Evaluation
   - Why: SCOPE-RL: the OPE/offline-RL evaluation library that frames the honest OPE gate (ties BVFT).
8. **2604.24404** (REF-RL-022, 19d, FT-PARTIAL) -- Open-Source 5G Public Warning System Spoofing Testbed
   - Why: 5G public-warning broadcasts are unauthenticated/spoofable (open-source testbed) -> must sign CAP + authenticated mesh. (Ledger axis A6, but this is an alerting/security paper.)
9. **2003.01279** (REF-ROB-130, 19d, ABS) -- Disrupting Deepfakes: Adversarial Attacks Against Facial Manipulation Systems
   - Why: Disrupting Deepfakes: adversarial attacks on facial manipulation -- defensive-only framing for WS2 (ledger axis WS6/robustness).
10. **2007.05848** (REF-EVAL-025, 19b, FT-PARTIAL) -- Fighting Disaster Misinformation in Latin America (#Verificado19S Mexico 2017 Earthquake)
   - Why: Crisis-informatics misinformation: social/deepfake signals are low-trust and must be corroborated (Rule 19).
11. **2603.17319** (REF-FUS-031, 19b, FT-PARTIAL) -- PIER: Physics-Informed Offline RL with Decoupled Post-hoc Shield
   - Why: PIER physics-informed offline RL (IQL) + decoupled shield; optimise the TAIL not the mean -- template for the safe-RL shield.
12. **2610.04828** (REF-PINN-006, 19a, FT-PARTIAL) -- Label-Free PINN Strength-Reduction Factor-of-Safety at Scale
   - Why: Label-free PINN slope FoS within 2-3% of FEM -> use FoS as a GATE not a probability (PINN feasibility evidence).
13. **2512.23964** (REF-PHY-007, 19a, ABS) -- DUALFloodGNN: Physics-informed Graph Neural Network for Operational Flood Modeling
   - Why: DUALFloodGNN: fast physics-informed GNN flood hydrodynamics -- SOTA, open-source surrogate for the flood/runout gate.
14. **2505.08553** (REF-PHY-006, 19a, ABS) -- Towards Digital Twin in Flood Forecasting with Data Assimilation of Satellite EO (Alzette)
   - Why: Particle-filter data-assimilation of Sentinel-1 into LISFLOOD-FP (digital-twin flood) -- closest published analogue to satellite-into-physics fusion + honest residual-uncertainty reporting.
15. **2211.10338** (REF-DATA-006, 19c, ABS) -- Deep learning based landslide density estimation on SAR data for rapid response
   - Why: SAR-only landslide density (0.814 AUC) with the honest sub-pixel limit (~45% of slides < 10 m S1 pixel) -- a must-cite baseline + resolution caveat.
16. **2512.12844** (REF-FUS-006, 19b, ABS) -- Selective Conformal Risk Control (SCRC)
   - Why: Selective Conformal Risk Control: abstain on low-confidence inputs, calibrate on the selected subset -- the principled fix for the conformal over-claim.
17. **2512.01384** (REF-FUS-007, 19b, ABS) -- CLAPS: Aleatoric-Epistemic Scaling via Last-Layer Laplace for Conformal Regression
   - Why: CLAPS: conformal intervals widen where training support is thin (aleatoric+epistemic) -- honest widening in the data-sparse Himalayan tail.
18. **2603.10392** (REF-FUS-005, 19b, ABS) -- Safe Probabilistic Planning for Human-Robot Interaction using Conformal Risk Control
   - Why: CBF + conformal risk control = formal, context-adaptive safety margins -- upgrades the ad-hoc hard-threshold shield.
19. **2104.11422** (REF-EVAL-001, 19b, ABS) -- Socio-meteorology: flood prediction social preparedness and cry wolf effects
   - Why: Socio-meteorology cry-wolf: false alarms erode trust/compliance, worse in low-frequency-disaster regions -- the social half of the threshold design.
20. **2509.11789** (REF-EVAL-005, 19b, ABS) -- Watch Your Step: Cost-Sensitive Accelerometer Fall Detection in Real-World Streaming
   - Why: Cost-sensitive streaming fall-detection: tune the DECISION THRESHOLD by asymmetric miss>>FA cost; Recall 1.0 need not kill precision -- validates the p*=0.0476 methodology.
21. **2503.14621** (REF-EVAL-008, 19b, ABS) -- Reducing False Ventricular Tachycardia Alarms in ICU Settings: A Machine Learning Approach
   - Why: Learned true/false-alarm discriminator (ROC-AUC>0.96) that suppresses FAs without missing events -- supports a two-stage alarm-verification layer.
22. **2601.05921** (note-only -- NOT a ledger row; grounds equations-register E-07, FT (local note)) -- Decision-value / cost-loss Value Score for EWS verification (QUOTA#15)
   - Why: Cost-loss Value Score: evaluate EWS across a RANGE of C/L ratios, not a single AUC -- the primary evaluation metric (equations register E-07).
23. **2603.15945** (REF-ALERT-008, 19d, ABS) -- Evaluating Opportunistic Routing Protocols in a Disaster Scenario (DTN Earthquake Case Study)
   - Why: DTN opportunistic routing in a real disaster: Spray-and-Wait beats Epidemic -- which store-carry-forward protocol for backhaul-down alerting.
24. **2608.11142** (REF-DATA-037, 19c, FT-PARTIAL) -- SAR2Agri: Learning SAR Intensity Representations for Agricultural Monitoring
   - Why: SAR2Agri: SSL on SAR-intensity only (+15.3 pt IoU vs optical) -- the SAR-first self-supervised encoder recipe for data-poor regions.
25. **2509.17942** (REF-DATA-005, 19c, ABS) -- StefaLand: An Efficient Geoscience Foundation Model Improving Dynamic Land-Surface Predictions
   - Why: StefaLand geoscience foundation model: strong SPATIAL generalization on landslide/soil-moisture, academic-compute trainable -- the most on-point external FM/backbone candidate.
26. **2306.00001** (REF-CCTV-001, 19c, ABS) -- TinyissimoYOLO: Quantized Low-Memory TinyML Object Detection for Low-Power Microcontrollers
   - Why: TinyissimoYOLO: real-time INT8 detection at 196 uJ/inference on an MCU -- hard evidence of what a <=Rs.2000 edge node can actually run (vs GPU benchmarks).
27. **2610.06453** (REF-CCTV-021, 19c, FT-PARTIAL) -- NCL: Normal-Subspace Constrained Learning for Foundation-Model Anomaly Detection
   - Why: NCL: foundation models reconstruct anomalies too well -> reconstruction-error anomaly scores collapse -- a warning for the anomaly/drift layer.

28. **Iverson (2000), Water Resources Research** (classic; no arXiv/DOI in ledger) — Transient pressure-head infiltration; slope enters ONLY via D1=D0/cos^2(delta) (the Bug #3 guard). Equations register GH-02/E-02.
29. **Fukuzono (1985) / Voight (1988)** (classic; no arXiv/DOI in ledger) — Inverse-velocity failure-time: 1/v = A(alpha-1)(t_f - t), alpha~2 -> 1/v linear. Equations register E-04/GH (time-to-failure).
30. **Heskestad (1983)** (classic; no arXiv/DOI in ledger) — Mean flame height L = 0.235 Q^(2/5) - 1.02 D and plume centerline -- fire-physics anchor. Equations register EF-01/EF-03.

## 6. Note on 2608.22293 (why the correction matters)
`_CANON.md` §6 corrects an earlier draft that cited **2608.22293** for the spatial-CV verdict and states it is "NOT in the source artifacts". In the live ledger, 2608.22293 **is** present (REF-ALERT-068, ABS): "Spatial Anatomy of Urban Wildfire Vulnerability (GeoAI Palisades)" — a *different* topic. So the operative rule holds (do **not** cite 2608.22293 for spatial-CV; use **2608.12422**), but the parenthetical "not in the source artifacts" is inaccurate for the current file. Flagged for the consistency gate.

# 20 — Glossary and Notation

> **Scope and honesty.** Every entry below is defined **as the term is used in TRINETRA (HIMKAVACH)**,
> harvested from the already-written chapters, `_CANON.md`, and the code they cite. Units are the project's
> units. Where an expansion or meaning could not be sourced from a chapter / `_CANON` / code it is marked
> **(definition not established in sources)**; an expansion that is inferred rather than stated is tagged
> `[LIKELY]`. Source-reported numbers are *other papers' results on their own data* and never TRINETRA
> measurements (`_CANON.md §1`, Rule 16). The single operating point appears two ways: **`p*` (used by
> `_CANON.md §4` and the code) ≡ `τ*` (the symbol the HLD uses)** — the same cost-loss alarm threshold
> ≈ 0.0476; see the SYMBOLS table.
>
> "Chapter where it matters" uses the user doc-frame numbering (00–25). The three workstream numbering
> schemes are reconciled in `_CANON.md §3` and in the DOMAIN TERMS entry "workstream (WS) schemes".

---

## 1. Abbreviations and Acronyms (alphabetical)

| Abbreviation | Expansion | Meaning in TRINETRA | Chapter |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ABS** `[ABS]` | Abstract-only read | Read-depth / honesty label: a source read at abstract level only; may **never** be stated as established fact (`_CANON.md §1,§7`). | 05, 08, 10, 12, 19 |
| **ACI** | Adaptive Conformal Inference | Online conformal method (Gibbs & Candès 2021) that keeps **long-run** coverage under drift by nudging the working miss-rate `α_t`; the `AdaptiveConformal` class in `ws6_robust/conformal.py`. | 12 |
| **AMP** | Automatic Mixed Precision | PyTorch fp16/bf16 training speedup (`torch.cuda.amp.autocast` + `GradScaler`), on by default in `deep/train.py`; a large speedup on Turing T4 GPUs. | 05a, 11 |
| **APNs** | Apple Push Notification service | OS push service cited as requiring the internet — one reason "offline alerting by IP" is `[INFEASIBLE]`. | 08 |
| **ASN** | Autonomous System Number | Network-topology identifier used to show an IP marks *where you attach*, not where you stand (IP-verdict argument). | 08 |
| **AUC / ROC-AUC** | (Receiver-Operating-Characteristic) Area Under the Curve | Discrimination metric; in this project treated as **base-rate-dependent and not comparable across hazards**, which is why the cost-aware Value Score is primary. Source-reported collapse 0.90→0.76/0.71/0.54 under spatial-CV. | 12 |
| **BCa** | Bias-corrected and accelerated (bootstrap interval) | The default confidence-interval method in the `real_win` admission test (`eval/_stats.bca_interval`); coverage error O(1/n) vs O(1/√n) for percentile. | 12 |
| **BLE** | Bluetooth Low Energy | Candidate last-100 m alert transport (BlueFlood-style flood) to unmodified phones; density/interference-fragile, hardware-unverified `[LIKELY]`. | 08 |
| **BLUE / GLS** | Best Linear Unbiased Estimator / Generalised Least Squares | Correlation-aware minimum-variance fusion weights (Aitken/GLS) so redundant sensors don't double-count; `ws5_fusion_rl/correlation.py`. Negative "hedging" weights are clipped (safety deviation). | 02, 05b |
| **BOM** | Bill of Materials | Per-node hardware cost list; all ₹ figures are `[EST]` (suppliers 403'd); Node A ≈ ₹1,930, Node B ≈ ₹1,980; ≤₹2000 gate (C2) not yet live-enforceable. | 02 (C2), 03, 13 |
| **Brier** | Brier score | Mean squared error of probabilistic forecasts, `mean((p−y)²)`, with Murphy decomposition into reliability − resolution + uncertainty; `eval/calibration.py`. | 12 |
| **BVFT** | Batch Value-Function Tournament | Offline policy-**selection** method (arXiv 2110.14000) in the research-grade RL valuation plan; spec/plan only, not measured. | 10 |
| **CAP** | Common Alerting Protocol | Signed XML alert format (CAP 1.2) carrying origin/area/severity/expiry/nonce; `ws3_alert/cap.py` `build_cap` **refuses** to emit without an `APPROVED:` operator token (Rule 19) and HMAC-SHA256-signs the payload. | 02, 08 |
| **CGNAT** | Carrier-Grade NAT | One public IPv4 shared across thousands of mobile subscribers; a core reason you cannot push to a specific handset "by IP" — the public IP identifies the carrier NAT, not a person. | 08 |
| **CI** | Continuous Integration (also: Confidence Interval) | (1) The 6 fail-closed `scripts/ci_gates.py` honesty/safety gates — **ALL 6 CI GATES PASSED** `[CONFIRMED]`. (2) In Fukuzono / real-win contexts, a bootstrap/delta-method confidence interval. Both senses occur; disambiguate by context. | 02, 05b, 12 |
| **CNN** | Convolutional Neural Network | Backbone of the CCTV FireSmokeNet detector (CNN→GRU). | 05, 09 |
| **CP** | Conformal Prediction | Umbrella for the split-CP / WCPS / ACI / Mondrian / CRC calibration toolkit; `ws6_robust/conformal.py`. | 12 |
| **CQL** | Conservative Q-Learning | The implemented offline-RL learner (Model 6, Kumar et al. 2006.04779); conservative penalty lower-bounds OOD-action value; `γ=0` by default ⇒ one-step contextual bandit. `py_compile`-clean, never GPU-trained — UNTESTED on GPU. | 10 |
| **CRC** | Conformal Risk Control | RCPS-style threshold (Angelopoulos et al. 2022) that bounds the **miss-rate** with finite-sample slack `B/(n+1)`; `conformal_risk_threshold`. | 12 |
| **CUSUM** | Cumulative Sum (control chart) | Sequential change-point detector in `ws6_robust/drift_monitor.py` (`cusum_update`, slack `k=0.5`, threshold `h=5.0`); drift voids the conformal bound. | 12, 13, 15 |
| **CV** (spatial-CV / spatial-block CV) | Cross-Validation | Mandatory **spatial-block** CV (whole zones/tiles withheld) — random CV overstates skill. The only admissible split for a headline number. | 12 |
| **CVaR** | Conditional Value-at-Risk | Worst-case tail metric (e.g. CVaR@5%) reported in the SCOPE-RL RL risk-evaluation plan — the correct posture when the tail is a mass-casualty event. Plan only. | 10 |
| **C-DOT** | Centre for Development of Telematics (India) | Operator (with NDMA) of India's SACHET CAP alerting path; TRINETRA can only **request** an official alert from them. | 08 |
| **DHCP** | Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol | Dynamically reassigns private addresses, so there is no stable per-device IP to target — part of the IP-alerting `[INFEASIBLE]` argument. | 08 |
| **DL** | Deep Learning | Shorthand in the eval chapter; source-reported finding: five DL models do **not** decisively beat a gradient-boosted baseline under spatial-CV. | 12, 13 |
| **DDP** | DistributedDataParallel (PyTorch) | Max-throughput multi-GPU training path (`deep/ddp.py`, one process/GPU, NCCL all-reduce, rank-0 save); used from a plain `.py` script. | 11, 16 |
| **DataParallel** | `nn.DataParallel` (PyTorch) | Single-process multi-GPU scatter/gather; the default `--parallel` mode for most models. Source of three fixed multi-GPU bugs (leaf-tensor, drop_last, None-label). RL deliberately avoids it (model too small). | 10, 11, 13 |
| **DTN** | Delay-Tolerant Networking | Store-carry-forward alert dissemination (Tier-0 backstop); `ws3_alert/dtn.py` `DTNQueue` uses **binary Spray-and-Wait**; realises feature F-10, mitigates FM-11. | 02, 08 |
| **ECE** | Expected Calibration Error | Bin-weighted mean gap between confidence and accuracy, `Σ (n_bin/N)·|acc−conf|`; `eval/calibration.py`. | 12 |
| **EO** | Earth Observation | Free satellite imagery (ESA/NASA) ingested via a **frozen EO foundation model** encoder; EO is a Tier-1/2 (never Tier-0) input. | 02, 05 |
| **EO-FM** | Earth-Observation Foundation Model | The frozen multispectral/SAR encoder (Prithvi/SatMAE/Clay-class, named in code docstrings, no repo arXiv) whose embeddings feed the EO downstream head. | 02, 05 |
| **ESS** | Effective Sample Size | OPE honesty guardrail `(Σw)²/Σw²`; `ope_feasible` refuses if ESS < 10% of N (weights too concentrated). Also appears as the spatial `N_eff` theorem (distinct use). | 10, 12 |
| **EST** `[EST]` | Estimated | Honesty label for planning-level figures not live-verified (all BOM ₹ costs, `_CANON.md §8`). | 03, 13 |
| **EVT** | Extreme-Value Theory | Tail prior proposed where no calibrated solver exists (ungauged Himalaya) and for extreme-transition lag. | 13 |
| **EWS** | Early-Warning System | The high-recall supervised ensemble role (XGBoost EWS + per-hazard heads). | 02 |
| **FA / C_FA** | False Alarm / False-Alarm cost | Cost of alarming on a non-event; `C_FA = 5` in the canonical cost table. | 10, 12 |
| **FCM** | Firebase Cloud Messaging | Android OS push service; cited (with APNs) as internet-dependent — defeats "offline by IP". | 08 |
| **FM-1 … FM-6** | Fusion Model 1…6 | The six derived meta-fusion options: FM-1 precision-weighted mean (**Class-A default/fallback**), evidential, conformal-stacked, covariance-intersection, physics-gated MoE, RL-tuned. Class-B/C ones are flag-gated with FM-1 fallback. | 02, 05, 05b |
| **FM-01 … FM-40** | Failure Mode 01…40 | The failure-mode catalogue IDs (`analysis/05`); e.g. FM-11 backhaul-down, FM-05 shield unrealizability, FM-20 proximity-bias overconfidence. **Distinct** from the FM-1..6 fusion models above. | 08, 13 |
| **FEM** | Finite-Element Method | 2-D/FEM slope solver, **rejected** for the edge path (needs mesh/geometry; not offline-cheap). | 05b |
| **fps** | frames per second | Unit flagged in Bug #14: "57 fps / <1 s on-edge" was an L40S server-GPU number mis-attributed to a Jetson. | 13 |
| **FQE** | Fitted Q-Evaluation | Named OPE method to **rank** policies offline (iterate only if OPE feasible); plan only. | 10 |
| **FS / FoS** | Factor of Safety | Infinite-slope landslide stability ratio; FS<1 ⇒ unstable and forces a shield floor (ORANGE). Hard deterministic gate, `ws1b_geophys/fs.py`. (Also the SYMBOLS table.) | 02, 05, 05b, 13 |
| **FT / FT-PARTIAL / FT-REF** | Full-Text / partial / reference-only read-depth | Source read-depth labels (`_CANON.md §7`): full text, partially read, or seen only as a reference. | 19 (defined), used throughout |
| **GBDT / GB** | Gradient-Boosted Decision Trees | A mandatory, independent-feature admission baseline a deep model must beat; source-reported to beat five DL models. Not in the numpy core (no sklearn). | 12, 13 |
| **GLOF** | Glacial Lake Outburst Flood | A primary target hazard; its rarity motivates Mondrian per-zone coverage; shield RED on lake-drop + downstream stage-jump. | 00, 05b, 08, 12 |
| **GLS** | Generalised Least Squares | See **BLUE / GLS**. | 05b |
| **GMF** | Gated-Mixture Fusion | Gated-mixture base + a **bounded residual** (clipped ±cap, default 0) that can run a learned head; with no head GMF ≡ FM-1; `ws5_fusion_rl/gmf.py`. | 02, 05, 05b |
| **GPIO** | General-Purpose Input/Output | Firmware-side pins driving siren/relay in `SirenBus` integration. | 08 |
| **GRD** | Ground-Range-Detected (Sentinel-1 SAR product) | SAR product whose ~900 m² minimum detectable area is the GLOF-precursor resolution floor (FM-27). | 13 |
| **GRU** | Gated Recurrent Unit | Temporal head of FireSmokeNet that suppresses single-frame fire false alarms (glint/headlights). | 05 |
| **GST** | Goods and Services Tax (India) | Included in the ≤₹2000 per-node BOM budget (C2) alongside shipping + ~10% contingency. | 03 |
| **HMAC(-SHA256)** | Hash-based Message Authentication Code | Keyed signature appended to CAP XML by `build_cap`; also the mesh-leg authentication requirement. | 08 |
| **HLD / LLD** | High-/Low-Level Design | Design documents in `DESIGN/`; HLD uses the symbol `τ*` where `_CANON.md`/code use `p*` (same operating point). | 02 (sources) |
| **I–D** | Intensity–Duration (rainfall threshold) | Caine power-law landslide-triggering screen `I_threshold = a·D^(−b)`; a soft `p_caine` into the geo gate; `ws1b_geophys/caine.py`. | 02, 05b |
| **IMERG** | Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for GPM | Satellite precipitation product bias-corrected by LoRa rain gauges in the calibration loop. | 02 |
| **InSAR** | Interferometric Synthetic-Aperture Radar | Ground-deformation / precursor sensing cached at the gateway tier. | 02 |
| **iForest** | Isolation Forest | A component of the anomaly stack (and the numpy "iForest-lite" always-on fallback). | 02 |
| **IoT** | Internet of Things | The ground sensor nodes (Tier-0): tilt/stage/rain, on-node FS and 1/v, LoRa uplink. | 02, 03 |
| **IQL** | Implicit Q-Learning | Offline-RL alternative (2110.06169) that **never queries OOD actions**; attractive for safety; not implemented. | 10 |
| **ISM** | Industrial, Scientific, Medical (radio band) | Licence-exempt band context; Bug #6 — 433 MHz is **not** an Indian ISM/LoRa band (IN865–867 is). | 13 |
| **LoRa** | Long Range (radio modulation) | Low-rate long-range radio for node→gateway links and the mesh tier; India band **IN865–867 MHz** on an **SX1262** transceiver; ≤51-byte frames. | 02, 08, 13 |
| **LoRa (PEFT) / LoRA** | Low-Rank Adaptation | A parameter-efficient fine-tuning method (PEFT) for adapting frozen backbones under the GPU budget. **Note the name clash** with the LoRa radio above — context disambiguates (training vs transceiver). | 11, 05a |
| **LSPIV** | Large-Scale Particle Image Velocimetry | Camera-based river-surface velocity method. **(definition not established in sources — the acronym does not appear in the chapters read; expansion is the standard field term `[LIKELY]`.)** | — |
| **LMEM / GLRT** | Linear Mixed-Effects Model / Generalised Likelihood-Ratio Test | The "real-win" statistical gate on every claimed improvement (provenance/reproducibility, F-17). | 02 |
| **MCE** | Maximum Calibration Error | `max over non-empty bins of |acc−conf|`; `eval/calibration.py`. | 12 |
| **MCU** | Microcontroller Unit | Tier-0 node processor; heavy models are Tier-1/2 only because Tier-0 runs only what fits MCU SRAM/flash/energy (C8). | 02 |
| **mDNS** | multicast DNS | Local-link discovery usable for same-LAN push — but only to devices already joined and listening (the narrow Tier-2 residual). | 08 |
| **MDP** | Markov Decision Process | The RL problem framing (state/action/reward/transition); specified only — nothing simulated. | 10 |
| **MILP** | Mixed-Integer Linear Programming | A strong non-RL optimiser baseline (GREAT-EER) the RL policy must beat, else "use the non-RL optimizer". | 10 |
| **MoE** | Mixture of Experts | Fusion routing (FM-5 physics-gated MoE); FM-06 warns of routing collapse → soft gating used. | 02, 13 |
| **Mondrian (CP)** | Mondrian Conformal Prediction | Per-group (per-hazard/zone) conformal coverage so a rare class (GLOF) isn't hidden by good marginal coverage; unseen groups fall back to the most conservative quantile. | 12 |
| **NAT** | Network Address Translation | Private, reassigned addresses behind NAT mean no routable per-device target — part of the IP `[INFEASIBLE]` verdict. | 08 |
| **NDMA** | National Disaster Management Authority (India) | Alerting authority; origination of cell broadcast/WEA is **their** function, not TRINETRA's. | 08 |
| **ND-1 / ND-2 / ND-3** | Novel Dimensionless fire terms | Three Class-C, default-OFF soft fire features (de-aliased flicker; smoke-transmittance temperature; ignition index), uncertainty grows as data degrade; `ws1a_firephys/novel_nd.py`. | 05b |
| **NF-1 … NF-4** | Novel-Fusion primitives 1…4 | Soft weighting/uncertainty primitives (consistency, reliability, conflict→uncertainty, salience) every fusion model reuses; `ws5_fusion_rl/nf.py`. They re-weight, never fabricate a probability. | 02, 05, 05b |
| **ns-3** | network simulator 3 | Planned primary alert-network simulator (LoRaWAN module); nothing simulated yet. | 08 |
| **OOD** | Out-Of-Distribution | (state,action) pairs the logging policy rarely took; CQL's conservative penalty pushes Q down on OOD actions. | 05, 10 |
| **OOF** | Out-Of-Fold | The model's own held-out score used as a "learned baseline"; a **circular** (weak) comparator — hence physics-rule/GBDT baselines are weighted as the ones that matter. | 12 |
| **OPE** | Off-Policy Evaluation | Estimating a learned policy's value from logged data; the deploy gate admits the learned policy only if OPE is feasible (positivity+ESS) **and** its value ≥ rule baseline. | 05, 10 |
| **PA** | Public Address (voice) | Multi-modal Tier-1 alert channel (with siren + strobe) for accessibility (blind users). | 08 |
| **PAV** | Pool-Adjacent-Violators (algorithm) | The isotonic recalibrator's engine: merges monotonicity-violating adjacent blocks into weighted means; `IsotonicCalibrator`. | 12 |
| **PBRS** | Potential-Based Reward Shaping | Reward-design discipline that preserves optimality — a mitigation against reward hacking. | 10, 13 |
| **PDR** | Packet Delivery Ratio | Alert-network simulation metric (source-reported, often SIMULATION-only). | 08 |
| **PEFT** | Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning | The "fine-tune, don't pretrain" compute strategy (frozen backbone + small adapters/LoRA) that makes the ≤30 GPU-h plan `[LIKELY]` feasible. | 03, 11 |
| **PHARAOH** | (project name for the adaptive-order power-mean fusion operator) | Class-C, default-OFF power-mean operator whose order `ρ=1+κ·D·S` bends toward "max" only under a credible physics-consistent alarm (anti-complacency); fails open to "uncertain". Expansion as an acronym **(definition not established in sources — treated as a project code-name)**. | 02, 05, 05b |
| **PINN** | Physics-Informed Neural Network | Geo-PINN uses physics (FS<1, Iverson residual) as a label-free penalty; a **full on-device fire-PINN solver is `[INFEASIBLE]`** now (stiffness, spectral bias) → physics enters as soft features with Class-A fallback. | 05, 13 |
| **PSI** | Population Stability Index | Drift metric in `drift_monitor.py` (>0.1 moderate, >0.2 significant); drift voids the coverage bound → reliability "Unreliable". | 12, 13, 15 |
| **PWS / SIB** | Public Warning System / System Information Block | 3GPP cell-broadcast delivery; SIBs are broadcast **without authentication** → spoofable (arXiv 2604.24404), hence signed-CAP + cross-cell corroboration. | 08 |
| **RCPS** | Risk-Controlling Prediction Sets | The CRC family that bounds a chosen risk (here the miss-rate) with finite-sample slack. | 12 |
| **ReportGuard** | (code object) | The gate (`eval/report.py`) that **refuses to emit a headline metric** unless spatial-CV + a real win over every baseline hold (Rule 16); today it reads **NOT ADMITTED**. | 12 |
| **RL** | Reinforcement Learning | Offline (batch) RL only — no live exploration in a life-safety valley; output is **advisory**, shielded, OPE-gated. | 02, 10 |
| **RMS** | Root Mean Square | Tiny Tier-0 statistical screen on tilt; also "FoS RMS error" in FM-24. | 02, 13, 15 |
| **RTA** | Run-Time Assurance | Framing of the shield as a conservative fixed-fallback RTA (Bug #26: a predictive/reachability-aware shield is future work). | 13 |
| **SACHET** | (India's CAP-based public alerting platform, NDMA/C-DOT) | The official CAP/cell-broadcast feed TRINETRA may **request** but never originate. Expansion as acronym **(definition not established in sources — used as the platform's name)**. | 02, 08 |
| **SAR** | Synthetic-Aperture Radar | Cloud-penetrating EO modality (Sentinel-1); its resolution floor limits small-GLOF detection (FM-27). | 02, 13 |
| **SCOPE-RL** | (offline-RL evaluation library/method) | RL risk-evaluation plan: report CVaR@5%, worst-case return, full return distribution (arXiv 2311.18206). Plan only. | 10 |
| **SF** | Spreading Factor (LoRa) | LoRa link-budget dial (SF7–SF12): higher SF = longer range, lower rate; source-reported SF7-8 ~120 dB … SF12 ~180 dB. | 08 |
| **SMS** | Short Message Service | Needs cellular + per-number opt-in → **not** "offline" and registry-limited (Tier-3 adjunct). | 08 |
| **SNR** | Signal-to-Noise Ratio | Radio-link quality in source-reported mesh ranges (e.g. Meshtastic +2.75 dB SNR). | 08 |
| **SoC** | System on Chip | Gateway (Tier-1) edge compute. | 02 |
| **SSL** | Self-Supervised Learning | EO encoder pretraining/adaptation paradigm (full SSL pretrain on Kaggle is `[INFEASIBLE]` under budget → PEFT). | 11 |
| **SX1262 / SX1278** | Semtech LoRa transceiver ICs | SX1262 is the **compliant** IN865–867 radio; SX1278 (433 MHz) was the non-compliant Bug #6 part. | 02, 13 |
| **TCN** | Temporal Convolutional Network | Causal encoder of the DeepAnomaly model (TCN AE + forecast + Deep-SVDD). | 05a, 11 |
| **TD3-BC** | Twin-Delayed DDPG + Behaviour Cloning | A minimalist offline-RL baseline (2106.06860); `FEATURES.md` F-06 names it "baseline-first", but the implemented Model 6 is **CQL** (documented divergence). | 10 |
| **TF32 / bf16 / fp16** | reduced-precision float formats | Mixed-precision training formats enabled by AMP/`setup_perf()`. | 11 |
| **TinyML** | Tiny Machine Learning | On-node pre-filter at Tier-0 (fits MCU budget). | 02 |
| **TRIGRS** | Transient Rainfall Infiltration and Grid-based Regional Slope-stability | The lineage that confirms the Iverson bug-guard `D1=D0/cos²β` with no extra transient cosine (Bug #3 refs). | 05b, 13 |
| **TRINETRA / HIMKAVACH** | project names (alternatives for the same project) | An offline-first, physics-grounded, **advisory** early-warning + hazard-detection research program **and** its reference code implementation. Component words are **(definition not established in sources — proper project names)**. | all |
| **UDP** | User Datagram Protocol | Transport for same-LAN broadcast/multicast push (Tier-2 residual). | 08 |
| **UNVERIFIED** `[UNVERIFIED]` | not confirmed against a primary source | Honesty tag for leads needing professional/primary-source confirmation (e.g. the regulatory "a private project cannot originate WEA" claim; all India legal/radio/alerting facts, N-7). | 03, 08 |
| **UNTESTED** | not executed in this environment | Status tag for the PyTorch `deep/`+`kaggle/` code: `py_compile`-clean but **never run on a GPU** here (no torch/CUDA in the sandbox). | 05, 05a, 10, 11 |
| **VAD** | Video Anomaly Detection `[LIKELY]` | A heavy Tier-1 video component listed in the architecture; expansion inferred from context (heavy video model). | 02 |
| **VPN** | Virtual Private Network | Relocates apparent IP, silently defeating any geo-IP logic (IP-verdict argument). | 08 |
| **VS** | Value Score | Cost-aware primary ranking metric, `VS = 1 − E_forecast/E_climate` (1 perfect; ≤0 no skill over climatology); `eval/value_score.py`. | 12 |
| **WAN** | Wide-Area Network | "Offline-first" = the primary path works with no internet/WAN backhaul. | 08 |
| **WCPS** | Weighted Conformal Prediction (under covariate Shift) | Reweights calibration residuals by a train→test likelihood ratio to keep coverage honest under input shift; `weighted_conformal_quantile`. (Written "WCPS" in `_CANON`/arch; `WeightedConformal` in code.) | 02, 12 |
| **WEA** | Wireless Emergency Alerts (US cell broadcast) | Authority-operated broadcast to all phones in a cell; source-reported behaviour change (−1.1 °F thermostat) and payload-limited geo-fencing (polygons → 9.7–23.6%). Not TRINETRA's to originate. | 08 |
| **WIS** | Weighted Importance Sampling | One-step OPE value estimator `Σ(w·r)/Σw` with clipped ratios + ESS; `rl.wis_value`. | 10 |
| **WS1 … WS8** | Workstream 1…8 | Internal artifact workstreams; map to the six user doc-frame workstreams per `_CANON.md §3` (see DOMAIN TERMS "workstream (WS) schemes"). | all (esp. 02, 03) |
| **XGBoost** | eXtreme Gradient Boosting | The supervised high-recall EWS / per-hazard ensemble and an anomaly-stack component (planned; sklearn/xgboost absent from the numpy sandbox). | 02 |
