## 2. Symbols and Notation (mathematical, alphabetical by role)

| Symbol | Meaning | Units | Where defined |
|---|---|---|---|
| **FS** | Factor of Safety; FS<1 ⇒ unstable, forces shield floor | dimensionless | `ws1b_geophys/fs.py` (05b §9) |
| **c′** | effective cohesion (Mohr–Coulomb) | kPa | fs.py (05b §9) |
| **φ′** | effective friction angle | degrees | fs.py (05b §9) |
| **γ** (soil) | soil unit weight | kN/m³ | fs.py (05b §9) |
| **γ_w** | unit weight of water (`u_w = γ_w·ψ`) | 9.81 kN/m³ | fs.py (05b §9) |
| **z** | depth to the failure plane | m | fs.py (05b §9) |
| **β** | slope angle | degrees | fs.py / iverson.py (05b §9–10) |
| **u_w** | pore-water pressure | kPa | fs.py (05b §9) |
| **σ_s** | suction stress (apparent-cohesion); σ_s ≥ 0, **vanishes at saturation** | kPa | fs.py (05b §9); Bug #2 |
| **σ′_n** | effective normal stress `= γz cos²β − u_w + σ_s` | kPa | fs.py (05b §9) |
| **S_e** | effective saturation; `S_e→1 ⇒ σ_s→0` | dimensionless (0–1) | 05b §9 |
| **ψ** | (transient) pressure head → becomes `u_w` for FS | m | iverson.py (05b §10) |
| **Z** | depth coordinate in the Iverson transient solution | m | iverson.py (05b §10) |
| **t** | time (consistent with D0) | s | iverson.py (05b §10) |
| **D0** | saturated hydraulic diffusivity | m²/s | iverson.py (05b §10) |
| **D1** | slope-adjusted diffusivity, **`D1 = D0/cos²β`** (the ONLY place slope enters — bug-guard) | m²/s | iverson.py (05b §10); `_CANON §4` |
| **K_z** | vertical saturated hydraulic conductivity | m/s | iverson.py (05b §10) |
| **I_z** | surface infiltration flux (`I_z ≤ K_z`) | m/s | iverson.py (05b §10) |
| **ierfc(x)** | integral of the complementary error function, `exp(−x²)/√π − x·erfc(x)`, `ierfc(0)=1/√π` | dimensionless | iverson.py (05b §10) |
| **v, 1/v** | surface-displacement velocity and its inverse (Fukuzono) | 1/v: time/length (consistent units) | fukuzono.py (05b §11) |
| **α** (Fukuzono) | inverse-velocity exponent; **α=2 ⇒ 1/v linear in t**; α≠2 linearises `v^(1−α)` | dimensionless | fukuzono.py (05b §11) |
| **t_f** | forecast failure time (x-intercept of 1/v), reported with a prediction interval `[t_f_low, t_f_high]` | same time units as input | fukuzono.py (05b §11) |
| **z** (CI) | normal quantile for the interval, `z=1.96 ≈ 95%` | dimensionless | fukuzono.py (05b §11) |
| **r²** | weighted goodness-of-fit; gates the Fukuzono contribution (`p_fk ∝ r²`) | dimensionless (0–1) | fukuzono.py (05b §11) |
| **I, D** | rainfall intensity, duration (Caine I–D) | I [mm/h], D [h] | caine.py (05b §12) |
| **a, b** | Caine threshold coefficients `I_threshold = a·D^(−b)`; **must be re-fit per region** (defaults a=14, b=0.39) | a carries mm·h^(b−1); b dimensionless | caine.py (05b §12) |
| **ratio** (Caine) | `I / I_threshold`; exceedance when > 1 | dimensionless | caine.py (05b §12) |
| **p\*** | cost-loss alarm operating point, **`p* = C_FA/(C_FA+C_miss) = 5/105 ≈ 0.0476`**; default `RuleBaselinePolicy` threshold | probability (0–1) | `_CANON §4`; value_score.py; decision.py |
| **τ\*** | the HLD's symbol for the same operating point — **τ\* ≡ p\* ≈ 0.0476** (`_CANON §4` uses p*, HLD uses τ*) | probability (0–1) | DESIGN/HLD.md (noted in this chapter header) |
| **C_FA** | false-alarm cost | **5** (unitless cost) | 10, 12; `_CANON §4` |
| **C_miss** | missed-event cost (≈20× C_FA) | **100** (unitless cost) | 10, 12; `_CANON §4` |
| **level cut points** | conformal-level cuts `(p*, 4p*, 10p*)` by default, or calibrated CRC cuts | probability | decision.conformal_level (05b §29) |
| **VS** | Value Score `1 − E_forecast/E_climate` | dimensionless | value_score.py (12.2.1) |
| **ECE, MCE** | expected / maximum calibration error | dimensionless (0–1) | calibration.py (12.2.5) |
| **Brier** | `mean((p−y)²)` | dimensionless (0–1) | calibration.py (12.2.5) |
| **α_t** (ACI) | adaptive miss-rate, `α_{t+1}=clip(α_t+γ(α_target−err_t),0,1)` | dimensionless (0–1) | conformal.py (12.7) |
| **γ** (ACI) | ACI learning rate (note: name clash with soil γ and RL γ) | dimensionless | conformal.py (12.7) |
| **q** (conformal) | adjusted calibration quantile, `k=ceil((n+1)(1−α))−1` | score units | conformal.py (12.2.6) |
| **λ** (CRC) | lowest alarm threshold whose corrected miss-rate ≤ target | score units | conformal_risk_threshold (12.7) |
| **p, u, c, r** | an `ExpertOutput`'s probability, uncertainty, conflict/consistency, reliability | each in [0,1] | common/types.py (02.7) |
| **w̃_i** | effective (gating) weight `= available·r_i·c_i·exp(−u_i/τ)` | dimensionless | nf.effective_weight (05 CLOSING A) |
| **τ** (gating) | gating temperature in w̃ (default 0.5) — **not** the operating point τ\* | dimensionless | nf.py (05b §20) |
| **U\*** | conflict-aware fused uncertainty `Σ w_i u_i + λ·D(p)`; U\*>0.6 ⇒ uncertain | dimensionless (0–1) | nf.nf3 (05b §20) |
| **D(p)** | weighted dispersion of expert probabilities (disagreement) | dimensionless | nf.py (05b §20) |
| **λ** (NF-3) | dispersion weight in U\* (default 0.3) | dimensionless | nf.py (05b §20) |
| **S** | salience `max_i[r_i·c_i·p_i]` over available experts | dimensionless (0–1) | nf.nf4 (05b §20) |
| **ρ** (PHARAOH) | power-mean order `1+κ·D·S`, clipped [1,8]; ρ=1 ⇒ arithmetic mean | dimensionless | pharaoh.py (05b §22) |
| **κ** | PHARAOH order gain (default 2) | dimensionless | pharaoh.py (05b §22) |
| **k_fs** | geo-gate FS→probability steepness, `p_fs=sigmoid(k_fs·(1−FS))`, k_fs=4.0 | dimensionless | gate.py (05b §13) |
| **cap / residual_cap** | hard clip on the GMF/attention learned residual (default 0.1) | probability units | gmf.py (05 CLOSING A) |
| **λ** (CQL) / cql_alpha | conservative-penalty weight in the CQL loss (default 1.0) | dimensionless | offline_rl.py (10.3.1) |
| **γ** (RL discount) | RL discount; **default 0.0** ⇒ one-step contextual bandit | dimensionless (0–1) | CQLConfig (10.3.1) |
| **τ** (Polyak) | target-net tracking rate `target←(1−τ)target+τ·online`, 0.005 | dimensionless | offline_rl.py (10.3.1) |
| **w_i** (WIS) | importance ratio `clip(target/clip(behavior,1e-6),0,1e3)` | dimensionless | rl.wis_value (10.3.2) |
| **ESS** | effective sample size `(Σw)²/Σw²` | count | rl.py (10.3.2) |
| **L** (flame) | Heskestad flame height `0.235·Q̇^(2/5) − 1.02·D` | m | established_ef.py (05b §14) |
| **Q̇ / Q** | heat-release rate (total / convective Q̇_c) | kW | established_ef.py (05b §14) |
| **D** (fire) | fire/pool diameter | m | established_ef.py (05b §14) |
| **f** (flicker) | Strouhal puffing frequency `f ≈ 1.5/√D` | Hz | established_ef.py (05b §16) |
| **St** | Strouhal number `St = f·√(D/g)` ~ const | dimensionless | established_ef.py (05b §14) |
| **N_c** | Byram convection number `2g·Q̇_c/(ρ c_p T∞ U³)`; >~2 plume-dominated, <~1 wind-dominated | dimensionless | established_ef.py (05b §14) |
| **U** (wind) | wind speed in the Byram number | m/s | established_ef.py (05b §14) |
| **E, T, ε** | gray-body radiance `E=ε·σ·T⁴`, temperature, emissivity | E [W/m²], T [K], ε (0–1) | established_ef.py (05b §14) |
| **σ** (Stefan–Boltzmann) | radiation constant 5.670374419e-8 | W·m⁻²·K⁻⁴ | established_ef.py (05b §14) |
| **τ** (Beer–Lambert) | transmittance `exp(−(κ+σ)·L)` (yet another τ — optical, not τ\*/gating) | dimensionless (0–1] | established_ef.py (05b §14) |
| **ΔT₀** | Heskestad plume centerline temperature rise | K | established_ef.py (05b §14) |
| **σ_K** (ND-2) | smoke-temperature uncertainty that **blows up as τ_s→0** (ill-conditioned ⇒ "uncertain") | K | novel_nd.py (05b §18) |
| **N_eff** | effective sample size under spatial correlation, **`N_eff = Θ(n²/r²)`** (naive CIs too narrow) | count | 12.1 (arXiv 2610.08227) |
| **g** (buffer) | spatial-CV correlation-range buffer, require `g ≥ r` (variogram) | length | 12.1 |
| **PSI** | population stability index (>0.1 moderate, >0.2 significant) | dimensionless | drift_monitor.py (15.x) |

> **Overloaded symbols — read by context:** `γ` is soil unit weight (geo), the ACI learning rate (conformal),
> and the RL discount; `τ` is the operating point `τ*`, the gating temperature, the Polyak rate, **and**
> optical transmittance; `λ` is the NF-3 dispersion weight **and** the CQL conservative weight; `D` is pool
> diameter (fire), rainfall duration (Caine), and probability dispersion (NF). `z` is depth (geo) and the CI
> normal quantile (Fukuzono). Each row above names which use it is.

## 3. Domain Terms (alphabetical)

| Term | Definition (grounded in the chapters) |
|---|---|
| **advisory level (Green/Yellow/Orange/Red)** | The system's only output: a four-level ordered advisory `Level` for a **human** operator, who alone decides on public dissemination. Green < Yellow < Orange < Red; the shield maps rules onto this lattice and the CAP builder maps levels to Severity/Urgency/Certainty deterministically (02.7, 08.4). |
| **advisory invariant / `advisory=True`** | Every `Decision` is marked advisory; **no code path issues an autonomous public alert** (Rule 19). Enforced by CI gate G-advisory and the banned-token G-legacy gate. |
| **bounded residual** | The central fusion safety property: a learned head may add only a residual **hard-clipped to ±cap** on top of the physics-anchored base, so a mis-trained head cannot dominate; with no head the residual is 0 (GMF ≡ FM-1). |
| **conformal coverage** | The realised fraction of outcomes falling in the prediction set/interval. Reported as **marginal and per-zone (Mondrian)**; **never called a "guarantee"** — it holds only under exchangeability/correct weights and is **voided under drift**. |
| **cost-loss / cry-wolf** | Scoring by a decision-theoretic cost table (C_FA=5, C_miss=100) rather than accuracy/AUC, because a missed event (death risk) is priced ~20× a false alarm. "Cry-wolf" is the failure where repeated false alarms erode compliance → future missed warnings (FM-09), which is why the FA cost is a real calibrated term. |
| **drift (PSI / CUSUM)** | Distribution shift detected by `drift_monitor.py` (PSI threshold, sequential CUSUM). On drift the conformal bound is void, reliability forced to **Unreliable**, and the decision fails to "uncertain". |
| **Deep-SVDD** | Deep Support-Vector Data Description: a one-class, normal-only anomaly head (Ruff et al. 2018) in the anomaly stack; prone to hypersphere collapse (Bug #22) → `init_center` + a model-free fallback kept. |
| **fail-safe to uncertain** | When no experts are available, conflict is high (U\*>0.6), or drift fires, the system **abstains and escalates to a human** — it is never silently confident and never goes silent at the top (Rule 19). |
| **forecast-residual anomaly** | Unsupervised anomaly signal = the residual between a one-step forecast and the observation; part of the WS8 ensemble (always-on numpy `AR(1)` residual + the deep TCN head). |
| **graceful degradation** | Each tier/layer keeps working when the one above is gone; a dropped modality is marked unavailable and widens uncertainty rather than crashing or faking a value (C8, missing-modality adapter). Winter/monsoon solar gaps make node outage **expected**, not exceptional. |
| **human-in-the-loop** | A human reviews `operator.present()` and must issue an `APPROVED:` token before any public CAP exists; "a machine proposes, a human authority disposes" (Rule 19). |
| **leakage** | Information bleeding from test into train — spatially (near-twin tiles in both splits) or temporally (post-event feature). It inflates skill; `assert_no_time_leak` + spatial-block CV + CI gate G-leak prevent it; a leaked number is **void**. |
| **meta-fusion** | The head that combines expert `ExpertOutput`s (physics gates, deep models, anomaly, RL) into one calibrated advisory via FM-1/GMF/PHARAOH + NF primitives + BLUE/GLS + hierarchical fusion, feeding the single `decide()`. |
| **offline-first / store-carry-forward** | The primary life-safety path must function with **no internet/WAN**, using owned local radio; DTN nodes **store** an alert, **carry** it, and **forward** it opportunistically when a link returns (binary Spray-and-Wait). |
| **physics Class A/B/C** | Trust labels (Rule 20): **A** = deterministic/established physics; **B** = physics-informed/-regularised learning; **C** = novel term, **default-OFF with an A/B fallback**. Class-C use is always flagged (`used_classC`). |
| **real-win gate** | A model is admitted only if its paired per-block cost saving over **every** baseline has a bootstrap **CI lower bound > 0** (`eval/real_win.py`, BCa over blocks). "Does not beat baseline" is a valid, published verdict. |
| **safety shield (monotone floor)** | A deterministic, hard-coded floor (`shield.py`) that can only **RAISE** the advisory level (FS<1→Orange, corroborated tilt→Red, etc.), applied **after** the learner (post-posed). Monotone over the Green<Yellow<Orange<Red lattice ⇒ total and realizable; a single uncorroborated node cannot reach RED. |
| **soft feature** | Physics quantities (e.g. fire-PINN outputs, ND terms, Caine ratio) entering fusion as *features/consistency* that nudge, never as hard triggers — the admitted way physics enters when a full solver is `[INFEASIBLE]`. |
| **spatial-block CV** | Cross-validation withholding whole spatial blocks (zones/catchments/tiles) so a model is always scored on unseen terrain; **mandatory** — random CV overstates skill. Companion: strict temporal holdout. |
| **workstream (WS) schemes** | Three numbering schemes coexist (`_CANON.md §3`): the **user doc-frame** (6 workstreams WS1–WS6 ≈ chapters), the **internal artifact** workstreams (WS1a/WS1b physics, WS2 deepfake/eval, WS3 alerting, WS4 CCTV, WS5 fusion/RL, WS6 robustness, WS7 IoT, WS8 anomaly), and the **code packages**. Always state which scheme a sentence uses. |
| **zero-shot complement** | Deepfake/zero-shot/crowd-sourced/social-media signals are **low-trust advisory only** (reliability hard-capped at r ≤ 0.4), must be corroborated, and can never gate a life-safety decision (`_CANON.md §6`). |

## 4. Honesty Labels, Rules, and Constraints (one place)

### 4.1 Honesty / status labels (apply to every non-trivial claim)

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **[CONFIRMED]** | Measured by us (e.g. "128 numpy tests pass; 6 CI gates pass") **or** verified in a cited source. (`_CANON.md §1`.) |
| **[LIKELY]** | Plausible but still needs our validation. (`_CANON.md §1`.) |
| **[HYPOTHESIS]** | Our unvalidated idea (e.g. the Class-C novel terms, PHARAOH benefit). (`_CANON.md §1`.) |
| **[INFEASIBLE]** | Ruled out (e.g. IP-based alerting; full on-device fire-PINN solver; autonomous public alerting without authority). (`_CANON.md §1,§6`.) |
| **[ABS]** | Abstract-only source read; **may never be stated as established fact**. Variants: ABS-CANONICAL. (`_CANON.md §1,§7`.) |
| **[EST]** | Estimated / planning-level figure not live-verified (all BOM ₹ costs). (`_CANON.md §8`.) |
| **[UNVERIFIED]** | A lead not confirmed against a primary source (e.g. the WEA-origination regulatory claim; all India legal/radio/alerting facts). |
| **UNTESTED** | Code that is `py_compile`-clean but **never executed** here (the PyTorch `deep/` + Kaggle layer — no GPU/torch in the sandbox). |
| Read-depth labels (sources) | **FT** full text · **FT-PARTIAL** partially read · **ABS** abstract · **ABS-CANONICAL** · **FT-REF** reference-only. (`_CANON.md §7`.) |

> Source-reported numbers must read "Paper X (arXiv NNNN.NNNNN) reports …" and be kept **visibly separate**
> from "Our measurement: …". Where a TRINETRA number would be expected, the honest answer is
> **"not measured"** — because **no model has been trained and no dataset downloaded** (`_CANON.md §0`).

### 4.2 Safety / honesty rules enforced in code (cite by number)

| Rule | Statement (verbatim intent, `_CANON.md §5`) | Where enforced |
|---|---|---|
| **R16** | No performance claim before the eval admission gate (ReportGuard). | `eval/report.py`; CI; chapter 12 |
| **R19** | Advisory, human-in-the-loop, fail-safe to "uncertain/offline"; **NEVER** an autonomous public alert. | shield, `decide`, `cap.build_cap` (APPROVED token); CI gate G-advisory; chapters 08, 10 |
| **R20** | Class A/B/C labels; Class-C novel terms **default-OFF** with an A/B fallback. | `used_classC`; CI gate G-classC; chapters 05b, 06 |
| **R21** | Novelty = "not found in sources searched", **never** "does not exist". | novelty log; CR-06; chapter 13 (Bug #5) |

### 4.3 Hard constraints (binding; chapter 03.3, with `_CANON.md §5` carrying C1,C2,C3,C6,C7,C8)

| ID | Constraint | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **C1** | Offline-first alert path | node→LoRa/DTN→gateway→siren works cloud-offline; cloud never on the critical path. |
| **C2** | ≤ ₹2000 per IoT node (incl. GST + shipping, ~10% contingency) | tiered BOM; all ₹ are `[EST]` until live-verified. |
| **C3** | Build compute = Kaggle only, ~25–30 GPU-h/week, ≥15% reserve | PEFT/frozen-backbone first; CPU for all non-training work. |
| **C4** | Free data only may be selected | datasets are candidates; licenses unverified. |
| **C5** | Life-safety → advisory, human-in-loop, fail-safe (= R19) | no autonomous alert; fail to "uncertain/offline". |
| **C6** | Endpoint allow-list (no credential egress) | enforced in CI; signed CAP; key rotation. |
| **C7** | No raw-video egress / privacy | edge-scored; only events/scores leave the node. |
| **C8** | Heavy models Tier-1/2 only | Tier-0 runs only MCU-feasible statistics. |
| **C9** | India LoRa band = IN865–867 MHz | SX1262 radio; 433 MHz SX1278 is non-compliant (Bug #6). |
| **C10** | Honesty rules R16/R19/R20/R21 | no claim pre-gate; class labels; novelty = search claim. |

> **Note on C-numbering:** `_CANON.md §5` lists only **C1, C2, C3, C6, C7, C8** explicitly; the fuller
> **C1–C10** set (including C4 free-data, C5 advisory, C9 LoRa band, C10 honesty-rules) is from
> `03_requirements_and_scope.md §3.3`. The task brief asked for "C1–C9"; C10 is included for completeness
> as it is sourced in chapter 03.

# 21 — FAQ & Troubleshooting

This chapter answers the questions a real user hits when they first read, run, extend, or try to deploy
TRINETRA (HIMKAVACH). It is a Q&A guide, cross-referenced to the chapter that owns each topic. It agrees
with `_CANON.md` exactly; where it quotes a run result, that result was observed in this environment and is
tagged `[CONFIRMED]`.

**Honesty labels (from `_CANON.md §1`):** `[CONFIRMED]` = measured by us here or verified in a cited source;
`[LIKELY]` = plausible, needs our validation; `[HYPOTHESIS]` = our unvalidated idea; `[INFEASIBLE]` = ruled
out; `[EST]` = planning estimate; **UNTESTED** = not executed in this environment.

**The one fact that resolves most confusion up front:** the **numpy core** runs here — `python run_tests.py`
→ **128 tests OK**, `python scripts/ci_gates.py` → **ALL 6 CI GATES PASSED**, `python demo.py` → an
end-to-end advisory decision — all `[CONFIRMED]`. The **torch / GPU / Kaggle** layer and **all datasets** are
**NOT runnable here** (no torch/CUDA/GPU, no data; sandbox has numpy, pandas, lxml only — `_CANON.md §2`).
Every answer in the KAGGLE/GPU section is therefore `[LIKELY]`/`[HYPOTHESIS]` guidance, not observed
behaviour; where an error string appears it is a **likely message** and is marked as such.

---

## 21.1 GENERAL FAQ

### Q. Is there any trained model, or any measured accuracy / skill / recall / latency / cost number?
**No. Nothing has been trained and nothing has been measured — by design.** `_CANON.md §0` and
`00_README_START_HERE.md §0.1` state it plainly, and `FINAL_REPORT.md` says verbatim: *"Nothing was built,
trained, or measured."* No TRINETRA model has been trained and no dataset has been downloaded, so there is
**no** TRINETRA accuracy, skill, recall, false-alarm, lead-time, latency, or cost figure anywhere. The only
"admitted" signal that exists is produced on **synthetic** demo data and it reads `admitted=False` (see
§21.2 and `18_reproduce_from_scratch.md §18.4`). This is the deliberate honesty-first state of a life-safety
project, not a documentation gap. `[CONFIRMED]`

### Q. Then why are all the performance numbers in the docs from other papers?
Two reasons, both deliberate. (1) **Rule 16 honesty (R16, `_CANON.md §5`):** no own performance claim may be
made before the spatial-CV eval admission gate passes, and since no model has been trained, that gate has
never been cleared — so there is no own number to quote. (2) **The research program never built or trained
anything** (`_CANON.md §0`); its job was to decide *what to build and why*, grounded in 631 arXiv references.
Every performance figure attributed to a *paper* is **SOURCE-REPORTED** on that paper's own data and is kept
visibly separate from "Our measurement: …" (`_CANON.md §1`). Full reference detail is in chapter 19; the
science posture is in chapter 12. `[CONFIRMED]`

### Q. Is this production-ready?
**No.** It is a **research program plus a reference-code implementation**. The numpy core runs and is tested,
but the system is **advisory-only and human-in-the-loop** by hard rule (R19), nothing has been trained, no
dataset or license has been verified, and the IoT cost/compute gates are not yet live-verified
(`_CANON.md §8`). Treat it as a correctness-proven skeleton and a decision/design record, not a deployable
product. See chapter 22 (limitations) and chapter 15 (deployment/ops) for what remains before any field use.
`[CONFIRMED]` for the code status; the "not production-ready" verdict follows from R16/R19 and the untrained
state.

### Q. Can it send alerts automatically?
**No — never, by rule.** R19 (`_CANON.md §5`) makes the system **advisory, human-in-the-loop, fail-safe to
"uncertain/offline"**, and this is enforced in code, not just documentation: `Config().require_human_approval()`
is hard-wired `True`, and `build_cap(...)` raises `SafetyViolation` if you try to build a public CAP message
without a human approval token. The CI gate **G-advisory** fails the build if either guarantee is removed, and
the banned token `advisory=False` is blocked by **G-legacy** (`17_testing_and_validation.md §17.4`). The one
autonomous actuation permitted is a **local siren / DTN rebroadcast** on the offline edge path — never a
public alert. Alerting detail is in chapter 08. `[CONFIRMED]` (gate observed passing here).

### Q. Why can't I just alert people by their IP address?
Because **IP-address-based alerting is `[INFEASIBLE]`** for life-safety targeting — this is a load-bearing
verdict the docs must carry un-softened (`_CANON.md §6`, source `FINAL_REPORT.md §4`). Consumer IP
geolocation resolves only to ISP/city granularity (often tens of km), is corrupted by CGNAT / VPN / DHCP,
does not map to a premises, and cannot address a specific person at risk. Public-IP exposure is instead
treated as a **security** concern (authenticated endpoints, allow-list C6). The full argument and the verdict
live in **chapter 08** (`08_ws3_offline_alerting.md`). `[INFEASIBLE]`

### Q. Which workstream is which? I keep seeing WS1a, WS1b, WS5, and also "WS1 physics".
Three numbering schemes exist and they are mapped explicitly in **`_CANON.md §3`**. Short version: the
user-facing **doc chapter frame** uses six workstreams (WS1 physics+meta-fusion, WS2 deepfake/media, WS3
offline alerting, WS4 CCTV, WS5 RL, WS6 robustness/bugs); the **internal artifacts** split finer (WS1a
fire-physics, WS1b geo-physics, WS5 fusion, WS7 IoT, WS8 anomaly, eval); and the **code packages** are
`ws1a_firephys/`, `ws1b_geophys/`, `ws5_fusion_rl/`, `ws6_robust/`, `ws7_iot/`, `ws8_anomaly/`, `eval/`, etc.
Always state which scheme a sentence uses. The canonical table is in `_CANON.md §3`. `[CONFIRMED]`

---

## 21.2 RUNNING THE CODE (numpy core — all answers `[CONFIRMED]` here)

### Q. `run_tests.py` prints `[exit code: 1]` at the end — did the tests fail?
**No — this is a known, benign quirk, not a failure.** `run_tests.py` returns `0` only when
`result.wasSuccessful()` (line 23), but `unittest.TextTestRunner` writes its **entire** report — including the
final `OK` — to **stderr**. Under this harness a command with non-empty stderr can surface a trailing
`[exit code: 1]` marker even on a clean, all-passing run.

The **authoritative** pass/fail signals (`17_testing_and_validation.md §17.6`), in order:
1. Final line is `OK` **and** the count line reads `Ran 128 tests` → **real pass**, regardless of
   `[exit code: 1]`.
2. Final line is `FAILED (failures=N, errors=M)`, or the count is not 128 → **real failure** (scroll up for
   `FAIL:` / `ERROR:` tracebacks).

The exact observed output in this environment was:
```
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 128 tests in 0.468s
OK
[exit code: 1]
```
`Ran 128 tests ... OK` is the pass. (`scripts/ci_gates.py` is unaffected — it exits `0` cleanly and prints
`ALL 6 CI GATES PASSED`.) `[CONFIRMED]`

### Q. I get a `UnicodeEncodeError` (or garbled/truncated output) on Windows when running the tests.
Set UTF-8 output **before** running, so `unittest`'s stderr summary renders cleanly:
```powershell
$env:PYTHONIOENCODING = "utf-8"
python run_tests.py
```
`unittest` writes its progress and summary to stderr; without a UTF-8 stream the Windows console can mangle or
truncate it. This is the exact env var that produced the recorded 128-tests / 6-gates result
(`_CANON.md §2`, `00_README_START_HERE.md §0.4`, `18_reproduce_from_scratch.md §18.1`). `[CONFIRMED]`

### Q. `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'numpy'` (or `trinetra`).
The core needs **numpy + stdlib**. Install the CORE tier from the package root:
```powershell
cd trinetra
pip install -e .          # declares numpy, pandas, lxml (pyproject.toml)
```
The code paths exercised by the tests, CI gates, and demo use **only numpy + stdlib** (`trinetra/README.md`,
`_CANON.md §2`). Note: `run_tests.py`, `scripts/ci_gates.py`, and `demo.py` each insert `src/` onto
`sys.path` themselves, so they also run straight from the repo root **without** `pip install -e .` as long as
numpy is importable (`18_reproduce_from_scratch.md §18.2`). If you see `ModuleNotFoundError: trinetra`, you
are running from the wrong directory — `cd` into the folder that contains `pyproject.toml` / `run_tests.py`.
`[CONFIRMED]`

### Q. `ImportError: No module named 'torch'` (or `MissingDependency`) when I touch a deep model.
**Expected — this is the design working, not a bug.** torch is confined to the quarantined `trinetra.deep`
package; the numpy core never imports it (`16_code_guide.md §16.3`). Every torch-only entry point raises
`MissingDependency` **on purpose** rather than fabricating a result — e.g. `EdgeDetector().detect(...)`,
`EOEncoder().embed(...)`, `DeepfakeDetector().score(...)`, `OfflineRLPolicy().fit(...)`
(`17_testing_and_validation.md §17.3.15`). The interface tests actually *assert* these raises as the proof
that "no path invents a number." To run a deep model you need the DEEP tier on a GPU box:
```bash
pip install -r requirements-deep.txt   # torch 2.3.1, torchvision, sklearn, xgboost, timm, d3rlpy, ...
```
This tier is **UNTESTED here** (no torch/GPU in the sandbox, `_CANON.md §2`); see chapters 05, 10, 11 and
`18_reproduce_from_scratch.md §18.5`. `[CONFIRMED]` that the stubs raise here; the DEEP install itself is
UNTESTED.

### Q. I hit an `AttributeError: 'numpy.ndarray' object has no attribute 'ptp'` on numpy 2.0.
numpy 2.0 removed the array **method** `arr.ptp()`. Use the **free function** `np.ptp(arr)` instead. The core
already does this throughout (`ws8_anomaly.iforest_lite_score` / `mahalanobis_lite_score` /
`anomaly_ensemble`), which is why it stays numpy-2.0 clean (`16_code_guide.md §16.7.3`). If you add code,
keep using `np.ptp(...)`. `[CONFIRMED — the fix is present in source]`

### Q. How do I run the demo, and what should I see?
From the `trinetra/` folder:
```powershell
$env:PYTHONIOENCODING = "utf-8"
python demo.py          # == python -m trinetra.pipeline.demo
```
Observed output (synthetic evidence — **no performance claim**, `18_reproduce_from_scratch.md §18.4`): a
Fukuzono inverse-velocity forecast `t_f ≈ 35.7 h (r2=0.973)`; a fused + conformal + shielded **advisory RED**
decision for zone `UK-CHX-07`, `risk=0.889`, `used_classC=False`, `fusion=FM-1`; the offline siren/DTN
fallback; a **human-gated** CAP 1.2 message; and the hindcast honesty gate printing `admitted=False` for both
the noise and the informative model. The `admitted=False` is **the Rule-16 gate working** on synthetic data,
not a failure — nothing may claim skill until it beats climatology + logistic baselines on spatial-CV with a
CI. `[CONFIRMED]`

## 21.3 KAGGLE / GPU (not runnable here — guidance is `[LIKELY]`/`[HYPOTHESIS]`, error strings are **likely messages**)

> None of the commands below were executed in this environment: there is no torch/CUDA/GPU and no dataset
> (`_CANON.md §2`). Flags are read verbatim from each script's real `argparse`
> (`18_reproduce_from_scratch.md §18.5`); runtimes and failure strings are planning-level guidance only. The
> operational contract for the ~25.5 usable GPU-h/week budget and resume logic is **chapter 11**
> (`11_training_compute_kaggle.md`); the Kaggle failure/fix table is also in chapter 11 §11.6.

### Q. Training dies with a CUDA out-of-memory error. [LIKELY]
Likely message (CUDA OOM): `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate ...`. Mitigations, in order:
- Lower **`--batch N`**, which is the **per-GPU** batch (effective batch = `N × n_gpus`, LR scaled linearly,
  Goyal 2017; `kaggle/README.md §2b`). Halving `--batch` roughly halves per-GPU activation memory.
- **Tile / stream** large inputs (EO patches, CCTV clips) instead of loading whole tensors.
- Use **gradient accumulation** to keep an effective batch while shrinking the per-step footprint.
- fp16 **AMP** is already on by default on the T4s, so you do not need to enable it manually.
`[LIKELY]` — not reproduced here.

### Q. Only one GPU shows up when I expected two T4s. [LIKELY]
On startup each script prints a banner like `GPUs visible=2 | DataParallel=True | effective_batch=128
lr=6.00e-04` (`18_reproduce_from_scratch.md §18.5.2`). If it says `GPUs visible=1`:
- Check **Settings → Accelerator = GPU T4 ×2** in the Kaggle session (`kaggle/README.md §1`); a P100 session
  is single-GPU by design.
- To *intentionally* run single-GPU, pass **`--parallel none`** (forces single-GPU); `--parallel dp` forces
  DataParallel, `--parallel auto` (default) uses DataParallel only when `n_gpus()>1`.
- Note **offline-RL is deliberately 1 GPU** (`scale_batch_by_gpus=False`; the Q-net is tiny, so scatter/gather
  costs more than it saves) and prints `offline-RL uses 1 GPU (tiny net)` — that is expected, not a fault.
`[LIKELY]`.

### Q. Geo-PINN throws a DataParallel autograd `RuntimeError`. [LIKELY]
The Geo-PINN physics loss uses `autograd.grad` **inside** the forward pass; DataParallel runs this per-replica
and *usually* works (`kaggle/README.md §2b`, chapter 13). The known-good fix — rebuilding `Z,t` as autograd
leaves inside `geo_pinn_step` via `detach().requires_grad_()` so autograd works under DataParallel — is
**already in the code** (`16_code_guide.md §16.5.8`, `GeoPINN`). So you should not hit it on the shipped path.
If a *custom change* reintroduces the error (a likely message would be a thread/autograd `RuntimeError` about
differentiating a non-leaf or a backward-through-replica failure), rerun with **`--parallel none`** or use the
DDP launcher (`trinetra.deep.ddp`). The root-cause write-up is in **chapter 13** (bugs/fixes). `[LIKELY]`.

### Q. My Kaggle session died at around 12 hours and I lost everything. [LIKELY]
Kaggle sessions are killed at ~12 h; a run that misses the wall **loses all its spent quota**
(`18_reproduce_from_scratch.md §18.5.3`). Protect every run:
- **Checkpoint to `/kaggle/working` every ≤30 min AND before the ~11 h wall** (one-hour margin), and
  **resume on restart**. Resume anchors are written per fold/model (`geo_pinn_fold{fold}.pt`,
  `{model}_fold{fold}.pt`, `anomaly_fold{fold}.pt`, `offline_rl.pt`, `gmf_head.pt`).
- Prefer **commit / batch runs** over interactive (idle timeout wastes quota).
The full resume contract is **chapter 11 §11.5**. `[LIKELY]`.

### Q. I ran out of my weekly GPU quota. [LIKELY]
The planning budget is ~**30 GPU-h/week**, kept to ~**25.5 usable** with a ≥15% reserve (`_CANON.md §8`);
these are **widely-published, not freshly fetched** numbers — **re-confirm them on the live Kaggle quota
panel first**. To live within it, follow **chapter 11**'s per-workstream GPU-hour budget and cut-list
(e.g. WS1 flood 5.0, landslide 2.5, anomaly 2.0, RL 1.0, media 1.0 GPU-h `[EST]`,
`18_reproduce_from_scratch.md §18.7`): train the highest-value models first, use checkpoint/resume so no quota
is wasted on a killed session, and drop the lowest-priority runs from the cut-list when the reserve is tight.
`[LIKELY]`/`[EST]`.

## 21.4 RESULTS / SCIENCE

### Q. My trained result differs from the number the paper reported. Is something wrong?
**Probably not.** Paper numbers are **source-reported on the paper's own data and split** (`_CANON.md §1`),
not on yours. Two structural reasons your number will differ — and usually be **lower**:
- **Different data / region / split.** You are evaluating on your data with **mandatory spatial-block CV**
  (train/val never share a spatial cell); the paper may have used random CV, which **overstates** skill. The
  grounded source `arXiv 2608.12422` shows naive terrain ROC-AUC ~0.90 collapsing to 0.76/0.71/0.54 under
  matched spatial-CV (`_CANON.md §6`, `analysis/07_claims_table.csv` C001–C003).
- **The admission bar is stricter.** A number only "counts" for TRINETRA if it passes the **real-win gate**
  (beats every baseline on spatial-CV with a bootstrap CI whose lower bound > 0). See **chapter 12**
  (`12_evaluation_and_results.md`). A lower-but-admitted number is the honest one. `[CONFIRMED]` for the
  protocol; your specific number is **UNTESTED here**.

### Q. My model doesn't beat the baseline. Did I fail?
**No — that is a valid, reportable scientific outcome, and the system is built to accept it.** The eval
harness compares against mandatory non-learned baselines (climatology, persistence, physics-rule) plus a
pure-numpy logistic learner, and `real_win` only returns `True` when the CI lower bound on the cost saving is
> 0 (`16_code_guide.md §16.5.6`, chapter 12). If your model loses, **report that** — and critically, **do not
tune on the test fold** to manufacture a win; that destroys the spatial-CV guarantee. An honest "did not beat
baseline" is a result; a tuned-on-test "win" is a Rule-16 violation. `[CONFIRMED]` for the gate behaviour.

### Q. My conformal coverage isn't exactly 90%.
Conformal coverage is **marginal and approximate**, and it degrades **under distribution shift** — exact
finite-sample coverage holds only under exchangeability. On exchangeable data the core lands within ±0.03 of
1−α (`17_testing_and_validation.md §17.3.13`). Under shift, use the adaptive variants the code already ships:
**WCPS** (weighted CP for covariate shift), **ACI** (Adaptive Conformal Inference — tracks ~90% long-run
coverage under drift), **Mondrian** (per-hazard group coverage), and **conformal risk control** (bounds the
realized miss rate). Also check the **drift monitor** (PSI/CUSUM) — a fired drift flag **voids** the CP
guarantee and should drop reliability to `Unreliable`. Details in **chapter 12**
(`16_code_guide.md §16.5.5`). `[CONFIRMED]` for the implemented behaviour.

### Q. `ReportGuard` refuses to print my metric / raises `ReportGuardError`. Is that a bug?
**No — that is R16 enforcement working.** `ReportGuard.headline()` **refuses** to emit a headline number
unless (a) spatial-CV was used, (b) baselines are registered, and (c) a **real win over every** baseline is
recorded (`16_code_guide.md §16.5.6`, `17_testing_and_validation.md §17.3.10`). The refusal means your result
has **not passed the admission gate**, so it may not be reported as skill — exactly the intended behaviour in
a life-safety domain. Add the missing spatial-CV / baselines, or accept that the metric is not admissible yet.
See chapter 12 for the full admission protocol. `[CONFIRMED]`.

---

## 21.5 EXTENDING THE CODE

All recipes below are from **chapter 16** (`16_code_guide.md §16.8`); honor §16.7.2 (new dataclass fields get
defaults; new function params are keyword-only after `*`) so the 128 tests keep passing, and keep every
Class-C path default-OFF (Rule 20). Add a matching test every time (`17_testing_and_validation.md §17.8`).

### Q. How do I add a new dataset?
Document the dataset's provenance / structure / license / splits in **chapter 04** (`04_DATASETS.md`), then
wire it for training per the **chapter 16** recipe: add a Kaggle `.npz` entry in `deep/datamodules.py`
(`KagglePaths` + a `Dataset` class exposing a `.block` array), and build `block` from lat/lon via
`datamodules.spatial_block(lat, lon)` so **train/val never share a spatial cell** (mandatory spatial-block CV,
`_CANON.md §6`, `kaggle/README.md §2`). The expected per-model `.npz` key layouts are in `kaggle/README.md §2`
and `18_reproduce_from_scratch.md §18.6`. **Licenses are not verified anywhere in this project — confirm each
dataset's license at download time before use** (`18_reproduce_from_scratch.md §18.6`). `[CONFIRMED]` for the
recipe; datasets themselves are **UNTESTED / not downloaded**.

### Q. How do I plug in a new model / expert?
Follow `16_code_guide.md §16.8.1`:
1. Implement the torch model under `src/trinetra/deep/<model>.py` (mirror `fire_cnn.py`: a `@dataclass`
   config, an `nn.Module` returning `{"logit"/"prob", …}`, a `.loss(...)`); keep it torch-only.
2. Register its **trust policy** in `ws5_fusion_rl/adapters.py` `_POLICY` as `(default_r, cap_r,
   PhysicsClass)`; at runtime `deep_expert("<source>", prob)` yields an `ExpertOutput` with the right class
   and a reliability cap (unknown sources raise `KeyError`, by design).
3. Add a Kaggle kernel under `kaggle/` and the dataset entry in `deep/datamodules.py`.
4. The expert then flows through `decide()` **unchanged** — no decision-path edits (single decision path).
5. **Add a test** in `tests/interfaces/` that the torch stub raises `MissingDependency`, and in
   `tests/fusion/` (like `test_adapters.py::test_flows_through_decide`) that `deep_expert("<source>", p)` has
   the right `cls` / capped `r` and flows through `decide()`. `[CONFIRMED]` for the recipe.

### Q. How do I add a new physics relation, a new fusion option, or a new eval baseline?
All three are in **chapter 16 §16.8**:
- **Physics relation (§16.8.2):** add the function to `ws1b_geophys/` or `ws1a_firephys/` (pure numpy, with a
  Class label and `[coeff-verify]`); if Class C it must be **default-OFF behind a `firephys.ndX` /
  `geophys.*` flag with a Class-A/B fallback**. Wire it into the package `gate.py` as a **soft** sub-signal
  (noisy-OR for geo; consistency/uncertainty for fire) — never a hard trigger. If you also add a
  differentiable PINN version in `deep/losses.py`, keep the **slope-only-via-D1 bug-guard**. Test: a
  limit/monotonicity golden in `tests/physics_golden/`, plus `test_classC_off_by_default` if Class C.
- **Fusion option (§16.8.3):** implement the operator in `ws5_fusion_rl/`, register it in
  `fusion_models.fuse()`'s dispatcher behind a `fusion.model` value (or an `operator.*` flag if Class C —
  default OFF), make sure it reports `used_classC` and **can never lower the shield floor**, and keep **FM-1
  as the fallback** when disabled or with <2 experts. Test: a property test in `tests/fusion/` plus
  `test_default_is_fm1_not_classC`.
- **Eval baseline (§16.8.4):** add it to `eval/baselines.py` (numpy/stdlib only, like `LogisticNumpy`), then
  register it as a mandatory comparator in both `pipeline/hindcast.run_hindcast` and
  `deep/train.admit_model` (call `guard.add_baseline_verdict(name, real_win(...))`). Because `ReportGuard`
  requires a real win over **every** baseline, adding one makes the gate strictly harder — exactly the intent
  (R16). Test: extend `tests/eval/` (`test_better_model_wins_worse_does_not`, `test_not_admitted_blocks_claim`).
`[CONFIRMED]` for the recipes.

# 22 — Limitations, Risks & Open Problems

> This is the chapter where honesty is most load-bearing. Read it before you trust any other number in this
> documentation set. Everything here agrees with `_CANON.md`; where a limitation touches a canonical fact the
> number is copied exactly. Honesty labels follow `_CANON.md §1`: `[CONFIRMED]` (measured by us or verified in
> a cited source), `[LIKELY]`, `[HYPOTHESIS]`, `[INFEASIBLE]`, plus `[UNVERIFIED]` for unchecked external facts
> and `[EST]` for estimated figures. "Paper X reports …" is kept visibly separate from "Our state: …".
>
> One sentence governs the whole chapter: **No TRINETRA model has been trained and no dataset has been
> downloaded, so no accuracy, skill, latency, false-alarm, coverage, or cost number in this project is a
> measured result of TRINETRA.** Every weakness below is stated plainly and is not mitigated away. Where a
> mitigation is only an intention, it is labelled `[HYPOTHESIS]` — a design plan, not a demonstrated control.

---

## A. Fundamental state limitations (the big ones)

These are not gaps to be apologised for; they are the deliberate, declared state of a research-first,
honesty-first, life-safety project. They dominate every other limitation in this chapter.

- **A1 — Nothing was trained.** [CONFIRMED] `FINAL_REPORT.md` states verbatim: *"Nothing was built, trained,
  or measured."* No weights exist for any of the six PyTorch models, no fusion head is fitted, no RL policy is
  learned. Any model-shaped artifact in the repo is a specification or an untrained module, not a trained
  system.
- **A2 — No dataset was downloaded.** [CONFIRMED] Every dataset is `STATUS = candidate [D]` (D-numbered to
  D112); none is `selected`; none is on disk here. Dataset discovery produced a catalogue, not data.
- **A3 — No measured skill / accuracy / latency / false-alarm / coverage number exists.** [CONFIRMED] Every
  performance figure anywhere in this documentation is **SOURCE-REPORTED** — it is some other paper's result on
  that paper's own data, carried under Rule 16. Where a reader expects a TRINETRA result, the honest answer is
  **"not measured."** This includes: detection recall, smoke-specific recall, false-alarms/day,
  time-to-detection, PICP/coverage, averted loss, radio range, node current draw, RAM, and end-to-end latency.
- **A4 — The `deep/` layer is compile-only.** [CONFIRMED] The PyTorch `deep/` layer (6 models + fusion heads)
  and the `kaggle/` training scripts are verified by `py_compile` only. They have **never been run on a GPU in
  this environment** — the sandbox has numpy, pandas, lxml only (no torch / CUDA / scipy / sklearn / yaml).
  "Compiles" means the Python parses, not that the forward pass is correct, the shapes line up at runtime, the
  loss decreases, or the model trains. What *does* run and is verified: the pure-numpy core — `python
  run_tests.py` → **128 tests OK** and `python scripts/ci_gates.py` → **ALL 6 CI GATES PASSED** [CONFIRMED].
- **A5 — Dataset licenses are unverified.** [UNVERIFIED] All [D] candidate licenses are INDICATIVE only.
  Portal access and license verification are an OPEN backlog item. A dataset that looks free may carry
  redistribution, attribution, or non-commercial terms we have not read. No dataset may be used in a build
  until its license is confirmed (gate G7).
- **A6 — The BOM is entirely estimated; the ≤₹2000 gate is not enforceable.** [EST] Indian supplier pages
  returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) this session, so every ₹ figure is an estimate, not a dated live listing.
  Node A "Slope Sentinel" ≈ ₹1,930 [EST] and Node B "River Eye" ≈ ₹1,980 [EST] both sit *just under* the
  ₹2,000 ceiling — but the ceiling (constraint C2) **cannot be enforced** until every line item is re-quoted
  from ≥2 dated live listings (gate G5, OQ-05). A small price move on any component tips a node over budget.
- **A7 — Kaggle limits are not freshly fetched.** [UNVERIFIED] The compute plan assumes ~30 GPU-h/week
  (≈25.5 usable after a 15% reserve), ~12 h sessions, P100 (16 GB) or 2× T4 (2×16 GB), ~20 GB persistent +
  ~73 GB scratch, ~13–16 GB RAM. Kaggle's docs pages are JS-rendered and returned no usable text via
  `web_fetch`; these are the **widely-published** limits, not values read from the live quota panel. They must
  be re-confirmed on the account at the first build session before any schedule is committed (constraint C3).
- **A8 — India regulatory / LoRa-band / alerting-authority facts are unverified and are not legal advice.**
  [UNVERIFIED] Every India regulatory finding — fire-device certification, radio/LoRa-band legality
  (assumed IN865–867 MHz, SX1262), who may originate official CAP/SACHET/WEA alerts, data-protection in video,
  CCTV/surveillance rules, electronics certification — is a search lead flagged for qualified legal/standards
  review. The specific claim "authorities-only may originate WEA/SACHET" has **not** been checked against
  ITU/3GPP/NDMA. Nothing in this project is legal advice.
- **A9 — arXiv identifiers are largely subagent-reported, not independently re-fetched.** [UNVERIFIED,
  disclosed residual risk] The ledger holds **631 unique arXiv IDs** as snapshotted in FINAL_REPORT §5 (the
  live ledger has since grown to ~**775**; see `_CANON §7`/ch19) (681 ID-bearing rows; ~7.3% legitimate
  cross-phase re-citations) with ≈436 new papers verified across phases.¹ Most IDs were reported by subagents;
  `web_search` had no API key and arXiv re-resolution was only via throttled `web_fetch`, so most IDs were
  **not independently re-fetched**. Residual risk: a cited ID may be mis-transcribed or point to a different
  paper than described. A load-bearing sample HAS now been resolved: 9 IDs in `_QG2_reference_verification_log.md`
  plus the ch19 "load-bearing references — fully verified (2026-10-10)" subsection (all HTTP 200 + title match);
  the long tail stays disclosed-unverified.

  > ¹ The figures **681 ID-bearing rows** and **≈436 verified** are *not* canon numbers — they come from the
  > orchestrator's regex pass over `analysis/02_paper_ledger.csv` and the phase logs, not `_CANON §7` (which
  > records only 631-snapshot / ~775-live). Treat 681/436 as ledger-derived provenance detail, not a canonical count.

---

## B. Scientific / statistical limitations

These bound what any eventual TRINETRA skill number could legitimately mean, even after a full build.

- **B1 — Very few geo events (n ≈ 5-ish) → any skill estimate is variance-dominated.** [CONFIRMED as a
  structural limit] Rapid-onset Himalayan hazards are rare; with on the order of five labelled geo events, a
  point estimate of skill (ROC-AUC, MCC, recall) carries confidence intervals so wide that the number is
  essentially uninformative on its own. Headline skill claims must be reported with intervals (IQM + CIs), and
  a tight-looking mean on five events is **not** evidence.
- **B2 — Spatial leakage inflates skill; random CV overstates it.** Paper reports: **arXiv 2608.12422**
  (FT-PARTIAL, on OUR hazards / region / free-data constraint) finds naive non-spatial evaluation inflates
  terrain-susceptibility ROC-AUC from a naive ~0.90 down to **0.76 / 0.71 / 0.54** (GLOF-burst / landslide /
  small-flood) under honest tile-withheld spatial-CV with case-control matching — an inflation of ≈0.15–0.35
  AUC. The finite-sample side is **2610.08227** (effective sample size N_eff = Θ(n²/r²); buffer g = Θ(r·log(n/δ))).
  Our state: spatial-block CV with a buffer ≥ the measured spatial-correlation range is **mandatory** before
  any skill claim (gate G2); random CV is forbidden as a headline. We have **not** measured the correlation
  range r on Himalayan (anisotropic) terrain — that remains open.
- **B3 — Calibrated members ≠ a calibrated ensemble.** Paper reports: **arXiv 2101.05397** — averaging
  individually-calibrated models does not yield a calibrated ensemble. Our state: the fused output must be
  **re-calibrated per availability** (per-zone Mondrian conformal), and member-level calibration is never
  taken as ensemble-level calibration. This is a design response `[HYPOTHESIS]`, not a demonstrated outcome.
- **B4 — Conformal coverage degrades under drift; it is approximate, not a guarantee.** Papers report:
  split-conformal coverage collapses from 90% toward ~65% under moderate shift (**2604.22787**); EnbPI
  (**2010.09107**) gives coverage with an explicit, shift-sensitive *gap* that only → 0 under regularity;
  DistMatch (**2606.00690**) and AFOCP (**2511.15838**) keep *long-term/asymptotic* validity but note **local
  miscoverage right after an abrupt shift** — exactly the rare-hazard moment. Our state: we must **never**
  claim a hard 1−α coverage on these streams. Coverage is approximate-under-stability; a tight conformal
  interval must never suppress a physics-gated alarm (shield priority). Empirical per-zone coverage on
  Himalayan streams is unmeasured.
- **B5 — The admission-baseline circularity.** [CONFIRMED limitation of the current code path] The eval
  admission classifier / anomaly-logistic is fit on the **model's own out-of-fold (OOF) score**, so part of
  the admission signal is circular — the gate is partly judging the model against a label derived from the
  model. The *geo* path uses real external features (terrain, antecedent rainfall), which breaks the
  circularity there; the fire/anomaly logistic path does not fully. Until the admission gate is driven by
  independent labels, an "admitted" verdict is weaker than it appears.
- **B6 — Confident-while-wrong failure.** Paper reports: **arXiv 2610.08810** — models stay confident while
  being wrong under distribution shift. Our state: a high model probability is **not** evidence of
  correctness; uncertainty-entropy is used as an alert gate and cross-sensor corroboration is required, because
  a single confident model output cannot be trusted at a decision boundary. This is a known, named failure the
  design must assume is present, not a solved problem.

---

## C. Engineering / deployment risks

- **C1 — Single-node false RED.** A single faulty IoT node (stuck tilt, water-ingress short, drifted gauge)
  can emit a spuriously extreme reading. Intended mitigation `[HYPOTHESIS]`: fault-vs-event discrimination
  (a physically implausible lone spike is treated as a fault, not an event) plus the deterministic shield and
  cross-sensor corroboration. None of this is measured; a false RED from a single node is a live risk until the
  discrimination logic is validated against real fault data (gate G5).
- **C2 — IMERG precipitation underestimation.** Satellite IMERG precip is known to underestimate intense
  orographic/convective rainfall — the exact regime that drives cloudbursts and flash floods. Intended
  mitigation `[HYPOTHESIS]`: LoRa rain-gauge bias-correction of IMERG at the gateway. Residual: where no gauge
  exists, the precip input is biased low precisely when it matters most.
- **C3 — INT8 smoke-recall loss.** INT8 quantisation of the edge CCTV detector (needed to fit Tier-0/Tier-1
  budgets) is expected to cost recall, and smoke (low-contrast, diffuse) is the most fragile class. We have
  **not** measured the INT8 recall drop; it is a known quantisation risk, not a quantified one.
- **C4 — LoRa regulatory / band risk.** [UNVERIFIED] The design assumes IN865–867 MHz (SX1262). If the
  assumed band or duty-cycle is wrong for India, the radio is illegal or non-functional (assumption A-06). Not
  verified against the regulator; blocks hardware order (gate G5).
- **C5 — Solar brownout / winter-monsoon outages.** Node outage is treated as **EXPECTED, not exceptional**:
  winter and monsoon solar gaps will starve nodes. Intended mitigation `[HYPOTHESIS]`: oversized power,
  LiFePO4 storage, deep-sleep duty-cycling, store-carry-forward (DTN). Residual: the alert path must degrade
  gracefully to "uncertain/offline" during multi-day outages — unmeasured.
- **C6 — India data portals are JS-only and unverified.** [UNVERIFIED] Bhuvan / MOSDAC / VEDAS / NRSC / IMD /
  CWC / GSI portals are JavaScript-rendered and returned no usable static content; programmatic access,
  availability, and terms are unconfirmed. A data pipeline that assumes these portals may not be buildable as
  designed (gate G7).
- **C7 — Class-C physics and fusion are unvalidated and expert-review-pending.** Class-C novel terms
  (fire flicker/ND terms C-01/C-02; the PHARAOH power-mean operator) are **documentation-only, default-OFF**,
  with a Class-A fallback. They are hypotheses with validation roadmaps and a **mandatory fire-science /
  fusion expert review** that has not happened. They must not be described as established or validated
  (gate G1).

---

## D. RL-specific limitations

- **D1 — No off-the-shelf disaster-evacuation RL environment (BUILD GAP).** [CONFIRMED gap] There is no
  existing simulator for the disaster-evacuation / dispatch decision problem. One must be **built** before any
  RL training or offline-policy evaluation is meaningful. Until it exists, every RL claim is purely a design.
- **D2 — Off-policy evaluation (OPE) positivity / ESS fragility.** OPE on logged or simulated episodes is only
  valid where the logging policy had support (positivity) and the effective sample size is adequate. The
  design requires a DataCOPE-style **OPE-feasibility gate** (2311.14110): if the offline data does not support
  evaluating a policy, fall back to a one-step / shielded fixed policy. This means an RL policy may be
  **un-evaluable** on our data and therefore undeployable.
- **D3 — Reward-inversion / reward-hacking risk.** A mis-specified reward can be gamed — e.g. minimising false
  alarms by never alarming, or chasing a proxy that inverts the life-safety objective (a missed event is far
  worse than a false alarm: C_miss=100 vs C_FA=5, p* ≈ 0.0476). Reward design is thinly sourced on arXiv
  (one hard number, 2109.07745) and is an open item.
- **D4 — RL must beat MILP / non-RL baselines or it does not deploy.** [CONFIRMED doctrine] Papers report RL
  only *sometimes* beats classical baselines and naive RL underperforms (2509.19972; MILP 2602.14676;
  stochastic-program alternative 2608.26304). Our state: RL is **advisory only** (ranked options to a human
  dispatcher, never actuation) and must beat a fixed-threshold → one-step → MILP/stochastic-program ladder
  under our protocol, or it is not carried. We have no evidence it does; the burden of proof is on RL.

---

## E. Security / privacy residuals

- **E1 — Placeholder cryptography.** [CONFIRMED current state] CAP-alert and IoT-message signing is
  **HMAC-SHA256 placeholder** crypto because the sandbox lacks the `cryptography` library. Production intent is
  **Ed25519 / XML-DSig** for CAP, which is **not implemented**. HMAC with a shared secret does not give the
  non-repudiation and public-key verification an authority-grade alert feed needs; this is a stub, not the
  production security posture.
- **E2 — Several security mitigations are design-intent only.** [HYPOTHESIS] The following are specified, not
  demonstrated: tamper detection, adversarial-patch defence on the CCTV detector, face-blur / privacy
  redaction, and key rotation. Each is a plan in the design docs; none is validated, red-teamed, or measured.
  Treat them as intended controls, not controls in place.

## F. Known open consistency items (from `PROGRESS_DOC.md`)

These are code-internal / cross-artifact nuances flagged by chapter writers for the QG4 consistency gate.
They are **not** contradictions with `_CANON.md`; they are divergences to reconcile in the docs. Listed here so
a reader is not surprised by them.

- **F-a — RL action cardinality 3-vs-binary.** `deep/offline_rl.py` uses 3 actions {HOLD, WATCH, ALARM};
  the numpy `rl.py RuleBaselinePolicy.act` is binary {0,1}. The 3→binary mapping used in OPE-vs-baseline is
  implicit ([LIKELY] {WATCH, ALARM}→alarm). Canonical statement still to be fixed.
- **F-b — "TD3-BC" label vs implemented CQL.** `FEATURES.md` F-06 labels the RL component "TD3-BC
  baseline-first", but implemented Model-6 is **CQL** (one-step, γ=0). Consistent in spirit; a one-line
  reconciliation is needed (docs only — do not edit `FEATURES.md`).
- **F-c — Shield only in torch `act()`.** The safety shield exists only in torch `CQLPolicy.act`
  (`shield_floor_idx`); `rl.py` has no standalone shield class, and the realizability check is **specified,
  not implemented**. The "hard monotone shield" is therefore not uniformly present across both code paths.
- **F-d — CCTV→fusion via adapter, not a direct call.** CCTV→fusion wiring is via
  `ws5_fusion_rl/adapters.deep_expert` + `_POLICY` caps, not a direct call in `ws4_cctv`; no explicit
  orchestrator call-site was found. The end-to-end "frame → fusion" claim should be softened accordingly.
- **F-e — Battery chemistry LiFePO4 vs Li-ion 18650.** `HLD §4` says LiFePO4; `firmware/FIRMWARE_SPEC.md`
  says Li-ion 18650 + PV; `_CANON.md §8` is silent. Both are reported; canonical choice is undecided.
- **F-f — Tilt-rate unit deg/s vs deg/day.** `ws7_iot/edge_screen.py` uses `tilt_rate_dps` (deg/s);
  `COMPONENT_DESIGN.md §5` says "5°/day". The code marks these thresholds illustrative, but the unit
  discrepancy is unresolved and safety-relevant for an edge screen.
- **F-g — Demo invocation.** Documentation shows `python demo.py` (per `00_README`), while the module path is
  `python -m trinetra.pipeline.demo`. The two invocation forms must be reconciled so the quick-start command
  actually runs.
- **F-h — Stale test count in `MODEL_CARDS.md`.** `MODEL_CARDS.md` says "93 tests" (stale); canonical is
  **128** (`_CANON §2`, `CODE_INVENTORY.md`). Source artifact, not edited; noted as stale.

## What high performance on any single benchmark would NOT prove

Suppose, after a build, TRINETRA posts a strong number on one benchmark — say high ROC-AUC on a landslide
susceptibility set, or EFA-YOLO-class mAP on a public fire-image test. That result, **on its own, would prove
almost nothing that matters for this system.** It would not prove the skill survives honest tile-withheld
spatial-CV with a buffer ≥ the terrain correlation range (random-split skill is known to collapse by
≈0.15–0.35 AUC on our hazards, 2608.12422); it would not prove the estimate is stable, because with n ≈ 5 geo
events the confidence interval swallows the mean; it would not prove calibration, because a calibrated model on
one split is routinely miscalibrated under the distribution shift and sensor-dropout the field guarantees
(2610.08810, 2604.22787); it would not prove the conformal coverage holds at the one moment it must — the
abrupt onset of a rare hazard, where even asymptotically-valid conformal shows local miscoverage; it would not
prove the edge-deployed INT8 model keeps its smoke recall, nor that latency, current, RAM, and radio range
meet budget on real hardware (all unmeasured); it would not prove the node is affordable (≤₹2000 unenforced),
legal (LoRa band unverified), or that an authority may even originate the resulting alert (unverified); it
would not prove the RL policy beats a MILP/stochastic-program baseline, or is even evaluable under OPE
positivity; and it would say nothing about the system's behaviour when a sensor is lost precisely because the
event destroyed it (worst-case, not random, missingness). A single benchmark win measures one model on one
distribution under one evaluation choice. TRINETRA's claim is a *life-safety, cross-site, offline-first,
calibrated, shielded, human-in-the-loop advisory* — and that claim is only earned by passing the full gate
stack G1–G7 (physics golden-cases, the spatial-CV admission gate with baselines + CIs + cost-loss, the
decision-function + measured conformal coverage, fusion stability, supplier-verified BOM + LoRa band,
anti-leak + no-egress audit, and dataset-license + Kaggle-fit), with every number stated as "beats GB +
decision-tree + persistence under tile-withheld spatial-CV with case-control matching and fixed seeds, with
honest coverage" — never as a bare benchmark score. Until then, the only measured facts TRINETRA owns are:
**128 numpy unit tests pass and 6 CI gates pass.** Everything else is a plan, a hypothesis, or someone else's
result.

# 23 — Future Work & Roadmap

> **Read `_CANON.md §0` first.** This chapter is a **plan**. Per `FINAL_REPORT.md`:
> *"Nothing was built, trained, or measured."* No TRINETRA model has been trained and no dataset has
> been downloaded (`_CANON §0`). Therefore **every roadmap item below is future work** — nothing on
> this page is a result, a measurement, or a commitment that has been met. Items are tagged
> `[CONFIRMED]` / `[LIKELY]` / `[HYPOTHESIS]` / `[INFEASIBLE]` per `_CANON §1`. Where a number comes from
> a paper it is **SOURCE-REPORTED** (that paper's data, not ours, Rule 16). arXiv IDs are cited **only
> where the source artifact gives them**, and most are **subagent-reported, NOT independently re-fetched**
> (`_CANON §7`) — re-resolving them is itself a build gap (§4.5 below).

The two code-status facts that ARE real anchor the whole roadmap and must not be confused with roadmap
"results": `python run_tests.py` → **128 tests, OK**; `python scripts/ci_gates.py` → **ALL 6 CI GATES
PASSED** (numpy core; `_CANON §2`). The PyTorch `deep/` layer and Kaggle scripts are **compile-verified
only, never GPU-trained here** (`_CANON §2`). Everything in this chapter builds forward from that state.

Sources for this chapter: `FINAL_REPORT.md §14` (build order) and `§15` (open backlog / next steps);

## 23.1 The build order (the ~8-step sequence)

Verbatim source: `FINAL_REPORT.md §14` ("Recommended build order"), cross-referenced to the gates in
`TRINETRA_Workstreams.md` (G1–G7, §"Cross-workstream quality gates") and the preliminary order in
`HANDOFF/BUILD_HANDOFF.md`. Each step lists its **precondition**, the **gate that admits it**, and its
**honest dependency**. Nothing in this sequence has been started; the whole sequence is `planned`.

Every step is additionally gated by its **pre-registered cross-camera/cross-site decision rule**
(`FINAL_REPORT §9`, `FEATURES.md §P17 admission rules`): keep a feature only if its improvement exceeds
seed/trial variance on a **held-out cross-camera/cross-site split**, confirmed by the inferential-
reproducibility test (F-17; 2302.04054 LMEM, source-reported). *A benchmark-local win that hurts
cross-camera is NOT a win.*

### Step 1 — Eval tooling + "real-win" gate + leakage-controlled benchmark
- **Build:** F-17 experiment tooling (provenance dagger 2006.07484 + inferential-reproducibility LMEM+GLRT
  2302.04054, both source-reported) and the data/benchmark curation that produces **C-05**, the
  leakage-controlled CCTV zero-shot benchmark (`FINAL_REPORT §13`), with datasheets.
- **Precondition:** none — this is first. `HANDOFF/BUILD_HANDOFF.md` makes the same call: the
  spatial-CV harness + baselines (persistence, gradient-boosted, 3-rule tree) **must exist before any
  model is trusted**.
- **Admitting gate:** **G2** (spatial-CV admission gate — the project-wide ADMISSION GATE that *blocks
  publication / any performance claim*) and **G7** (datacube/dataset/novelty/Kaggle). The benchmark must
  carry both random-CV and spatial-CV columns keyed to the spatial-CV result, with baselines in the same
  table (`TRINETRA_Workstreams.md` G2).
- **Honest dependency:** **datasets must be collected and licenses verified first** — all datasets are
  STATUS=candidate `[D]`, licenses INDICATIVE/UNVERIFIED, none selected (`FINAL_REPORT §5`,
  `_CANON §7` via `§9` map). Portal + license verification is an OPEN backlog item (`FINAL_REPORT §15.2`).
  This is a **~days-to-weeks** data-access + license task, not an afternoon. `[HYPOTHESIS]` that C-05 as
  specified is realizable until the data is in hand.

### Step 2 — Edge CCTV detector + physics feature
- **Build:** F-11 EFA-YOLO efficient edge detector (2409.12635 reports 1.4M params / 22.19 ms CPU,
  source-reported) + F-16 unsupervised IR optical-flow / flicker **physics feature** (1909.12937 reports
  95.39% frame-level, no labels, source-reported).
- **Precondition:** Step 1 — the tooling + benchmark + baselines exist, so a cross-camera "real win" is
  measurable.
- **Admitting gate:** **G2** real-win rule (F-11: keep only if cross-**camera** mAP gain > seed variance
  vs the current backbone; F-16: keep only if it adds signal over RGB-only on cross-site video). F-16 as a
  *physics* feature also lives under the WS1a Class-A/B/C discipline whose correctness gate is **G1**
  (physics golden tests), with Class-C novel flicker/ND terms **default-OFF with an A/B fallback**
  (`_CANON §4`, R20).
- **Honest dependency:** cross-camera data from Step 1; GPU time within the Kaggle budget
  (single-GPU retrain, `FEATURES.md` F-11). `[LIKELY]` (per `FINAL_REPORT §4`) that a compact edge
  detector cuts false alarms at acceptable latency — **not yet validated by us**. **Known risk
  (pre-registered):** micro-architecture mAP gains "often shrink cross-camera (single-split overfit)".

### Step 3 — Temporal event validation
- **Build:** F-12 temporal multi-frame event validation (confidence-weighted voting + cascade filter;
  2607.03131 reports FA 52%→4%, <100 ms/frame, source-reported).
- **Precondition:** Step 2 — a detector exists to post-process.
- **Admitting gate:** **G2** cross-site rule: keep only if the false-alarm reduction holds **cross-site at
  matched sensitivity** and **does not raise the missed-event rate** (`FEATURES.md` F-12; SOTA-targets
  table `FINAL_REPORT §11`).
- **Honest dependency:** a framerate/latency-to-alert tradeoff must be measured (the confirmation window
  adds latency — `DEPLOYMENT/pilot_design.md §2` counts "the F-12 confirmation-window cost"). `[LIKELY]`.

### Step 4 — Calibrated fusion + conformal-under-shift + drift monitor
- **Build:** P14 calibrated meta-fusion (GMF: stacking + bounded residual + conformal, re-calibrated per
  availability) + F-13 WCPS conformal-under-shift (2404.15018 WCPS; split-CP collapses 90%→65.3%,
  source-reported) + F-14 label-free drift/calibration monitor (2103.00903 STUDD; 2510.25573
  CUSUM-calibration).
- **Precondition:** Steps 1–3 give calibrated member models whose outputs can be fused and monitored.
- **Admitting gate:** **G3** (single `decide()` function; realizable+total shield; measured conformal
  coverage near nominal on a drifting holdout; anomaly radius bounded away from zero) **and G4** (meta-head
  coefficients stable under resampling; degraded-modality down-weighting; GMF never lowers the shield
  floor). The canonical decision rule is `level = max(conformal_level(risk, p*), shield_floor)`,
  **p\* = C_FA/(C_FA+C_miss) ≈ 0.0476** (`_CANON §4`).
- **Honest dependency:** `[CONFIRMED by sources]` that calibrated members ≠ calibrated ensemble
  (2101.05397) and vanilla split-CP collapses under moderate shift (2604.22787) — so the fused output
  must be **re-calibrated per availability** (`FINAL_REPORT §1 WS1b`). **Do NOT claim 1−α coverage
  cross-site without reweighting** (`FEATURES.md` F-13 risk; conformal-under-drift is a known-hard problem,
  §5.3 below). `[HYPOTHESIS]` that the specific GMF composition wins cross-site.

### Step 5 — IoT node + drift correction + prototype
- **Build:** F-15 IoT GP drift correction + uncertainty-driven recalibration scheduling (2506.09186 reports
  MSE −up to 90%, source-reported; 1707.03682 PRNet blind calib) on the P6/P13 physical prototype
  (Node A "Slope Sentinel" ≈ ₹1,930 [EST]; Node B "River Eye" ≈ ₹1,980 [EST]; `_CANON §8`,
  `TRINETRA_Workstreams.md` WS5).
- **Precondition:** the two nodes are re-spec'd (compliant SX1262 radio, tiered edge/cloud compute) per
  WS5; prices are live-verified.
- **Admitting gate:** **G5** (both node totals ≤ ₹2,000 **after price-verification**; every model assigned
  to a hardware-feasible tier with a stated compute/energy budget; a single faulty node cannot trigger RED
  unaided; LoRa band = **865–867 MHz** / IN865–867, SX1262).
- **Honest dependency:** **the ≤₹2000 BOM is NOT yet enforceable** — all ₹ figures are `[EST]`, suppliers
  returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch, so no price was independently confirmed; the price-verification
  gate (re-check each line item against ≥2 live Indian suppliers) is a mandatory deliverable *before any
  order* (`_CANON §8`, `TRINETRA_Workstreams.md` price-verification gate, `FINAL_REPORT §8`). On-device
  latency/RAM/current + radio range + final price are OPEN and require **physical measurement**
  (`FINAL_REPORT §8`, `§15.5`). F-15 risk: blind/neighbour calibration fails on sparse/isolated nodes.
  `[LIKELY]` for GP drift correction (source-reported).

### Step 6 — Robustness red-team
- **Build:** P16 robustness program — cross-sensor corroboration (the most transferable defense),
  uncertainty-entropy as an alert gate (confident-while-wrong 2610.08810), honest worst-case reporting;
  plus the WS6 integrity fixes (remove the key-exfiltrating proxy `#12`; CAP/SACHET signing; EO
  future-information-leak audit `#7`).
- **Precondition:** Steps 1–5 give the models, fusion and nodes that are the red-team's targets.
- **Admitting gate:** **G6** (no credential leaves the official endpoint; alert path works offline;
  feature-timestamp audit passes) — this gate *blocks the field pilot*. Robustness evidence also feeds the
  pilot's "evidence required before any automated public alert" bar (`DEPLOYMENT/pilot_design.md §6`).
- **Honest dependency:** `[CONFIRMED by sources]` that single-model hardening is benchmark-local while
  cross-sensor corroboration transfers (`FINAL_REPORT §1 WS6`, `§7`); certified robustness is a small-scale
  lower bound (1910.14655). Red-teaming is **continuous** because defenses and evasions co-evolve
  (2003.01279, deepfake context). `[LIKELY]` that corroboration bounds a single bad/attacked source.

### Step 7 — Anomaly + advisory RL (after the evac env is built)
- **Build:** WS8 anomaly heads (forecast-residual + Deep-SVDD, collapse-prevented) under the **STRICT
  protocol** (`FINAL_REPORT §3`: must beat persistence/general baseline; leakage control; report under
  shift; advisory input to fusion, never a standalone alert) + WS5 **advisory** offline-RL alarm policy
  (ranked options to a human dispatcher, never actuation; must BEAT strong non-RL baselines, e.g. MILP
  2602.14676).
- **Precondition:** **the disaster-evacuation RL environment must be built first** — there is **no
  off-the-shelf disaster-evac env** (`FINAL_REPORT §1 WS5`, `§15.8`; a declared BUILD GAP, §4.2 below).
- **Admitting gate:** **G2** (strict anomaly/RL valuation — honest OPE: select by BVFT 2110.14000,
  risk-evaluate by SCOPE-RL CVaR@5% 2311.18206, deploy only if the OPE lower bound ≥ rule baseline;
  `TRINETRA_Workstreams.md` WS2 task 4) and the RL safety shield from **G3**.
- **Honest dependency:** `[CONFIRMED by sources]` that naive RL underperforms and RL beats baselines only
  sometimes (2509.19972) → RL must beat MILP/non-RL and stay advisory. The evac env, OPE harness, and ≥100
  seeds (RB-13 policy) are prerequisites. `[HYPOTHESIS]` for every RL/anomaly skill claim until the env is
  built and the OPE gate passes.

### Step 8 — India shadow → advisory pilot
- **Build:** the staged pilot in `DEPLOYMENT/pilot_design.md`: STAGE 0 offline replay → STAGE 1 **SHADOW**
  (observe + log, trigger nothing) → STAGE 2 **ADVISORY** (human decides). STAGE 3 (beyond advisory) is
  explicitly **out of scope** of this program.
- **Precondition:** all prior steps + their gates; independent **ethics-review approval** before Stage 1
  (`DEPLOYMENT/pilot_design.md §4`).
- **Admitting gate:** the whole gate stack G1–G7, plus pre-registered pilot metrics (false-alarms/day,
  time-to-detection, missed-event rate + its uncertainty, calibration/PICP, operator accuracy) with
  stopping/rollback rules (`FINAL_REPORT §12`, `DEPLOYMENT/pilot_design.md §2–3`).
- **Honest dependency:** India regulatory / LoRa-band legality / who-may-originate-official-alerts items
  are **all `[UNVERIFIED]` search leads** requiring official-source + qualified-professional verification
  (`DEPLOYMENT/standards_and_regulation.md`, §4.4 below). **`[INFEASIBLE]` now:** autonomous public
  alerting without certification/authority (`_CANON §6`). The pilot's own honesty note:
  *"this bar is NOT met by any research-phase output"* (`DEPLOYMENT/pilot_design.md §6`).

These are the OPEN items from `FINAL_REPORT §15` and `TRINETRA_Workstreams.md` gates. Until they close, the

### 4.1 Datasets collected + licenses verified
All discovered datasets are STATUS=candidate `[D]` (D-numbered through D112), license INDICATIVE/UNVERIFIED;
**no dataset with STATUS=selected is paid, because none is selected** (`FINAL_REPORT §5`). Portal access +

candidate registry entries (GLOFNet 2510.10546; HMAGLOFDB 589 outbursts via 2608.12422; Sentinel-1/-2, GPM
IMERG, SMAP, ERA5-Land free-but-confirm; Bhuvan/NRSC landslide inventory — *verify license*)
(`TRINETRA_Workstreams.md` WS7 task 2). **Honest timeline:** data access + license clearance is a
days-to-weeks dependency and is the precondition for Step 1 / Phase P-0. `[HYPOTHESIS]` that C-05 is
buildable as specified until data is in hand.

### 4.2 Disaster-evacuation RL environment (no off-the-shelf env)
`FINAL_REPORT §1 WS5` and `§15.8`: **"Build the disaster-evacuation RL environment (no off-the-shelf env
exists — BUILD GAP)."** This blocks Step 7 (anomaly + advisory RL) entirely. The env must support the honest
OPE protocol (BVFT selection, SCOPE-RL CVaR@5% risk, one-step offline baseline, feedback-aware OPE 2312.01530)
and the RB-13 rigor policy (≥100 seeds, report tail + dispersion, beat trivial baselines). `[HYPOTHESIS]` on
any RL skill until the env exists and the OPE lower bound ≥ rule baseline.

### 4.3 Live-verified ≤₹2000 BOM
Every ₹ figure is `[EST]`; Robu.in / Amazon.in returned **HTTP 403** to automated fetch, so no price was
independently confirmed (`TRINETRA_Workstreams.md` price-verification gate; `_CANON §8`). The ≤₹2000 gate
(**C2**) is **NOT yet enforceable**. Procurement rule: no node is ordered until each line item is re-checked
against **≥2 live Indian suppliers** and the per-node total is re-confirmed ≤ ₹2,000 (Node A ≈ ₹1,930 [EST];
Node B ≈ ₹1,980 [EST]). On-device latency / RAM / current / radio-range and the final price need **physical
measurement** (`FINAL_REPORT §8`, `§15.5`). Blocks Step 5 / G5.

### 4.4 India regulatory / LoRa-band / alerting-authority verification
All items are `[UNVERIFIED]` search leads for official-source verification + qualified legal/standards review
— **not legal advice** (`DEPLOYMENT/standards_and_regulation.md`; `FINAL_REPORT §12`). Specifically: fire-
device certification; **radio/LoRa-band legality** (planned IN865–867 MHz / SX1262, `_CANON §8` — confirm it
is legal and within power/duty-cycle limits); **who may originate official alerts** (a private/academic party
*likely MAY NOT* originate official alerts); data-protection in video; surveillance/CCTV rules; social-media
ToS; electronics certification. Blocks the pilot (Step 8) and any alerting integration. **`[INFEASIBLE]`
now:** autonomous public alerting without certification/authority (`_CANON §6`). **`[INFEASIBLE]`:**
IP-address-based alerting for life-safety targeting — not carried (`_CANON §6`, `FINAL_REPORT §4`).

### 4.5 Independent re-resolution of subagent-reported arXiv IDs
The ledger holds **631 unique arXiv IDs** (FINAL_REPORT snapshot; the live ledger has grown to ~**775** — see `_CANON §7`), but *most are subagent-reported and NOT independently re-fetched*
(web_search had no API key; arXiv re-resolution only via throttled web_fetch) — a **disclosed residual risk**
(`FINAL_REPORT §5`, `§15.9`, `_CANON §7`). Before any paper's reported number is used to justify a build
hyperparameter or claim, its ID and figure must be independently re-resolved against arXiv. Full-text reads
are still needed for exact Wave-1 hyperparameters (2503.07371, 2607.03131, 2610.09208, 2406.17813,
2406.17488 — `FINAL_REPORT §15.7`). This gap touches **every** source-reported number in this chapter.

## 23.5 Research directions (literature-backed, [HYPOTHESIS])

These are open research threads the sources name but the program did not pursue to depth. All `[HYPOTHESIS]`.

### 5.1 SAR foundation-model trade study (P7 parked items)
`HANDOFF/BUILD_HANDOFF.md` (P3) records the **SAR-first encoder stance (CR-01)**: SAR beats optical in two
independent all-weather votes (SAR2Agri 2608.11142 +15.3 pt; GLOF SAR seg 2512.24117 IoU 0.9130,
source-reported). The P7 trade study must evaluate named SAR-specific contenders **on OUR task** — TerraMind,
Copernicus-FM, SAR-JEPA, SARMAE, SAR-W-MixMAE, SAMBA (Mamba, linear-cost → edge budget), OceanSAR — selected
by on-our-task probing + CKA shift budget, **not leaderboard**. Carried as an open item (`§P3`:
"SAR-FM trade (P7)"). `[HYPOTHESIS]` that a SAR encoder beats the frozen Prithvi-EO-2.0 (2412.02732) /
Galileo (2502.09356) baseline under our spatial-CV protocol.

### 5.2 Zero-shot complement maturation (P14Z)
Zero-shot / open-vocab detection is admitted **only** as a calibrated LOW-WEIGHT complement into GMF +
conformal + shield, never an autonomous trigger (D-011; `FINAL_REPORT §1 WS4`; `BUILD_HANDOFF §P3`:
P14Z registered). Sources favour trained over zero-shot in the fire domain (2504.13231, 2610.10946,
2607.07951). Research direction: mature the low-weight ZS complement and the leakage-controlled CCTV
zero-shot benchmark **C-05** (contribution C-05, `FINAL_REPORT §13`). `[HYPOTHESIS]`.

### 5.3 Better conformal-under-drift
`[CONFIRMED by sources]` that vanilla split-CP collapses under moderate shift (2604.22787; 90%→65.3%),
is valid only with reweighting (2404.15018 WCPS), and concept drift voids covariate-shift bounds
(`FINAL_REPORT §7`). Open thread: adaptive conformal (2202.07282 ACI/AgACI, 2303.12783 HopCPT, 2406.05405
missingness; `TRINETRA_Workstreams.md` WS3 task 4) with measured marginal **and per-zone** coverage, claiming
*risk-control* not a fixed 90%. `[HYPOTHESIS]` that any method restores near-nominal coverage on our
drifting Himalayan holdout.

### 5.4 Feedback-aware OPE
`TRINETRA_Workstreams.md` WS2 task 5 (#23) + `FINAL_REPORT §4` LIKELY cluster: model evacuation/alarm/
maintenance feedback in off-policy evaluation (2312.01530) so the RL alarm policy is valued under the
feedback its own alerts induce. Prerequisite: the evac env (§4.2). `[HYPOTHESIS]`.

### 5.5 Cross-sensor corroboration expansion
`[CONFIRMED by sources]` that cross-sensor corroboration is the most transferable robustness defense and
bounds a single bad/attacked source (`FINAL_REPORT §1 WS6`, `§4` LIKELY). Research direction: expand
corroboration across modalities with per-modality reliability gating (2603.01511 MERA, `Workstreams` WS4
task 2) and Neyman-Pearson fault-vs-event + cross-node spatial consistency before a single node drives a
shield override (`Workstreams` WS5 task 3; 1203.0541). `[HYPOTHESIS]` on the quantitative bound.
